English translation:
Harmiysis [...] from Aphrodisium [of the Small Oasis], to Diogenes son of Sarapion [...], former agoranomus, [gymnasiarch] in office of the city of the Oxyrhynchites, temple-warden of Tyche, [greetings]. I acknowledge that I have received [from you two hundred and sixty] drachmas of silver as principal, to which [nothing has been added], at interest of one drachma per mina each month from the [present month] Pharmuthi. I shall repay [the principal] together with the interest [on the thirtieth] of Phamenoth of the coming tenth year of [Aureli]us Antoninus Caesar the lord without delay; otherwise I shall pay you with the addition of one half, together with interest for the overdue time at the same rate of one drachma per mina per month, you having the right of execution upon me and upon all my property. The aforesaid two hundred and sixty drachmas I have laid out on the purchase of hay, which is to be stored in the camel-shed of Similis at Oxyrhynchus which I hold on lease; and I shall not be permitted to remove this hay, nor to sell it, nor to mortgage it, until I repay you the principal and the interest, because it is pledged to you. If any risk befalls the said hay, no loss shall result to you, because the money together with the interest is free from every risk. The note of hand, written in duplicate, is valid wherever it is produced.

Year 9 of the Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Augustus Armeniacus Medicus Parthicus Maximus, [Pharmuthi ..].

We, Hermogenes son of Hermogenes and Hermias the younger son of Zenodorus, have borrowed the one hundred and eight silver drachmas of capital and shall repay, as sureties for each other, as aforesaid. We, Hermias the younger son of Zenodorus and Hermogenes the younger, have borrowed the one hundred and eight silver drachmas of capital and shall repay, as sureties for each other, as aforesaid, without any prejudice to you regarding the other debts which I owe you under another security. Heracles and Ptollas, both sons of Ptolemaeus, of those from the city of the Oxyrhynchi, Persians of the epigone, to Diogas son of Heracles, greetings. We have received from you from hand to hand out of (your) house twelve drachmas of silver of Imperial coinage as capital, and in place of the interest on these we have ceded (to you) the use of the weaver's loom which we have, of three cubits less two palms, with its two antia, two histopodes and one epimitron, for six months from the present day, after which we will repay you the twelve drachmas of silver without delay. If we do not repay as written, we will pay you these with half as much again and interest. Upon the repayment of the money you will hand the loom back to us in sound condition, apart from wear, we being mutual sureties for payment, and you having the right of execution upon us and upon whichever of us you choose and upon all our property. The note of hand is valid wherever produced. Year 2 of Imperator Caesar Domitianus Augustus, month Neos Sebastos 19.

(2nd hand) I, Heracles son of Ptolemaeus, have received together with my brother, in return for the use of the loom, the twelve drachmas of silver of capital, and we will repay [...] as aforesaid. Year 2 of Imperator Caesar [Domitianus] Augustus, [month Neos] Sebastos [19].

[Fragment A] Copy. The seventh year of the Emperor Caesar Titus Aelius Hadrianus Antoninus Augustus Pius, in the month Hadrianus, at Oxyrhynchus in the Thebaid. Sarapion son of Herodes son of Exacon, of Oxyrhynchus, his mother being Caecilia Polla, has lent to Thatres and Teteorion, both daughters of Apollonius son of [...], and to their mother Demas daughter of Apollonius son of Panechotes, her mother being Philotera, all three Persian women from the village of Pela, each with a guardian - Thatres with her husband Peteuris son of Ammonas son of Sagathes, his mother being Panechotis, of Oxyrhynchus; Teteorion with her maternal uncle Panechotes son of Apollonius, his mother being Philotera, of the aforesaid Pela; Demas with her paternal uncle Hatres son of Panechotes son of Apollonius, of the same Pela - in the street, one thousand drachmas of silver of imperial coinage as principal, to which nothing has been added, at interest of three obols per mina each month from the present month Hadrianus. The borrowers shall pay the lender the interest at the close of each twelve-month period, the lender being believed concerning whatever payments the borrowers do not produce his written receipts for, and the principal on the thirtieth of the month Caesareus of the ninth year of Antoninus Caesar the lord, together with the interest of the remaining nine months, without delay. Otherwise, Thatres and Teteorion agree that the lender and his assigns shall have, in place of the principal and of whatever interest he does not receive, from the time of repayment, the possession and ownership for all time of what belongs to them in equal shares near the same Pela, in the cavalry holding of Diocles and Ptolemaeus, Persian, of the third part formerly a vineyard, now dry vine-land, from the most northerly part of the same third part: one and a half, a quarter and a sixty-fourth aroura (1 49/64 arouras), with everything in it; its neighbours: to the south, [the land] of Stephanus [...] and the aforesaid Thatres [daughter of Apollonius]; to the north, [...]; to the east, a canal [...] of the same and [of Stephanus]; to the west, [...] brother [...] [...]

Thonis son of Psenephthas grandson of Psenephthas, mother ......, from the city of Oxyrhynchus, fire-kindler (pyraithes) of Athena Thoeris, the most great goddess, Persian of the epigone, to my nephew Thonis son of Hephaestas grandson of Psenephthas, mother Taseus, from the same city, fire-kindler of the same goddess, greeting. English translation:
The Aurelii Pekysis son of Pausiris, his mother being Soeris, and his son Petenuphis, his mother being Sintheus, both from the city of Oxyrhynchus, to Aurelius Theon son of Didymus, from the same city, greeting. We both acknowledge, equally, that we have received and had measured out to us by you, of the produce of the past 4th year, four artabas of wheat at interest of one half, so that the total of wheat with the interest is six artabas, which I (sic) will repay to you on mutual security in the month of Payni at the threshing floor of the village of Teruthis, in wheat new, clean, unadulterated, free of earth, free of barley, sifted, measured as for the public granary, by your receiving measure by which we also received, the measuring being done by your agents. If I do not repay, as we have written, the aforesaid six artabas of wheat with the interest, I will pay them to you with the addition of one half, and interest for the overdue time likewise at one half, (you having the right of execution) upon us, as mutual sureties for the payment, or upon whichever of us you choose, and upon all our property of every kind, as if by legal decision. The document, written in duplicate, is valid as if deposited in a public archive, and concerning these things being rightly and duly done, having been asked by you, we have agreed. Year 5 of Imperator Caesar Marcus Aurelius Severus Alexander Pius Felix Augustus, Hathyr 8.

To Protarchus from ... Theon son of A[.]sa[... and] from Aristonicus son of Aisa[..., Persian] of the epigone. Concerning the points at issue, Aristonicus agrees that he has borrowed from Theon in cash out of the house 100 drachmas of Ptolemaic silver; and in lieu of the interest on it and of the three drachmas and three obols which Theon will pay him in advance each month, Aristonicus shall necessarily permit Theon and [his agents] for a period of twelve months from Phamenoth of the present 17th [year of Caesar] to dwell in the room belonging to him and to his sister [Philo]tera in a tenement house in the Delta (quarter), which is enclosed all round, using also the vestibule belonging to it and the conveniences of the tenement house in common, all the repairs of both the room and the vestibule, as often as needed, being the responsibility of Aristonicus, who shall not evict Theon or his agents within the period; and when this has elapsed he will repay the 100 drachmas of silver without interest, without any delay; or else, in whatever respect he transgresses, he shall immediately be liable to seizure and be held under arrest until he has paid the loan plus half as much again, and for the time exceeding (the term) the two-drachma interest according to the ordinance, the right of execution belonging to Theon both from Aristonicus himself and from all his property, as if by a legal judgment, all safeguards that he may adduce and every protection being invalid. Theon shall have the occupancy of both the room and the vestibule, and further also of the storeroom in them; and Theon shall pay in addition to Aristonicus the three drachmas and three obols monthly for the twelve months, and having dwelt (there) for these, upon recovering the 100 drachmas of silver without interest, he shall make a release of this agreement and vacate the dwellings and hand them over clean of dung, with the fixtures, such as he received them, or else he himself shall be liable to the fixed penalty.

This loan, the six artabas of barley, the borrower shall repay to Heracles or his representatives in the month Pauni of the present thirty-third year of Caesar, repaying new, clean barley by the sample of Hermophantus, by the merchants' fourth-measure of Heracles, with measuring and a fair leveller, delivered to the granary of [..]rus in the village, he himself paying the granary rent. Year 2 of Tiberius Caesar Augustus, month Neos Sebastos 28.

In the second year of Tiberius Caesar Augustus, on the twenty-eighth of the month Neos Sebastos, in Tebtynis of the Polemon division of the Arsinoite nome. Acusilaus son of Cleanor, aged about thirty-five, with a scar on the right hand, lent to Paopis, aged about thirty-eight, with a distinguishing mark on the right eye and a scar by the right cheek, and to Orseus, aged about thirty-five, with a scar on the left eyebrow, both sons of Phomnasis, Persians of the epigone, and to their wives, (the wife) of Paopis, Thaubastis daughter of Peeus, aged about thirty-two, with a scar on the upper lip on the left, and (the wife) of Orseus, Tamystas daughter of Peeus, aged about thirty-seven, squinting and with a scar on the right forearm, both Persian women, each with her aforementioned husband as guardian, the four being sureties for one another for payment, a capital of twenty-nine artabas of new, clean, unadulterated wheat, which they shall also repay in the month Pauni of the present second year of Tiberius Caesar Augustus, delivered to the village of Tebtynis, by the four-choenix measure of the granary of Livia Augusta, by which they also received them. If they do not repay as written within the fixed time, the borrowers shall pay Acusilaus immediately as the price of each artaba nine drachmas of silver or the highest price that obtains in the village, the right of execution for what is due under the contract lying with Acusilaus or his representatives [upon] the borrowers and upon whichever of them he chooses and upon all their property, as if by legal decision, apart from the other debts which Orseus owes [...] to Acusilaus under another security. English translation:
Heraclius, aged 35, mole on the middle of the nose.

In the third year of Tiberius Caesar Augustus, on the tenth of the month Xanthicus, Mecheir tenth, [in Oxyr]hyncha of the Polemon division of the Arsinoite nome. Heraclius son of [Hera]cles, aged about thirty-five, mole on the middle of the nose, lent to Dionysius son of Maron, [Persian] of the epigone, aged about forty-two, scar on the wrist of the right hand, and to his wife Thasos daughter of Psoiphis, Persian woman, aged about forty, scar on the right eyebrow, with her guardian, her aforementioned husband Dionysius, the two being sureties for one another for payment, four hundred and eighty drachmas of coined silver as capital, which they have also received from him immediately from hand to hand out of the house, at interest of one drachma three obols per mina for each month. This loan, the four hundred and eighty drachmas of coined silver, the borrowers shall repay to Heraclius in the month Tybi of the coming fourth year of Tiberius Caesar Augustus. If they do not repay, they shall pay the loan increased by one half and the interest simple, the right of execution lying with Heraclius upon the borrowers and upon all their property. And I, Heraclius son of Heracles, have lent the aforesaid four hundred and eighty drachmas of silver on all the terms written above.

I, Dionysius son of Maron, Persian of the epigone, and my wife Thasos daughter of Psoiphis, Persian woman, with me, her aforementioned husband Dionysius, as guardian, being sureties for one another for payment, have the loan from Heraclius son of Heracles, who manages the affairs of Heraclius son of Heracles son of Herodes, the four hundred and eighty drachmas of coined silver, at interest of one drachma three obols per mina for each month, which we will also repay in the month Tybi of the coming fourth year of Tiberius Caesar Augustus, as stated above. I, the aforementioned Dionysius, have also written for my wife Thasos, as she does not know letters, and I am registered as her guardian. I am aged about forty-two, scar on the wrist of the right hand.

In the third year of Tiberius Caesar Augustus, Mecheir tenth, through Hermias, nomographos of Oxyrhyncha of the Arsinoite (nome).

Verso: Loan of 480 drachmas of silver, of Heraclius to Dionysius and his wife.

Copy of a loan. In the nineteenth year of Tiberius Caesar Augustus, on the twenty-fifth of the month Apellaeus, Phaophi 25, at Socnopaei Nesus in the division of Heraclides of the Arsinoite nome. Tanephrummis daughter of Onnophris, aged about fifty, with a scar on the shin and on the right foot, with as guardian her son Onnophris son of Tesenouphis, aged about thirty, with a scar on the right eyebrow, has lent: Thaesis daughter of Panephrummis, aged about thirty, with a scar on the right foot, Persian, with as guardian her husband Harpagathes son of Tesenouphis, aged about thirty-five, with a scar below the right knee: "I have the one hundred drachmas of coined silver, as capital, at interest of one drachma per mina each month, which I shall repay in the month Sebastos of the coming tenth year of Tiberius Caesar Augustus. If I do not repay as apportioned, two hundred and fifty drachmas."

Subscriber for the lender: Stotoetis son of Panephrummis, aged about fifty-one, with a scar in the middle of the forehead; and for the borrower: Herieus son of Herieus, aged about twenty-five, without distinguishing mark.

Copy of the subscription: I, Thaesis daughter of Panephrummis, with as guardian my husband Harpagathes son of Tesenouphis, acknowledge that we have the loan from Tanephrummis daughter of Onnophris, with as guardian her son Onnophris son of Tesenouphis, the one hundred drachmas of coined silver, and I shall guarantee it with every guarantee as written above. English translation:
Chaeremon to Cronion, who manages the record office, greetings. A copy of the petition submitted to us is appended below. Please, therefore, follow up what is set out in it, as is proper. Farewell. In the twenty-third year of Tiberius Caesar Augustus, Choiak third.

To Chaeremon, exegetes, from Taorseus daughter of Eutychus, with as guardian her kinsman Ptolemaeus son of Chaeremon. My husband Galates son of Lysimachus has died, leaving three under-age sons by me, Lysas, Lysimachus and Eutychas, whose guardian I also had myself registered through you. Galates, together with his own brothers Didymus the elder, Didymus the younger and Lysimachus, owed to Castor and Lysimachus, both sons of Lysimachus, under a mortgage executed in year 1[.] of Tiberius Caesar Augustus on the paternal catoecic lands belonging to them, a catoecic allotment of eighty-two arouras in the division of Polemon, of which thirty-seven arouras in two parcels are near Tebtynis, twenty-five arouras in one parcel near Theogonis, formerly of Lucius Terentius, and the remaining twenty arouras in another parcel near Kerkesis, so that the aforesaid arouras of the allotment are eighty-two or however many they may be, the neighbours of each parcel and the other details being set out in the said mortgage, in respect of the two talents and one thousand two hundred drachmas of silver capital lent under it and the interest accrued from the said transaction up to now; and Castor and Lysimachus have taken possession of the said eighty-two arouras of the allotment, on the basis of the transfer of registration which they made in year 21 of Tiberius Caesar Augustus through the catoecic registry, and have ceded part to their own brothers. Hence we asked Castor and his brother Lysimachus to treat us kindly, on condition that we give them two thousand five hundred drachmas of silver in part payment of what Galates and his brothers owe, public, private and other debts, and that we all withdraw and consent to the transfer of registration made through the catoecic registry and to the cessions to the brothers of Castor and his associates. And I ask you to give instructions to write to the manager of the record office to draw up with me, as I submit in the names of my said under-age sons with myself as guardian, and with the brothers of Galates, Didymus the elder, Didymus the younger, Lysimachus and Haryotes, submitting jointly with me, the agreement of withdrawal and consent concerning the sixth share falling to my under-age sons, the guarantee resting on me together with the brothers of Galates under mutual surety, so that I with my children may be benefited.

It has been read. Year 23 of Tiberius Caesar Augustus, Choiak 3. Farewell.

I, Harmiysis son of Orseus, my mother being Tapeeis, acknowledge that I have sold to Onnophris son of Kollouthos, his mother being Terepsais, in accordance with this sale, from the present day for all time, the two parts out of three belonging to me of my paternal three-storeyed house, common and undivided, in Tebtynis; the neighbours of the whole house are: on the south, formerly of my brother Orseus, now of Castor son of Lysima[...]; on the north, the house of the sons of Au....rus; on the west, the courtyard of Harmiysis son of Lotis; on the east, the royal street. And I have received from Onnophris the agreed price, all of it, in full, at once from hand to hand out of the house, and I will guarantee (the sale) with every guarantee against public dues from former times up to the present year, and against private debts and every claim for all time, as aforesaid. I, Orseus son of Orseus, acknowledge that I have sold to Cronion son of Labesis, in accordance with this agreement, from the present day for all time, the fourth share, common and undivided, of the new three-storeyed house belonging to me and of all its appurtenances in Tebtynis; the neighbours of the whole house are: on the south, the house and courtyard of the sons of Panos and in part the house of Chratas son of Hippalus; on the north, the entrance and exit of the sons of Hatres and of the sons of Heraclitus son of Maron and of Orseus the elder, son of Paopis; on the west, the courtyard of our son Orseus and of Areius son of Patynis; on the east, the royal street. And I have received from Cronion the agreed price, all of it, in full, at once from hand to hand out of the house, and I will guarantee (the sale) with every guarantee against public dues from former times up to the month Pharmuthi and for the month Pharmuthi itself of the coming ninth year of Tiberius Claudius Caesar Augustus Germanicus Imperator, and against private debts and every claim for all time. My wife Taarmiysis daughter of Patynis consents [to this agreement and] will not proceed against it nor bring any claim, [nor will anyone else on her behalf, as aforesaid. Sarapion son of Pto]lemaeus [wrote for them] because [they do not know letters].

I, Orseus son of Orseus, Persian of the epigone, and my wife Taarmiysis daughter of Patynis, with me as her guardian, the two of us mutual sureties for payment, have received the loan from Cronion son of Labesis, one hundred and thirty-two drachmas of coined silver as capital, at interest of one drachma per mina per month each, which I will also repay in the month Pharmuthi of the coming ninth year of Tiberius Claudius Caesar Augustus Germanicus Imperator, as aforesaid. Sarapion son of Ptolemaeus wrote for them because he does not know letters.

Registered Mecheir 24: loan of Horion to Heraclides and his mother, 760 drachmas of silver.

In the twelfth year of Tiberius Claudius Caesar Augustus Germanicus Imperator, month Xandikos 24, Mecheir 24, at Tebtynis in the division of Polemon of the Arsinoite nome. Horion son of Cronion, about 30 years old, with a scar in the middle of the forehead, lent to Heraclides son of Ischyrion alias Nestnephis, Persian of the epigone, about 25 years old, with a scar on the first finger of the left hand, and to his mother Thaubarion daughter of Petemounis, Persian woman, about 50 years old, with a scar on the right thumb, with Heraclides himself as her guardian, the two mutual sureties for payment, seven hundred and sixty drachmas of coined silver as capital, which they have also received from him at once from hand to hand out of the house, at interest of one drachma per mina per month each; and this loan, the seven hundred and sixty drachmas of silver and the interest, let the borrowers repay to Horion in the month Tybi of the coming thirteenth year of Tiberius Claudius Caesar Augustus Germanicus Imperator; and if they do not repay as written, let the borrowers pay to Horion at once the loan plus half, and the interest simple, the right of execution belonging to Horion or his agents against the borrowers and against all their property, as if by legal judgment; Horion suffering no diminution of his rights in respect of what the debtors owe him under an agreement of mortgage (mesiteia) on the catoecic allotment of 3 3/4 arouras belonging to Heraclides near Theogonis, for 1,000 drachmas and the interest, which shall remain valid, and the borrowers shall not redeem the said mortgage unless they first repay the aforesaid capital and the interest. Signatory: Sarapion son of Ptolemaeus, about 40 years old, with a scar on the neck on the left side.

I, [Hera]clides son of Ischyrion alias Nestnephis, Persian of the epigone, and my mother Thaubarion daughter of Petemounis, Persian woman, [with] me as her guardian, the two of us mutual sureties for payment, have borrowed from Horion son of Cronion the seven hundred and sixty [drachmas] of silver as capital, at interest of one drachma per mina per month each, which we will also repay in the month Tybi of the coming thirteenth year of Tiberius Claudius Caesar Augustus Germanicus Imperator, Horion suffering no diminution of his rights in respect of what we owe him under an agreement of mortgage on the allotment of three and a half and a quarter arouras near Theogonis belonging to me, Heraclides, for one thousand drachmas of silver as capital and the interest, which we shall not redeem unless we first repay the aforesaid capital and the interest, as aforesaid. Sarapion son of Ptolemaeus wrote for them because they do not know letters.

I, Horion son of Cronion, have made the loan as aforesaid, my rights suffering no diminution in respect of what they owe me under a mortgage on three and a half and a quarter arouras for one thousand drachmas of silver and the interest, as aforesaid.

Tryphon son of Dionysius, Persian of the epigone, to Thoonis son of Thoonis, greetings. I acknowledge that I have received from you, through the bank of Ammonius and Epimachus at the Sarapeum near the city of Oxyrhynchus, one hundred and four drachmas of Augustan and Ptolemaic silver coinage, total 104 drachmas of Ptolemaic silver coinage, as capital, to which nothing at all has been added, which I will also repay to you on the thirtieth of Tybi of the present second year of Nero Claudius Caesar Augustus Germanicus Imperator, without any delay. And if I do not repay as written, I will pay you the whole aforesaid capital plus half, and the proper interest for the overdue time, the right of execution belonging to you against me and against all my property. Year six of Nero Claudius Caesar Augustus Germanicus Imperator, Pharmouthi 23, in the city of Oxyrhynchus of the Thebaid. Dioscus son of Pausiris and his wife Thermuthion daughter of Achilleus, with as her guardian Diogenes son of Pasion, husband of her mother Plutarche, all of the city of Oxyrhynchus, acknowledge in the street: Thermuthion, that she has given to her aforesaid husband Dioscus no more than two hundred drachmas of silver of the imperial and Ptolemaic coinage, as capital, out of the price of her paternal share of a house in the Hippodrome lane, which she sold to Didymus son of Didymus with the same Dioscus as guardian, because the rest of the price has been paid out by her to her mother Plutarche daughter of Harpaesis toward what was owed to her by Achilleus son of Pastous, father of the aforementioned Thermuthion and former, now deceased, husband of Plutarche, in accordance with the receipt issued to her; and Dioscus, that he has received forthwith from Thermuthion the aforesaid two hundred drachmas of silver and must repay them to her without interest within sixty days from the day on which they are demanded, or else she shall have the right of execution for them upon him and upon all his property, as if by a legal judgment. The contract is valid.

Year six of Nero Claudius Caesar Augustus Germanicus Imperator, Pharmouthi twenty-third. Registered through Andromachus, associate of Chaeremon and Sotades, agoranomoi.

And whereas there were owed to the same son of mine Eudaemon by the same debtor Didyme, by another loan contract through the same agoranomeion in the same fifth year, month Choiak, another nine hundred and fifty drachmas, for repayment in the month Kaisareios of the same fifth year, on the security of the aforesaid arouras; and by a diagraphe through the bank of Horion son of Syrus in the locality, in the name of the same Eudaemon, in the same fifth year, another four hundred and thirteen drachmas, for repayment in the month Kaisareios of the same fifth year, it having been added in writing to the diagraphe that Didyme may not release the mortgages unless she also repays what is due by the diagraphe; and since no repayment of any of the debts as aforesaid has been made up to now, neither to my son while he was alive nor to me after his death, I have of necessity come before your authority, and I ask you to order a letter to be written to the strategus of the Hermopolite (nome) to communicate to the debtor Didyme a copy of this memorandum, so that she may pay me all the aforesaid capital sums and the interest on the overdue (debts) up to now and the taxes and expenses, likewise with interest; or else she should know that, with regard to what is owed by the contracts, I will enter upon the arouras mortgaged as aforesaid and take possession of them as owner and carry off all their proceeds and moreover manage them as I choose, no claim whatever concerning them being left in future to her or to anyone else on her behalf, but that the guarantee also remains binding on her in accordance with the stipulations set out in the contracts; and that, with regard to what is owed by the diagraphe, I will exact payment from whatever other property of Didyme I find. Sixth year of Imperator Caesar Domitianus Augustus Germanicus, month Dystros twenty-sixth, Tybi twenty-sixth, at Bacchias of the Heraclides division of the Arsinoite nome. [...], Persian of the epigone, about fifty years old, scar in the middle of the forehead, acknowledges to Hermas son of Ptolemaeus, about fifty-two years old, scar in the middle of the forehead, that he has received from him forthwith from hand to hand out of the house sixty drachmas of coined silver; and that, in place of the interest on these, he, the acknowledging party, has agreed that Hermas and his representatives and whomever he wishes shall dwell for one year from the aforesaid date in the twenty-seventh share inherited from his father belonging to him, the acknowledging party, held in common and undivided with Hermas and others, of house plots and all their appurtenances in the aforesaid village; and that the acknowledging party and his representatives will guarantee to Hermas and his representatives the terms of this habitation with every guarantee, both for the period of it and for whatever period it may be necessary to dwell. In the tenth year of Imperator Caesar Domitianus Augustus Germanicus, month Artemisios 6, Phamenoth 6, at Soknopaiou Nesos in the Heraclides division of the Arsinoite nome. Panephremmis son of Panesneus, Persian of the epigone, aged about thirty-one, with a scar on the right forearm, acknowledges to Pekysis the younger, son of Pekysis, aged about forty, with a scar on the forehead on the right, that he, the acknowledging party, has received from him the price of seven and a half artabas of barley by the fourth measure, and two-fifths (of an artaba of wheat), and one hundred silver drachmas, which the acknowledging party shall also repay to Pekysis the younger in the month Payni of the present 10th year. (In the margin:) Original.

In the thirteenth year of Imperator Caesar Domitianus Augustus Germanicus, Tybi tenth, at Tebtunis in the Polemon division of the Arsinoite nome. Chaeremon, aged about twenty-five, with a scar on the left shin, and Cronion, aged about twenty-two, with a scar in the middle of the forehead, both sons of Acusilaus, Persians of the epigone, mutual sureties for payment, acknowledge to Lysimachus son of Didymus son of Lysimachus, aged about thirty-two, with a scar on the right [...], that they have received from him an interest-bearing loan of nine and [two-thirds] artabas of new, pure, unadulterated wheat by the four-choenix measure belonging to Lysimachus; and the acknowledging parties, Chaeremon and Cronion, are obliged to repay on mutual security to Lysimachus the nine [and two-thirds] artabas of wheat in the month Payni of the present thirteenth year of Imperator Caesar Domitianus Augustus Germanicus in the aforesaid village of Tebtunis, without any delay or evasion, Lysimachus having the right of execution upon the acknowledging parties and upon whichever of them he chooses and upon all their property, as if by a legal judgement. Subscriber for the acknowledging parties: Ischyrion son of Achilleus, aged 50, with a scar on the [chin on the left].

[We, Chaeremon and Cron]ion, sons of Acusilaus, [Persians of the epi]gone, mutual sureties [for payment, have received from] Lysimachus son of Didymus [an interest-bearing loan] of nine [and two-thirds] artabas of wheat [by the] four-choenix [measure] belonging to Lysimachus [and we shall repay in the] month Payni of the present [thirteenth] year. Choiak 11. Debt.

In the second year of Imperator Caesar Nerva Traianus Augustus Germanicus, Choiak 11, at Tebtunis in the Polemon division of the Arsinoite nome. Petesuchus son of Onnophris, of those from Talei, Persian of the epigone, aged about forty-five, with a scar on the little finger of the left hand, acknowledges to Zoilus son of Harmiusis, aged about forty-eight, with a scar on the right forearm, that he has received from him, Zoilus, from hand to hand out of the house a loan of one and one-sixth artabas of new, pure, unadulterated wheat and eight silver drachmas and one-third artaba of lentils, by the six-choenix measure of Talei; and the acknowledging party is obliged to repay to Zoilus all the aforesaid in the month Payni of the present second year, without any delay or evasion, Zoilus having the right of execution upon the acknowledging party and upon all his property. Subscriber: Lysimachus son of Cronion, aged about 58, with a scar on the little finger of the left hand.

I, Petesuchus son of Onnophris, of those from Talei, acknowledge that I have received from Zoilus son of Harmiusis a loan of one and one-sixth artabas of wheat by the six-choenix measure of Theogonis and eight silver drachmas and one-third artaba of lentils, which I shall also repay in the month Payni of the present second year, as stated above. Lysimachus son of Cronion wrote for him as he does not know letters. I, Zoilus son of Harmiusis: the agreement has been made with me as stated above.

English translation:
Epaphroditus, freedman of Aristocles son of Alexander, of those from the city of Oxyrhynchus, Persian of the epigone, to Theon son of Harpaesis son of Harpaesis, his mother being Tatreiphis daughter of Theon, of those from the same city, greetings. I acknowledge that I have received from you from hand to hand out of the house three hundred and fifty-six drachmas of silver of imperial coinage, total 356 silver drachmas, of capital, to which nothing at all has been added, at interest of one drachma per mina per month from the present month Neos Sebastos, which I shall pay you punctually each month. As security for these I mortgage to you the twenty-four artabas of Greek natron which I have, and another four talents by weight of natron, stored in a storeroom at the eastern gateway of the house of Taarpaesis in the South Quay quarter, of which in number ... prevented ... of which storeroom of Taarpaesis ..., the said storeroom having been sealed by me and by you. The capital I shall repay to you on the thirtieth of the month Germanikeios of the present second year of Imperator Caesar Nerva Traianus Augustus Germanicus, without any delay. If I do not repay as written, you shall be permitted to open the storeroom yourself and sell the natron at its current price and take the aforesaid capital, the trust lying with you ... the risk concerning the natron being with ...; the remainder I shall repay to you without delay or evasion, with an additional half, together with the interest for the overdue time, you having the right of execution upon me and upon all my property as if by a legal judgement, without prejudice to the exaction of whatever else I owe you under two other chirographs on the security of salt-land, nor of whatever else I owe you on pledges [...]. This hand is valid wherever produced and for anyone who produces it. Year 2 of Imperator Caesar Nerva Traianus Augustus Germanicus, month Neos Sebastos 2.

I, Epaphroditus, freedman of Aristocles, have from hand to hand the three hundred and fifty-six drachmas of silver on the mortgage of twenty-four artabas of Greek natron and four talents by weight, and I shall repay on the thirtieth of the month Germanikeios of the present [year 2]; I shall pay the monthly interest punctually, Theon suffering no prejudice in the exaction of the others which I owe him under two other chirographs on the mortgage of salt-land, nor of the others which I owe on pledges, as stated above. Year two of Imperator Caesar Nerva Traianus Augustus Germanicus, Hathyr 2.

Petesouchus, aged about forty years, with a scar on the left knee, and Peteeus, aged about twenty-five years, with a scar on the little finger of the left hand, both sons of Orsenouphis, of those from the village of Memphis in the same division, Persians of the epigone, mutual sureties for payment, acknowledge to Hermes alias Lysimachus son of Didymus, aged about forty years, with a scar on the right side of the forehead, that they have received from him, Hermes, from hand to hand out of the house, a loan of eighty-eight silver drachmas at interest, and that the acknowledging parties are obliged to repay to Hermes the eighty-eight silver drachmas of the loan and [their] interest in the month Pauni of the present second year of Imperator Caesar Nerva Traianus Augustus Germanicus without any delay, the right of execution belonging to Hermes both on the acknowledging parties, on each one of them and on whichever of them he chooses, and on all their property. Subscriber: Ischyrion son of Achilles, aged about 55, scar on the chin on the left. The agreement is valid.

(2nd hand) We, Petesouchus and Peteeus, the two sons of Orsenouphis, of those from the village of Memphis in the division of Polemon, Persians of the epigone, acknowledge that we have received from Hermes alias Lysimachus son of Didymus a loan of eighty-eight silver drachmas of principal at interest, which we will also repay in the month Pauni of the same second year of Traianus Augustus, as aforesaid. (3rd hand) I, Hermes son of Didymus: it has been done.

[Year thr]ee of Imperator Caesar Nerva Traianus Augustus Germanicus, Hathyr 29, at Thallou in the Patemites (toparchy) above Memphis of the Hermopolite (nome). Heracles the elder, son of Apollonius, his mother being [...], of those from Hermopolis, registered in the quarter Phrourion Apeliotes, aged about 67, of medium height, honey-coloured, long-faced, straight-nosed, with a scar on the middle of the forehead below the hair, lent to Demetria daughter of Epimachus alias Aphrodisius, her mother being Taos, aged about 55, of medium height, honey-coloured, long-faced, straight-nosed, with a scar on the right shin, [with her guardian], her son Minches son of Ouebis, aged about 24, of medium height, honey-coloured, long-faced, straight-nosed, with a scar above the right knee, they too being of those of the city registered in the quarter Outside the City West, of Augustan silver coinage, as principal one thousand three hundred [drachmas], which Demetria has taken up from Heracles through the private bank of Hermaeus son of Hephaestion in Thallou, at interest of one drachma on each mina every month for twenty-[four] months from Choiak of the present [3rd year], which interest drachmas, collected together, three hundred and twelve, make, interest and principal, one thousand six hundred and twelve drachmas, on mortgage of the six catoecic arouras belonging to Demetria near Thallou, [of the] kleros of [Glau]cias, full, sown, free from royal (land) and other categories. Let Demetria repay the one thousand six hundred and twelve silver drachmas to Heracles or his [representatives] [by] the 30th of Hathyr of the fifth year of Imperator Caesar Nerva Traianus Augustus Germanicus, in approved current silver, such as she has also received. If she does not repay, let it be permitted to Heracles or his [representatives] forthwith to have the aforesaid six arouras transferred to himself through the catoecic registry offices of the Hermopolite, and to possess them as owner and use and manage them in whatever way [he chooses], no claim being left afterwards to the debtor Demetria or to her representatives concerning anything pertaining to the mortgage, in any manner or under any pretext, but the guarantee [of the mortgage being incumbent upon] her at all times against every claim. The contract of loan is valid.

Payment through the private bank of Hermaeus son of Hephaestion in Thallou: Heraclides the elder, son of Apollonius, Hermopolite, registered in Phrourion Apeliotes, to Demetria daughter of Epimachus, her mother being Taos, of those from Thallou, with her guardian, her son Minches son of Ouebis, on mortgage of the six arouras of catoecic land belonging to her near Thallou of the kleros of Glaucias, which she will also repay by the 30th of Hathyr of the fifth year of Traianus Caesar the lord, in accordance with the contract of loan registered through the record office in Thallou, of silver principal one thousand three hundred drachmas, total 1,300 drachmas, at interest of one drachma on each mina every month.

I, Demetria daughter of Epimachus, my mother being Taos, of those from Thallou, have assented to the aforesaid payment and have taken up the one thousand three hundred silver drachmas at interest of one drachma on each mina every month for twenty-four months on mortgage of the six catoecic arouras belonging to me near Thallou of the kleros of Glaucias, and I will repay by the 30th of Hathyr of the fifth year of Traianus Caesar the lord, in accordance with the contract of loan registered through the record office in Thallou, as aforesaid. Year three of Imperator Caesar Nerva Traianus Augustus Germanicus, Choiak 1. I, Minches son of Ouebis, have signed as guardian of my mother and wrote on her behalf, as she does not know letters.

Year six of Imperator Caesar Nerva Trajan Augustus Germanicus Dacicus, month Xanthicus = Mecheir, at Hermopolis in the Thebaid. Areius son of Sarapion grandson of Hermaeus alias Areius, his mother being Tanemis, of Hermopolis, a minor registered in the quarter Phrourion East, aged about 6, honey-coloured, with as guardian his own father Sarapion son of Hermaeus alias Areius, aged about 46, of medium height, long-faced, straight-nosed, scar in the middle of the forehead, has lent further to Dioscorus alias Hermaeus son of Harpaesion grandson of Theon, his mother being Artemisia alias Taumesis daughter of Epimachus, of Hermopolis, registered in the quarter City West, Persian of the epigone, aged about 30, of medium height, honey-coloured, long-faced, straight-nosed, scar on the left shin, another five hundred drachmas of silver of imperial coinage, as capital, which he has received from him through the bank of Eudaemon, at interest of one drachma per mina per month from Phamenoth of the present year until the repayment set out below, five months, the interest amounting to twenty-five drachmas; all on the security which he previously mortgaged to him under other loan contracts through the agoranomeion in Hermopolis, one on the epagomenal days of the past fifth year of Imperator Caesar Nerva Trajan Augustus Germanicus Dacicus, the other in the month Tybi of the present year, for the debts owed under each of them, namely five and a half arouras of his maternal land, of the land around the court (peri aulen), in Upper Patemit near Mennis, from the allotment of Philon son of Onarasis, within their existing boundaries, and (now also for) this present loan, the five hundred and twenty-five drachmas of capital and interest together. Let Dioscorus repay to the lender or his successors on the thirtieth of Epeiph of the present sixth year in approved, current, acceptable silver. If he does not repay, as soon as the due date arrives, let the lender or his successors be permitted, without requiring renewal or a notice (diastolikon) or anything else at all, after paying the dues owed for the enkyklion tax, to make foreclosure (epikatabole) on the mortgaged five and a half [arouras], and let the lender and his successors possess them with full ownership in place of what is owed, and enter upon [them and take their produce and] lease them out [and carry off what] accrues [from them] annually [...] all, and use [and] manage them in whatever [way] they choose [for all time], no [claim] or pretext being left [hereafter to the borrower or] to others on his behalf [concerning these]. Let [the borrower] guarantee [this] mortgage [with every guarantee against] public and private [claims and against all] (claims) whatsoever, [and he shall not be permitted to sell it or to] mortgage [it to others ...] arouras [...]

And the acknowledging party and his heirs shall guarantee to Tapekysis and her heirs the terms of [this] habitation with [every] guarantee, and the acknowledging party shall ensure that no one hinders Tapekysis or her heirs [from living there] and from lodging others and collecting the rents and using all their appurtenances without hindrance. If Tapekysis is found to have spent money on repair of the dwelling, [and] Hermas, the acknowledging party, [wishes] to repay the aforesaid money, let him repay it together with the aforesaid money, [...] the credence resting with Tapekysis herself. (3rd hand) [I, Tapekysis] daughter of Horus, with my husband Horus as guardian: the agreement has been made with me as aforesaid. I, Ammonius son of Dioscorus, wrote for them since they do not know letters.

English translation:
In the reign of the King of Kings Arsaces, Benefactor, Just, Manifest and Friend of the Greeks, in the year 368 as the King of Kings reckons, but 432 by the former reckoning, on the twenty-sixth of the month Daisios, at Paliga, a village of the hyparchy around Iardas, before Metolbaissa son of Men[...] son of Menarnaeus, phrourarch and one of the first and most honoured Friends and of the bodyguards, and before the witnesses written below.

Phraates, eunuch, arkapates, one of the people of Manesus son of Phraates, of the batesa and of the free men, paraleptes and strategos of Mesopotamia and Parapotamia and Arabarch, lent to Barlaas son of Thathaeus, son of Ablaeus, of those [from] the village of [...] [...], four hundred drachmas of good silver of Tyrian coinage, on mortgage of all the property belonging to him [...], [which also] shall be with the owner. In place of the interest on this money, Barlaas, staying with [Phraates until the time of repayment], shall render him the services of a slave, doing everything that is ordered [him], not [being absent by day or by night without] the consent of Phraates. If he is absent by day or by night [from Phraates], he shall pay for each [day one drachma ...]. If he is ill for more than seven days, Barlaas shall pay [for each day on which] he is idle one drachma. If he takes refuge [in any temple], he shall be expelled from the temple, and Phraates shall use him [...]. Phraates, however, shall provide him with his daily food and clothing. In flight, death, damage and other risks the lender shall have no share.

The aforesaid money, and anything else that accrues from the idle days, Barlaas shall repay to Phraates in the month Daisios in the year 433 by the former reckoning. If he does not repay within the appointed time, Barlaas shall even so continue rendering to Phraates the same services on the aforesaid terms until the repayment of the money. If, however, after the time has passed, Phraates wishes to recover the money, and Barlaas, when asked, [fails] to repay the money, Phraates and anyone who presents this contract shall have the right of execution upon Barlaas and upon the property mortgaged to him and any other that he may acquire, exacting the whole with full authority, except [...] with the [...].

Barlaas undertook to renew this contract through the record office (chrematisterion) in Europos, when notified by Phraates, within five further days; if he does not renew it, he shall pay Phraates a penalty of four hundred drachmas of silver, and the same amount to the royal treasury, and this contract shall even so be valid.

In the seventh year of the Emperor Caesar Trajan Hadrian Augustus, on the twentieth of the month Sebastos, at Tebtynis of the division of Polemon of the Arsinoite nome. Heraclides alias Valerius, son of Heraclides, son of Maron, registered in the Tameia quarter, Persian of the epigone, about forty-six years old, with a scar on the left knee, acknowledges to Tamystha daughter of Didymus alias Mystharion, about thirty-five years old, without distinguishing mark, with her husband Lysimachus son of Apollonius as guardian, about thirty-eight years old, with a scar on the right foot, that he has received from her, Tamystha, forthwith, from hand to hand, out of the house, an interest-bearing loan of a capital sum of two hundred and twelve drachmas of coined silver; and the acknowledging party Heraclides alias Valerius is bound to repay to Tamystha the two hundred and twelve drachmas of silver, the capital of the loan, and the interest, on the twentieth of the month Tybi of the present seventh year, without any delay or evasion. If he does not repay as written, let Heraclides alias Valerius pay to Tamystha the aforesaid capital with half again, and the interest simple, Tamystha having the right of execution upon Heraclides alias Valerius and upon all his property.

(2nd hand) I, Heraclides alias Valerius, son of Heraclides, son of Maron, from Tameia, acknowledge that I have received from Tamystha daughter of Didymus alias Mystharion, from hand to hand, out of the house, an interest-bearing loan of a capital sum of two hundred and twelve drachmas of silver, which I shall also repay, as I am bound, on the twentieth of the month Tybi of the present seventh year without delay, she having the right of execution upon me and upon all my property, as aforesaid.

(3rd hand) Tamystha, with her husband Lysimachus as guardian: the agreement has been made with me as aforesaid.

Thonis son of Harthonis, son of Petosiris, his mother being Tausorapis, from the city of Oxyrhynchus, Persian of the epigone, to Dionysius son of Pasion, son of Pasion, from the same city, greeting. I acknowledge that I have received from you, from hand to hand, two thousand drachmas of silver, total 2,000 drachmas of silver of capital, to which nothing has been added, at interest of one drachma per mina for each month from the following month Hathyr, and that I shall repay to you the capital and the interest on the thirtieth of Mesore of the present seventh year of Hadrian Caesar the lord without delay; otherwise I shall pay you these with half again, together with interest for the overdue time at the same rate of one drachma per mina per month, you having the right of execution upon me and upon all my property, without prejudice to you, Dionysius, in the execution of the other two thousand drachmas of silver of capital which I owe you together with my son Paesis by another cheirograph, as it contains. This hand(written contract) is valid wherever it is produced and for anyone who produces it on your behalf. Year 7 of the Emperor Caesar Trajan Hadrian Augustus, Phaophi fourteenth.

(2nd hand) I, Thonis son of Harthonis, son of Petosiris, have received from Dionysius the two thousand drachmas of silver of capital and shall repay them with interest of one drachma (per mina per month) from the following month Hathyr on the thirtieth of Mesore of the present year, without prejudice to him regarding the other two thousand drachmas which I owe him together with my son Pausis by another cheirograph, as aforesaid. Seventh year of the Emperor Caesar Trajan Hadrian Augustus, Phaophi fourteenth.

(3rd hand) I, Dionysius, the aforesaid, have received from Thonis the aforesaid two thousand drachmas of silver and the interest, and I make no claim about anything at all. Eighth year of the Emperor Caesar Trajan Hadrian Augustus, Choiak 13.

(Recto) In the seventh [year] of the Emperor Caesar Trajan Hadrian [Augustus], on the seventh of the month Xandikos, Mecheir 7, at Bacchias of the division of Heraclides of the Arsinoite nome. Tauris daughter of [Ninis], about forty years old, with a scar on the left forearm near the wrist, [with] her paternal relative Horus son of Orsenuphis as guardian, about [...]-five years old, with a scar on the right shin, acknowledges to Tapekysis daughter of Horus, about 48 years old, with a scar on the [upper] lip to the left, with her husband Horus son of Horus as guardian, about 53 years old, with a scar on the left eyebrow, that she, the acknowledging party, has received from her a capital sum of sixty drachmas of coined silver of the imperial coinage, forthwith, from hand to hand, out of the house; and that in place of the interest on this the acknowledging party has granted to Tapekysis that she and her heirs and whomever she wishes shall live, for as long as the acknowledging party owes her the aforesaid money, in the paternal share of nine twenty-sevenths, held in common and undivided, of house-plots belonging to her, the acknowledging party, [in the] village, whose neighbours, as they dictated by mutual agreement, are: on the south, house-plots of Katoites son of Menches and partners, and for a certain part a common entrance and exit; on the north, a royal street; on the west, house-plots of Katoites son of Menches and partners; on the east, a courtyard of Horus son of Katoites, son of Belles, and his brothers; and that the acknowledging party guarantees it with every guarantee against anyone who may lay claim in any way whatsoever. If the acknowledging party wishes to repay the aforesaid money, let her repay [...] if Tapekysis is found to have spent money on repair of the dwelling, the credence resting with Tapekysis herself. Signatories: for the acknowledging party and her guardian, Dius son of Craton, about 25 years old, without distinguishing mark; for the others, Suchas son of Sochotes, about 43 years old, with a scar on the left wrist [...].

(2nd hand) I, Tauris daughter of Ninis, with my relative Horus son of Orsenuphis as guardian, acknowledge that I have received from Tapekysis the sixty drachmas of silver from hand to hand, and in place of the interest on these I grant her that she and her heirs [and whomever she wishes] shall live, for as long as I owe the aforesaid money, in the paternal [share of nine] twenty-sevenths, [held in common] and undivided, of house-plots belonging to me in [the village], whose [neighbours] are: on the south, house-plots of Katoites son of Menches and partners [...], [and for a certain] part an entrance [and exit]; [on the north], a royal street; on the west, [house-plots of] Katoites son of Menches [and partners; on the east, a courtyard of Horus] son of Katoites [son of Belles and his] brothers; [and] I shall guarantee it [with every guarantee against anyone] who may lay claim [in any way. If] I wish [to repay to Tapekysis the aforesaid] money, [I shall repay ... if Tapekysis is found] to have [spent money on repair of the dwelling, the credence resting with] Tape[kysis herself, as aforesaid]. [I, Dius son of Craton, wrote] for them since they do not know [letters].

(3rd hand) I, Tapekysis [daughter of Horus, with] my husband [Horus] son of [Horus as guardian]: [the agreement] has been made [with me] as aforesaid. I, [Such]as son of Sochotes, wrote [for them] since they do not know letters.

English translation:
Copy of an agreement.

In the tenth year of Emperor Caesar Trajan Hadrian Augustus, Pharmouthi 3, at Tebtunis in the division of Polemon of the Arsinoite nome. Dius, about twenty years old, with a scar on the second finger of the left hand, and Tyrannus alias Isidorus, about eighteen years old, with a scar on the forehead on the left below the hair, both sons of Zeuxis son of Dius, of the Sosikosmian tribe and Althaean deme, mutual sureties for payment, acknowledge to Hippalus son of Sarapas son of Areius, about forty-five years old, with a scar on the second finger of the left hand, that they have received from him, Hippalus, forthwith, from hand to hand, out of his house, an interest-bearing loan of capital of four hundred and ninety-six silver drachmas; and the acknowledging parties, Dius and Tyrannus alias Isidorus, are obliged to repay to Hippalus the four hundred and ninety-six silver drachmas of capital of the loan and the interest in the month Phamenoth of the coming eleventh year without any delay or evasion, Hippalus having the right of execution upon each of the acknowledging parties, upon one and upon whichever of them he chooses, and upon all their property [...], as if by a court judgment.

(Subscription) I, Dius son of Zeuxis, of the Sosikosmian tribe and Althaean deme, acknowledge that I have received, [together with] my [brother] Tyrannus alias Isidorus, under mutual surety, from Hippalus from hand to hand an interest-bearing loan of capital of four hundred and ninety-six silver drachmas, which we will repay in the month Phamenoth of the coming eleventh year without delay, as stated above.

I, Tyrannus alias Isidorus son of Zeuxis, of the Sosikosmian tribe and Althaean deme, acknowledge that I have received, together with my [brother Dius], under mutual surety, from Hippalus from hand to hand an interest-bearing loan of capital of 496 silver drachmas, which we will repay in the month Phamenoth of the coming eleventh year as stated above [...]. English translation:
Maximus to Isidorus, greetings. Look, it is three months since you received 14 drachmas from me, and you have given me neither interest nor capital. It is not reasonable that I should borrow while you owe me. I have no need of the interest. So give to my friend Serenus, the soldier in charge of fodder (chortarios), what I also owe (him). Farewell.

In the sixteenth year of Emperor Caesar Trajan Hadrian Augustus, month Sebastos 8, at Karanis in the division of Heraclides of the Arsinoite nome. Thasos daughter of Petheus son of Pasoknopaeus, about fifty years old, with a scar on the left hand, with her guardian, her husband Petesuchus son of Petaus, about sixty years old, with a scar on the left eyebrow, acknowledges to Petheus son of Pnepheros, about thirty years old, with a scar on the left knee, that she has received from him forthwith from hand to hand out of his house one hundred silver ⟨drachmas⟩ as a loan, at interest of one drachma per mina each month, and also twelve and one-sixth artabas of wheat by the six-choenix measure of the interpreter (hermeneus) of Karanis, which the acknowledging party is to repay to Petheus in the month Pauni of the present sixteenth year of Hadrian Caesar the lord. If she does not repay, let her pay forthwith with the half (penalty) and interest, Petheus having the right of execution upon the acknowledging party and upon all her property as if by a court judgment. Until she repays, Thasos is not permitted to sell or mortgage or otherwise dispose of the fifth share of a house and courtyard belonging to her in the village, of which the neighbours are: on the south the house of Mysthes son of Melanion, on the north the house of Bekeno.pso, on the west entrance and exit, on the east the royal [street]. Signatory: Heron son of Satyrus.

(Subscription) I, Thasos daughter of Petheus son of Pasoknopaeus, with my guardian, my husband Petesuchus son of Petaus, acknowledge that I have received from Petheus son of Pnepheros one hundred silver drachmas [...] and twelve and one-sixth artabas of wheat, [which I] will repay in the month Pauni of the present 16th year, and I keep secure the fifth share of a house and courtyard belonging to her in the same village. Heron son of Satyrus [wrote] on her behalf, as she does not know letters.

Registered through the record office in Karanis.

In the seventeenth year of Imperator Caesar Traianus Hadrianus Augustus, Pauni 28, at Tebtynis in the division of Polemon of the Arsinoite nome. Taonnophris daughter of Cronion the elder, son of Amais, from Tebtynis, about forty-eight years old, with a scar on the left hand, and her son Sarapion son of Heracles son of Heracles, about twenty-two years old, with a scar on the right forearm, both Persians of the epigone, Taonnophris acting with her son Sarapion as guardian and surety for payment, acknowledge to Herodes alias Diogenes son of Didymus the younger, one of the former gymnasiarchs, about forty-eight years old, without distinguishing marks, that they have received from Diogenes himself forthwith, through the bank of Apollonius and Sabinus at the Tameia in the metropolis, a loan of one thousand three hundred drachmas of silver capital, for one year from the present day, at interest of one drachma per mina each month.

And the acknowledging parties, Taonnophris and her son Sarapion, are obliged to repay to Diogenes, on mutual security, both the one thousand three hundred drachmas of capital and the one hundred and fifty-six drachmas of interest at one drachma accumulated over the year, together one thousand four hundred and fifty-six drachmas of silver, on the twenty-seventh of the month Pauni of the coming eighteenth year of Hadrianus Caesar the lord, without any delay or evasion.

And as security for the aforesaid capital and the interest, Taonnophris has voluntarily and of her own free choice pledged as hypallagma ⸌to Diogenes⸍, through the record office of property, the nine and a quarter arouras of purchased cleruchic land belonging to her around Tebtynis, in parts, in all, in two parcels, and in the village bare [plots], nine bikoi, one hundred and sixty-four and a half cubits; without prejudice to Herodes alias Diogenes regarding what the acknowledging parties [owe him] under another agreement of the present [day], of a capital of [one thousand two hundred drachmas of silver] and the interest [...].

Taonnophris daughter of Cronion [the elder, son of Amais, from Tebtynis], about forty-eight years old, with a scar on the left hand, and her [son Sarapion son of Heracles son of Heracles], about twenty-two years old, with a scar on the right forearm, both Persians of the [epigone, Taonnophris acting with] her son Sarapion [as guardian and surety] for payment, acknowledge to Herodes alias [Diogenes son of Didymus the younger, one of the former gymnasiarchs], about forty-eight years old, without distinguishing marks, [that they have received from Diogenes himself forthwith, through the] bank of Apollonius and Sabinus [at the Tameia] in the metropolis, [a loan of] one thousand two hundred [drachmas of silver capital], for one year from the present [day, at interest of one drachma per mina] each month.

And the acknowledging parties, [Taonnophris and her son Sarapion], are obliged [to repay] to Herodes alias Diogenes, on mutual security, both [the one thousand two hundred drachmas of capital and] the [one hundred and forty-four] drachmas of interest at one drachma accumulated over the year, [together] one thousand three hundred and forty-four drachmas of silver, [on the twenty-seventh of the month Pauni] of the coming eighteenth year of Hadrianus Caesar the [lord, without any delay or evasion];

without prejudice to Herodes alias Diogenes [regarding what the acknowledging parties owe him] under another agreement of the present day, [of a capital of one thousand three] hundred [drachmas of silver] and the interest, and regarding the [...] which he holds from Taonnophris [... belonging to her], nine and a quarter arouras of cleruchic land around Tebtynis and [in the village bare plots, nine bikoi], one hundred and sixty-four and a half cubits, and not [... if] she does not repay these also; Herodes alias [Diogenes having the right of execution] against Taonnophris and her son Sarapion and against each one [and against whichever of them he chooses, and against] the aforesaid property held under hypallagma [...].

Year 22 of Imperator Caesar Titus Aelius Hadrianus Augustus, Pauni 18. The following has been set down by the Mesobeites Tithoes son of Psenamounis son of Psais, his mother being Tasechthis, about 45 years old, with a scar under the left knee, and Talaeis daughter of Horus son of Patchalmis, her mother being Tapsais, about 40 years old, with a scar on the right shin, his wife, mutual sureties for payment, agreeing with the Mesobeites Tithoes son of Bekis son of Psais, his mother being Tbekis: We owe you one hundred and forty drachmas of silver, total 140 drachmas, which we will also repay to you in the coming 23rd year of Hadrianus Caesar the lord, Pauni 18, without delay. If we do not pay you in full by the aforesaid term, we will pay you interest at one drachma for the time overrun, and you may obtain satisfaction from all that we have and whatever we may acquire, and we shall not sell or mortgage until we have first paid you in full.

I, Harpocras, contract-writer (synallagmatographos) of Mesobe, have executed (this) through ..athes alias Philetes, the scribe.

We, Tithoes son of Psenamounis son of Psais, and Talaeis daughter of Horus, his wife, with her guardian Tithoes, the aforesaid, to Tithoes son of Bekis: we have made with you the aforesaid loan of the one hundred and forty drachmas of silver as aforesaid. In the fourth year of Imperator Caesar Titus Aelius Hadrianus Antoninus Augustus Pius, Thoth 28, at Tebtynis of the division of Polemon of the Arsinoite nome. Taorsenuphis, about forty-five years old, with a scar on the left shin, and Tephorsais, about thirty-five years old, with a scar on the left hand, both daughters of Cronion son of Cheos, each with a guardian, Taorsenuphis with her father Cronion son of Cheos, about seventy-eight years old, with a scar on the little finger of the left hand, and Tephorsais with her husband, who is also her brother, Harphaesis, about forty-eight years old, with a scar on the left thumb, the two Persian women of the descent, mutual sureties for payment, acknowledge to Didyme daughter of Heron son of Amais, about forty-six years old, with a scar on the left shin, with her guardian, her cousin on the mother's side Harpaesis son of Heracleus, about [...]ty years old, with a scar on the left hand, that they have received from her, Didyme, [immediately] from hand to hand an interest-bearing loan of a capital sum of [three hundred] seventy-[two silver drachmas], the repayment of which they shall [necessarily] make in [the month Thoth of the coming] fifth [year without delay]; and if they do not [repay as] written within the [aforesaid] term, Didyme [or her assign] shall be permitted, if she chooses, to take the produce for her own benefit, from the same fifth year, of two arouras out of the catoecic holding of four arouras belonging to Tephorsais near the village of Tebtynis in the so-called diaita of Stasicrates, from whichever end or part Didyme chooses, all the public dues on the two arouras being borne by Tephorsais; and if she does not allow Didyme to take the produce, Didyme shall have the right of execution upon [the acknowledging parties] or upon either one of them and upon all their property, [as if by a court] judgment. Signatory: Hippalus son of Chrates, about [seventy ...] years old, with a scar on the right forearm.

(Subscription) [We], Taorsenuphis and [Tephorsais], both daughters of Cronion, each with a guardian, [Taorsenuphis] with her father, Tephorsais with her husband Harphaesis, [acknowledge that we have] received from Didyme on mutual security the three hundred and eighty-two drachmas as a loan, which [we shall repay] in the month Thoth of the fifth year; and if [not, she may take] the produce of the two arouras near Tebtynis as [aforesaid. Hippalus son of Chrates wrote] on their behalf, as they do not know [letters].

[Didy]me daughter of Heron, with her guardian, her cousin on the mother's side [Harpaesis] son of Heracleus: the agreement has been made with me [as aforesaid]. Maron son of Maron wrote on their behalf, as they do not know letters.

English translation:
Dionysius alias P[lution ...] son of Dionysius [...] from [the city of the Oxyrhynchi] to Diodorus [...] from the same city, greeting. I acknowledge that I have received from you from hand to hand out of your house eight hundred [and forty]-eight drachmas of silver [of the imperial] coinage, to which nothing at all has been added, which I will also repay to you on the thirtieth [of the month ... of the] present fourth year of Antoninus Caesar the lord. If I do not repay as written, I will pay you the capital now stated plus one half, and interest at the drachma rate for the time elapsed beyond the term, you having the right of execution upon me and upon all my property, as if by a court judgment. This handwritten note of mine, Dionysius alias Plution, is valid wherever it is produced and for anyone who produces it. In the fourth year of Imperator Caesar Titus Aelius Hadrianus Antoninus Augustus Pius, Hathyr 24.

English translation:
Copy. To Eudaemon, former kosmetes, priest, chief judge (archidikastes) and in charge of the chrematistai and the other courts, from Lucius Valerius Ammonianus, actuarius of the cohort of armed Roman citizens, century of Apollinarius, and from Quintus Gellius Valens, soldier of the Augustan Alexandrian fleet, of the liburnian Luppa. Quintus Gellius Valens agrees that he has received from Lucius Valerius Ammonianus as a loan, through the money-changing bank of Andronicus son of Aphrodisius, eight hundred drachmas of silver of the imperial coinage, at interest of one drachma per mina per month, for eight months from the month Sebastos Eusebeios of the present seventh year of Antoninus Caesar the lord, on the mortgage of [...] [...] of the division of Heraclides [...] seventy-five arouras, whose neighbours, as they declared, are: on the south, (land) of Amadocus son of Ptolemaeus and in the name of [...]; on the north, [...] and royal land; on the east, royal land; on the west, the holding of Longinus. Quintus Gellius Valens shall necessarily repay to Lucius Valerius Ammonianus the eight hundred drachmas of silver within the aforesaid time, and the interest each month. If he does not repay, Lucius Valerius Ammonianus shall be permitted to carry out the legal procedures against the mortgage for whatever it may bear, and for any deficit he shall have the right of execution upon the other property of the debtor; and if, which may it not happen, any risk should befall the mortgage or part of it, in that case too the lender shall have the right of execution as has been stated for the deficit. And he (the borrower) shall provide the mortgage free, untouched and not pledged for any other loan or any debt, and no one laying claim to it in any way; without prejudice to Valerius Ammonianus regarding the other sums that the same Gellius Valens owes him under another agreement (synchoresis) of the past year, in the month Kaisareios, of another four hundred and sixty drachmas of silver and interest; and he shall not release this mortgage unless he first repays also the four hundred and sixty drachmas under the contract and the interest, because they are mutually secured. In the seventh year of Imperator Caesar Titus Aelius Hadrianus Antoninus Augustus Pius, month Sebastos Eusebeios 16.

From the register of the record office of the villages of Nilopolis and Socnopaei Nesus. Year 8 of the Emperor Caesar Titus Aelius Hadrianus Antoninus Augustus Pius, Epeiph 14. Soeris daughter of Stotoetis son of Panephremmis, her mother being Taphiomis, priestess, from the village of Socnopaei Nesus, aged about 50, with a scar on the right wrist, with her guardian, her husband Stotoetis son of Stotoetis, grandson of Stotoetis, called Paramon, priest of the second tribe of Socnopaeus the twice-great god, aged about 50, with a scar on the right shin, acknowledges to Anchophis son of Stotoetis son of Panephremmis, fellow priest, from the same village, aged about 40, with a scar on the little finger of the left hand, that she, the acknowledging party, has received from him forthwith from hand to hand five hundred drachmas of coined imperial silver as principal; [and in place of] their interest the acknowledging party Soeris is obliged to furnish to Anchophis and his assigns, [from the first of the month] Thoth of the coming 9th year of Antoninus Caesar the lord, the slave girl belonging to her, [called] Soteris, a weaver, working at the loom at the place of whomever Anchophis wishes, in [...]; she shall make over to Anchophis the daily wage for two years and [...] until the acknowledging party Soeris repays the aforesaid principal, the slave girl being fed and clothed by Soeris, and moreover all her public dues being the responsibility of the same Soeris. If the slave girl Soteris is idle, or runs away, or falls ill, she shall remain in service for an equal number of days for all of these after the term. If anything human befalls her within the term, the acknowledging party is obliged to repay the aforesaid principal together with the [interest] that will have accrued, Anchophis having the right of execution upon the acknowledging party and upon all her property [of every kind] as if by a court judgement; and the acknowledging party Soeris is obliged to furnish the [aforesaid] slave girl free of every public debt or private [obligation], and in the meantime [not to] deal [with her] through any record office until she [repays] the aforesaid [principal ...] [...] son of Dionysius, aged 3[.], [with a scar] on the right eyebrow and [...] left [...].

Twelfth year of the Emperor Caesar Titus Aelius Hadrianus Antoninus Augustus Pius, month Xandicus 12, Mecheir 12, at Heraclia of the division of Themistes of the Arsinoite nome. Thaesis daughter of Panephremmis son of Tesenouphis, from the village of Socnopaei Nesus, Persian, aged about 57, with a scar on the left forearm, with her guardian and surety, her son Stotoetis son of Stotoetis, aged about 30, with a scar on the left shin, and Thaesis' other sons, Horus, aged about 37, with a scar below the right knee, and Panephremmis, aged about 26, with a scar on the left forearm, both sons of Stotoetis, acknowledge to Heraclia daughter of Dioscorus son of Dioscorus, aged about 33, with a scar in the middle of the forehead below the hair, with her guardian, her kinsman Soterichus son of Zosimus, aged about 34, with a scar [...] left [...], that Thaesis has received from her forthwith from hand to hand an interest-bearing loan of one thousand two hundred drachmas of silver as principal, at interest of one drachma [per mina] each month, the repayment of which the acknowledging party Thaesis shall make to Heraclia in the month [Tybi of the] coming thirteenth year of Antoninus Caesar the lord without delay; and that Thaesis has given as a pledge and security for the aforesaid principal and the interest the five arouras of catoecic land belonging to her near the aforesaid village of Heraclia, formerly of Ammonarion daughter of Artemidorus, together with a third of an aroura of village epibole, and the two slaves belonging to her, maintained in partnership with Tamystha, weaver; over all of which she shall not have full power to sell, mortgage or otherwise dispose until she repays the aforesaid principal and the interest. As for the aforesaid sons Stotoetis [and Horus and] Panephremmis: if their mother Thaesis [does not repay] at the aforesaid term, or, if time is extended, does not pay [its] interest, they, the sons, [must] repay out of their own means, whether [their mother] is present or absent or no longer alive, without delay, Heraclia having the right of execution upon Thaesis and the aforesaid sons [and all their property] as if by a court judgement. Subscribers: for Thaesis, her guardian, and for Panephr[emmis ...].

[I, Thaesis daughter of Panephrem]mis son of [Tesen]ouphis, my mother being Soeris daughter of Panephremmis, with my guardian [and surety], my son Stotoetis son of Stotoetis, acknowledge that I have from Heraclia the [aforesaid] one thousand two hundred drachmas of silver as principal at interest of one drachma per mina each month, which I shall also repay in the month Tybi of the coming year, and I have given the aforesaid pledge as stated above. I, [Stotoe]tis, wrote [also for] my mother, who is illiterate. I, Panephremmis, stand surety as stated above. I, Horus son of Stotoetis, stand surety as stated above. I, Alcimus, scribe of the aforesaid [record office, wrote for] him, as he says he does not know letters. Registered through the record office at Heraclia.

[Ptolemaeus son of Apion grandson of Apion, mother Sarapous, from the city of Oxyrhynchus, Persian of the epigone, to Apion alias Petosorapis son of Petosorapis grandson of Petosorapis, one of the former kosmetai of the same city, greeting. I shall guarantee to you and your successors the slave and the offspring to be born from now on with every guarantee, and it shall not be permitted to me, unless I first repay the six hundred drachmas and the interest, to sell or mortgage or otherwise dispose of the slave Isarous or the offspring to be born of her, you having the choice, if I do not perform rightly, as you prefer, after the term either to be owner of the slave and of the offspring to be born in place of the six [hundred] drachmas and the interest, or to exact everything, including the interest at a drachma for the time overdue, from me and from the slave Isarous and the offspring to be born of her and from all my other property. If flight or death or injury befall the same Isarous or the offspring to be born, no loss shall follow for the [same c]apital and the interest, nor for any part, since [they are all] free from every risk. This autograph hand-written bond of mine, which I have written [in duplicate], is valid. Year thirteen of Imperator Caesar Titus Aelius Hadrianus [Anton]inus Augustus Pius, Pharmouthi 19.
