[Year fifteen of Imperator Caesar] Titus Ae[lius Hadrianus Anto]ninus Augustus [Pius, m]onth Hadrianos 2[.], at [Hermo]polis [the Great]. Hermione daughter of Eudaemon grandson of Sarapion, citizen, aged about 17, with as guardian her father Eudaemon son of Sarapion grandson of Dionysius, of the Sosikosmian tribe and the Althaean deme, aged about 65, with an injured left eye, has lent to Demetria alias Tereus daughter of Horion grandson of Eudaemon, [mother] Ptolema daughter of Hermocles, of Hermopolis, registered in the property records in the quarter of the Fort West and in the public accounts in the quarter of [the Fort East, aged about .., scar ...] on the left, with as guardian her husband Phibion [son of Pathotes, aged about] 36, scar on the forehead on the left, of silver of imperial coinage, capital two thousand drachmas, which the borrower has drawn from the lender through the overseers of the bank, at interest of four silver obols [per mina per mon]th each month from the month [Hadrianos of the] present year, for sixty months, the interest amounting to eight [hundred] drachmas, all on the security of the two and a half and one third arouras of catoecic land belonging to the borrower out of the kleros of Hippostratus near Tekerkethothis in the Lower Leukopyrgites, which the borrower shall also hand over in the field, sown, full by the just catoecic measuring line, free from royal (charges) and every kind at all, whose neighbours, as the borrower declared, are: on the south Sarammon son of Achilles, on the north and west Horigenes, on the east [... The loan, the] two thousand eight hundred drachmas of silver [of capital and inter]est, the borrower shall repay to the lender or her representatives on the thirtieth of the month Hathyr of the twentieth year of Antoninus Caesar the lord, forthwith, in approved, current, acceptable silver. If she does not repay when the [term] has arrived, [the lender shall be permitted immediately], or her representatives, without needing renewal or a letter of instruction or anything else at all, to have the mortgaged arouras transferred (to her name) through the catoecic registers, as is proper, and she and her representatives shall own them outright in place of the sums owed, and enter upon [them and en]joy their fruits and lease them out and carry off for their own the yearly produce from them and all profits, and moreover use and manage them in whatever way they choose for all time, no claim or pretext concerning this being left to the borrower or to anyone else on her behalf [hereafter] at all. The borrower shall guarantee this mortgage with every guarantee against public and private (claims) and against all at all, and she shall not be permitted to sell it or mortgage it to others or devise any other contrivance about it [contrary] to these terms in [any] way, [or else] anything contrary to these terms shall be invalid. If any risk arises concerning this mortgage, whole or part, in any way whatsoever, the borrower shall repay to the lender or her representatives all the sums owed, and for the time overdue after the [fixed] term interest of four silver obols per mina each month, and whatever taxes the lender may be required to pay for this mortgage and whatever expenses she may incur, likewise with interest, each forthwith, the lender or her representatives having the right of execution against the borrower and [against this] mortgage [and against] all her other property, as if by legal judgment. The contract is valid; and the borrower has been registered with it, the keepers of the property records having sent notification. I, Demetria alias Tereus daughter of Horion, with as guardian my husband Phibion son of Pathotes, [have borrowed from] Hermione [daughter of Eudae]mon the two thousand drachmas of silver of capital, which I have drawn from her through the aforesaid bank, at interest of four silver obols per mina each month from the month Hadrianos of the present year for sixty months, the interest amounting to eight hundred drachmas, all on the security of the two and a half and one third arouras of catoecic land, not liable to claim (anaitetos), belonging to me out of the kleros of Hippostratus near Tekerkethothis in the Lower Leukopyrgites, which I shall also hand over in the field, sown, full by the just catoecic measuring line, free from royal (charges) and [every kind at all, within the a]foresaid boundaries. This loan of capital and interest, two thousand eight hundred drachmas of silver, I shall repay on the thirtieth of the month Hathyr of the twentieth year of Antoninus Caesar the lord, and I shall guarantee this mortgage, and I consent to all the above-written terms. I, Phibion [son of Pathotes, have signed as guardian] of my wife and wrote on her behalf since she does not know letters. I, Hermione daughter of Eudaemon, citizen, consent. I, Eudaemon son of Sarapion grandson of Dionysius, of the Sosikosmian tribe and the Althaean deme, have signed as guardian of my daughter and wrote on her behalf since she does not know letters. English translation:
Year sixteen of Imperator Caesar Titus Aelius Hadrianus Antoninus Augustus Pius, month Artemisios, Phamenoth 28, at Hermopolis the Great. Hermione daughter of Eudaemon, citizen, aged about 19, with as guardian her father Eudaemon son of Sarapion grandson of Dionysius, of the Sosikosmian tribe and the Althaean deme, aged about 67, with an injured left eye, has lent to Ptolema alias Tbesis daughter of Horion grandson of Hermias, mother Demetria alias Tereus daughter of Horion, of Hermopolis, registered in the Fort West (quarter), aged about 30, scar in the middle of the forehead, with as guardian her father Horion son of Hermias, aged about 54, scar on the forehead on the left, of silver of imperial coinage, capital two hundred drachmas, which the borrower has drawn from the lender through the overseers of the bank, at interest of a drachma per mina each month from the present day for twenty-four months, the interest amounting to forty-eight drachmas, all on the security of the remaining one and one quarter beikos belonging to the borrower of an idle oil-press and vaulted room and court and all appurtenances in the village of Tekerkethothis in the Lower Leukopyrgites, after (the parts) sold from the same premises. The neighbours, as the borrower declared, are: on the south a public street, through which is the entrance and exit; on the north the heirs of Pathotes son of Phibis; on the east a road; on the west Demetria alias Tereus daughter of Horion. The loan, the two hundred forty-eight drachmas of silver of capital and interest, the borrower shall repay to the lender or her representatives when the two-year period is completed, forthwith, in approved, current, acceptable silver. If she does not repay when the term has arrived, the lender or her representatives shall be permitted immediately, without needing renewal or a letter of instruction or anything else at all, after paying the dues proper for the enkyklion (tax), to make foreclosure (epikatabole) on the one and one quarter beikos mortgaged as stated above, and she and her representatives shall own it outright in place of the sums owed, and enter upon it and settle tenants in it and collect rents and lease it out and carry off for their own all profits from it, and moreover use and manage it in whatever way they choose for all time, no claim or pretext concerning this being left to the borrower or to anyone else on her behalf hereafter at all. The borrower shall guarantee this mortgage with every guarantee against public and private (claims) and against all at all, and she shall not be permitted to sell it or mortgage it to others or devise any other contrivance about it contrary to these terms in any way, or else anything contrary to these terms shall be invalid. If any risk arises concerning this mortgage, whole or part, in any way whatsoever, the borrower shall repay to the lender or her representatives all the sums owed, and for the time overdue after the term interest of a drachma per mina each month, and whatever taxes the lender may be required to pay for this mortgage and whatever expenses she may incur, likewise with interest, each forthwith, the lender or her representatives having the right of execution against the borrower and against this mortgage and against all her other property, as if by legal judgment. The contract is valid. And the borrower has been registered with it, the keepers of the property records having sent notification. I, Ptolema alias Tbesis daughter of Horion, with as guardian my father Horion son of Hermias, have borrowed from Hermione daughter of Eudaemon two hundred drachmas of silver of capital, which I have drawn through the overseers of the bank, at interest of a drachma per mina each month from the present day for twenty-four months, the interest amounting to forty-eight drachmas, all on the security of the remaining one and one quarter beikos belonging to me of an idle oil-press and vaulted room and court and all appurtenances in the village of Tekerkethothis in the Lower Leukopyrgites, after (the parts) sold of the same premises, within the aforesaid boundaries. These two hundred forty-eight drachmas of silver of capital and interest I shall repay when the two-year period is completed, and I shall guarantee (the mortgage), and I consent to all the above-written terms. I, Herminus son of Herodes, wrote the body of the subscription.

English translation:
In the nineteenth year of Imperator Caesar Titus Aelius Hadrianus [Antoninus Augustus] Pius, month Hadrianus 9, through the record office of ... [at Tebtynis] of the Arsinoite nome. Lamprotyche, [freedwoman] of Heraclous alias Thermoutharion daughter of Didymus, [with as guardian the ... kinsman of her manumitter, Heraclides son of Heraclides], has lent [to Protous daughter of Heraclas son] of Herodes son of ... ... with [as guardian and] surety for payment her kinsman [Eutyches son of Ptolemaeus son of Ptolemaeus, ..., Persian of the epigone, aged] fifty-eight, [in accordance with the public] record office, [of silver capital] one thousand three hundred and sixty drachmas, which [the borrower] has also received [from the lender forthwith through the] bank of Aelius Euporus near the Gymnasium, for [nine] months [from the present month Hadrianus, at interest of] one drachma per mina each month. [The borrower is to repay] the one thousand three hundred and sixty drachmas lent [from the present month Hadrianus] and the interest at one drachma [in the month Mesore of the present] nineteenth year of Antoninus [Caesar the lord] without delay, [Lamprotyche having the right] of execution upon the property of Protous, [both upon] all the aforesaid or upon whichever she chooses [and upon] all [her property], as if by legal decision. ... has made ... for the aforesaid capital and interest ... of mortgage of a catoecic allotment of two arouras [near the village of Tebtynis] and a machimic [allotment of one aroura, together three arouras], [without prejudice to] her regarding the other sums which she owes her [... under] another loan of silver capital [nine hundred drachmas] and the interest from the present month Hadrianus. The loan [is to be valid].

I, [Protous daughter of Heraclas] son of Herodes, with as guardian and surety for payment my kinsman [Eutyches son of Ptolemaeus son of] Ptolemaeus, have borrowed from Lamprotyche through the bank of Aelius [Euporus] the one thousand three hundred and sixty silver drachmas, from the present month Hadrianus at interest of one drachma per mina each month, [and I will repay the] capital and the interest [in the month] Mesore of the present [nineteenth] year, [without prejudice] to her [regarding what I] owe her under another loan of capital [nine hundred drachmas] and the interest from the present month, the mortgage remaining valid as aforesaid. I, [Mench]es, wrote also on behalf of Protous, [who is illiterate].

I, Lamprotyche, freedwoman of Heraclous alias Thermoutharion daughter of Didymus, [with as guardian the ...] of my manumitter, [...] Heraclides son of Heraclides, [have lent] as aforesaid. I, Heraclides, [wrote] also on her behalf, [as she is illiterate]. [as she is illiterate].

English translation:
To Marcus Sempronius Liberalis, prefect of Egypt, from Pharion son of Eutyches son of Heraclides, of those from the metropolis of the Arsinoite nome. Of the petition which I submitted to you, my lord, and of the subscription I received under it, by which I was referred, as number 233, to Severus, the official in charge of the kekrimenoi, ... I have appended a copy. Since then ... of my adversary Heron son of Amatius, former exegetes of the city of the Arsinoites, with arrogance and violence, being very powerful in the district, and I shall not be able (to contend) against him before such judges, since he is a great potentate. That you may know Heron's arrogance: a certain Paulinus, son of a gymnasiarch, petitioned Eudorus, strategus of the (divisions) of Themistes and Polemon, bringing charges against Heron, and the strategus summoned Heron, and he behaved arrogantly, and the strategus recorded a minute about him. My lord prefect, I have shown you the arrogance of my adversary; I beg you, lord, saviour of Egypt, to hear me against him, so that I may be able to remain in my own home. The copy of the petition is as follows:

To Marcus Sempronius, prefect of Egypt, from Pharion son of Eutyches son of Heraclides. Since your innate beneficence, my lord prefect, has reached everyone, I too, being oppressed and wronged in many ways, have hastened to you as a refuge to obtain justice. I set out the matter: being in need, I borrowed from Heron son of Amatius, former exegetes of the city of the Arsinoites, small sums of money at various times; so that, relying on the dignity of his office, being very powerful in the district, he continually inflicts insults and wrongs on me, although he has been paid in full the interest at the rate of a stater which he forced me by violence to promise, which exceeded the capital by almost one and a half times. On account of this I am in danger of leaving and emigrating. Therefore, taking refuge with you, the saviour of all, I ask, if it please your Fortune, to hear me against him, so that what he has received from me may be reckoned up, and if from the reckoning of the account anything appears justly owed to him, he may receive it, so that I may be able to obtain (justice) through your beneficence.

If we do not repay as written, we shall pay you the aforesaid capital with the interest that will accrue, with half as much again, and you shall have the right of execution upon us and upon all our property, we being mutual sureties for payment, and upon whichever one of us you choose. The note of hand, written in two identical copies, is valid wherever produced and for everyone who produces it on your behalf. Year 2 of Imperator Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Augustus and Imperator Caesar Lucius Aurelius Verus Augustus, [...] 9.

I, Zoilus son of Aphynchis, have received together with the others nine artabas of barley and we shall repay [you] with interest of three artabas, total twelve artabas, as mutual sureties, as aforesaid. I, Didymus alias Zoilus son of Didymus, wrote on his behalf as he does not know letters. We, Pasis son of Diogenes and Psois son of Harpsois, have received jointly and will repay jointly as aforesaid. I, Heracles son of Achilles, wrote on their behalf as they do not know letters. The same date.

[Dionysia daughter of Diogenes, Persian of the Epigone, with her guardian, my husband Sarapion son of Soptakus, to Demetrius son of Sarapas by adoption, all from the city of Oxyrhynchus, greeting. I acknowledge that I have received from you from hand to hand as a loan eight hundred drachmas of silver of imperial coinage as capital], to which nothing at all [has been added], at interest of one drachma (per mina) per month from the present month Thoth, Thoth itself included; and I will pay you the interest monthly, credence resting with you concerning any (payments) for which I do not produce written receipts to you, and the capital on the thirtieth of Mesore of the coming ninth year of Antoninus and Verus the lords Imperatores, without delay. If I do not repay, I shall pay with the addition of one half, together with interest at one drachma also for the time overrun, you having the right of execution upon me and upon all my property, and you, Demetrius, being permitted yourself, from now, whenever you choose, to place a restraint on my name through the property record office until you recover the capital and the interest. The handwritten document is valid. Year 8 of Imperator Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Augustus Armeniacus Medicus Parthicus Maximus and Imperator Caesar Lucius Aurelius Verus Augustus Armeniacus Medicus Parthicus Maximus, Thoth 28.

English translation:
Recto: To Callon, nomarch of Antinoopolis, from Lysimachus alias Didymus and Philosarapis, both sons of Heraclides, of the Matidian deme also called Kalliteknian. Philantinous, another brother of ours, acting recklessly, mortgaged our mother's slave named Martilla to a certain moneylender in the Arsinoite, without our consent, on terms of rearing (ἐπʼ ἐκτροφῇ), improperly carrying off the money alone for his own use. We therefore submit this petition, asking that you keep it on record as testimony, so that we may be able to recover our own shares of the slave girl, that we may be helped. Farewell. Year 9 of Imperator Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Augustus Armeniacus Medicus Parthicus Maximus and Imperator Caesar Lucius Aurelius Verus Augustus Armeniacus Medicus Parthicus Maximus, Thoth 15. I, Lysimachus alias Didymus, have submitted it. I, Philosarapis son of Heraclides, have submitted it jointly.

Verso: Complaint of Lysimachus.

Col. 1: [...] the under[written ... of the under]written [...] 3 arouras [...] catoecic [...] 4 1/2 arouras [...] and ... 20 1/2 arouras [...] in the name of [his] father [...]. Concerning Pinauas [...] 2 arouras and catoecic [... in the] name of his father [...] 5 1/2 arouras. And thus [...] the keepers of the record office have [...] having been handed in [...] around the village of Kerke[...] the property [...] of the property record office [...] of the strategi [...] 1,500 [drachmas]. I [...] worth so much [...] talents [...] this [...] agreement [...].

Col. 2: and the interest up to year 12 [...] in the following year 13 to have been transferred for sale for the present year, 2,980 drachmas, total together 4 talents 2,980 drachmas. And if you think fit to write to the strategus of the nome to put these up for auction, and if he does not find a higher (bid), to deliver them to me at the price I offered, there being credited to me the capital owed on security and the interest; but if he finds more than the two talents, (the surplus) to be paid over to me, since I am eager to buy them, (namely) the capital owed to me and the interest, so that I may be benefited. Farewell.

Since it was ordered that these be delivered to the creditors only for the surplus, from among many precedents I have subjoined for you a copy of a letter of Mallius Crassus, former dioecetes:
"Mallius Crassus to Herodes, strategus of the Mendesian (nome), greeting. Having signed the petition of Damarion son of Isidorus, I have sent it to you. If then the loan stated was made before Apollonius, one of the debtors, became strategus, and this right was from that time lodged under his name in the property record office, the loan cannot be annulled. If, as the [chrematistai say], documents are produced from the record office in Alexandria, it is sufficient that the mortgaged properties, having been put up for auction, [be handed over], the surplus, if there is any, paying off the debts of the said Apollonius. Year 22 of Antoninus [Caesar the] lord, Tybi 1. I have signed [...]. [Herodes the strat]egus has replied."
Taartysis [...] to you, my lord, a petition [...] wishing [...] debt [...] talents [...].

Col. 3: [...] I wrote to you [...] public [...] your and the [...] wishing [...] none the less also [...] and of no other [...] you have received the writing [...] and of the declared [...]. Year 23 of Antoninus Caesar the lord [...]. And the above letters were subjoined [for Cosmus the procurator ...] and he replied: [...] "Cosmus to Isidorus [... greeting ...] still even now to put up for auction [...]. Year 23 of Antoninus Caesar [the lord ...]."

English translation:
Col. 1: Artemidorus, nomarch of Anti[noopolis], to Damarion, strategus of the Themistes and Polemon divisions, his dearest, greeting. Of the petition given to me on referral by the most excellent epistrategus Vettius Turbo, from Lysimachus alias Didymus son of Heraclides, of the Matidian deme also called Kalliteknian, I have sent you a copy, dearest, so that you may send here Serenus, named in it, to be judged according to the regulations for the Antinoites. I pray for your health, dearest. Year 22 of Imperator Caesar Marcus Aurelius Commodus Antoninus Augustus Armeniacus Medicus Parthicus Sarmaticus Germanicus Maximus, Mesore 2.

Col. 2: To Artemidorus, nomarch of Antinoopolis, from Lysimachus alias Didymus son of Heraclides, of the Matidian deme also called Kalliteknian. I have subjoined a copy of the petition which I submitted to Vettius Turbo, the most excellent epistrategus, and of the subscription I obtained from him, and I ask you to write to the strategus of the Themistes and Polemon divisions of the Arsinoite to send here the person named in it, to be judged with me according to the regulations for the Antinoites. Farewell. It is as follows: To Vettius Turbo, the most excellent epistrategus, from Lysimachus alias Didymus son of Heraclides, of the Matidian deme also called Kalliteknian, Antinoite. I lent, lord, to Dius son of Chaeremon grandson of Chaeremon, from the village of Talei of the Polemon division of the Arsinoite nome, by his cheirograph written in his own hand in duplicate, a capital of two hundred and forty silver drachmas at interest of one drachma per mina each month, in the 18th year of Aurelius Commodus Antoninus Caesar the lord, son of the god Aurelius Antoninus, in the month Hathyr; and before repayment had been made, the aforesaid Dius died leaving heirs. Since their guardian Serenus does not wish to make repayment to me of the capital and the interest, putting me off from one day to the next and despising my stay here, I beg you, if it please your fortune, to order that a letter be written to the strategus of the Themistes and Polemon divisions of the Arsinoite nome to send the aforesaid Serenus here to Antinoopolis, according to the regulations for the Antinoites, to be judged with me about this, so that I may be able with your help to recover what is mine and be forever grateful to your fortune, that I may be benefited. Farewell. I, Lysimachus alias Didymus, have submitted it. Year 22, Hadrianus 30.
Apply to the nomarch, who will examine your request. Return it. Up to here the copy. Year 22 of Imperator Caesar Marcus Aurelius Commodus Antoninus Augustus Armeniacus Medicus Parthicus Sarmaticus Germanicus Maximus, Epeiph 23. I, Lysimachus alias Didymus, have submitted it.

Aurelius Casius, priest and archidicastes, to the strategus of the Oxyrhynchite nome, greeting. Let a copy of the publication that has been effected be served, as set out below. Farewell. Year 24 of Aurelius Severus Antoninus Caesar the lord, Mecheir 5. I, Marcus Aurelius Harpocration, have signed; 14 drachmas. I, Marcus Aurelius Nemesianus also called Irenaeus, and however I am styled, scribe of the katalogeion, wrote the document.

To Lucius Septimius Aurelius Casius, priest, archidicastes and in charge of the superintendence of the chrematistae and the other courts, from Aurelia Didyme also called Dionysia, and however she is styled. A copy of the security issued to me in duplicate and of the subscription beneath it is appended:

'Pekysis son of Pausirion, his mother being Tetheus, from the city of Oxyrhynchus, to Aurelia Didyme also called Dionysia, and however she is styled, through Suchammon, freedman of your grandfather Aurelius Diogenes, greeting. I acknowledge that I owe you the forty-five artabas of wheat which I received from you on loan, and I will repay these to you without interest in the month Epeiph of the present 23rd year, in wheat that is new, pure, unadulterated, free of earth and of barley, sifted, as measured for the public account, here in the Oxyrhynchite nome, by your receiving-measure of the village of Syron, your agents doing the measuring, all without delay; otherwise I will pay you for the time overrun interest at the rate of one half, you having the right of execution upon me and upon all my property of every kind. This hand(-written bond), written in duplicate, is valid wherever it is produced and for anyone who produces it on your behalf. Year 23 of Imperator Caesar Marcus Antoninus Parthicus Maximus Britannicus Maximus Germanicus Maximus Pius Augustus, Choiak 20. I, Pekysis [son of Pausirion, have received the aforesaid] forty-five artabas and will repay as aforesaid.'

[Since the time limits have passed and] no repayment has been made, I wish, from the duplicate (bond), [...] [...]

Aurelius Heraclides son of Achilles [alias ...], his mother being Thaesis, from the city of Oxyrhynchus, [to Aurelius] ..., exegetes [...], pompagogos, councillor of the same [city, greeting]. Aurelius Cornelius son of Eudaemon, of Hermopolis, registered in the quarter of the West Fort, to Aurelius Phoebammon son of Posidonius, pancratiast, periodonikes, Roman, crowned with gold, paradoxos, and however I am styled, greetings. English translation:
In the sixteenth year of Emperor Caesar Trajan Hadrian Augustus, month Sebastos 8, at Karanis in the division of Heraclides of the Arsinoite nome. Thasos daughter of Petheus son of Pasoknopaeus, about fifty years old, with a scar on the left hand, with her guardian, her husband Petesuchus son of Petaus, about sixty years old, with a scar on the left eyebrow, acknowledges to Petheus son of Pnepheros, about thirty years old, with a scar on the left knee, that she has received from him forthwith from hand to hand out of his house one hundred silver ⟨drachmas⟩ as a loan, at interest of one drachma per mina each month, and also twelve and one-sixth artabas of wheat by the six-choenix measure of the interpreter (hermeneus) of Karanis, which the acknowledging party is to repay to Petheus in the month Pauni of the present sixteenth year of Hadrian Caesar the lord. If she does not repay, let her pay forthwith with the half (penalty) and interest, Petheus having the right of execution upon the acknowledging party and upon all her property as if by a court judgment. Until she repays, Thasos is not permitted to sell or mortgage or otherwise dispose of the fifth share of a house and courtyard belonging to her in the village, of which the neighbours are: on the south the house of Mysthes son of Melanion, on the north the house of Bekeno.pso, on the west entrance and exit, on the east the royal [street]. Signatory: Heron son of Satyrus.

(Subscription) I, Thasos daughter of Petheus son of Pasoknopaeus, with my guardian, my husband Petesuchus son of Petaus, acknowledge that I have received from Petheus son of Pnepheros one hundred silver drachmas [...] and twelve and one-sixth artabas of wheat, [which I] will repay in the month Pauni of the present 16th year, and I keep secure the fifth share of a house and courtyard belonging to her in the same village. Heron son of Satyrus [wrote] on her behalf, as she does not know letters.

Registered through the record office in Karanis.

Column i. Sheet. To Protarchus from Gaius Iulius Philius and from Lycarion son of Apollonius and Ptolemaeus son of Ptolemaeus, both Persians of the epigone, and Lycarion's wife Erotarion daughter of Achilles, Persian, with her husband as guardian. Concerning the points at issue, Lycarion and Ptolemaeus and Erotarion agree that they have received from Gaius Iulius Philius a loan through the money-changing bank of Castor of 300 drachmas of Ptolemaic silver without interest, which they will also repay within 10 months from the first of Pachon of the present [17th year] of Caesar, paying each day from the same first of the month Pachon one drachma, skipping no day; and they will do this without any delay, or else, on whatever day they skip, they shall immediately be liable to seizure and be held under arrest until they have paid, without waiting for the time apportioned to them, the whole principal or what will remain owing, plus half as much again, and for the time exceeding (the term) the two-drachma interest according to the ordinance, the right of execution belonging to Gaius Iulius Philius both from the three, who are mutual sureties for payment, and from one, and from whichever of them he chooses, and from all their property, as if by a legal judgment, and further also from the woodselling workshop belonging to Lycarion, which is near the Syrion in the property of Dorion; and until they have paid off (the debt) they shall keep it unalienated and unencumbered, and if some risk should

Column ii. Sheet. befall it, even so the loan shall be free of all risk; and they shall not take refuge in safeguards, nor in a sacred share (?), nor in a suppliant's petition, nor in a decree of benefactions or of labour, nor at a place of asylum, nor in private help, nor in any other protection whatsoever, or whatever they resort to shall be invalid. And Gaius Iulius Philius for his part agrees that he will invalidate the two loan agreements, of 120 drachmas of silver each, which the same debtors made with him through the same court, because he has been paid in full by them the 240 drachmas of silver in all, in cash, and that he will not proceed against them concerning these, but only concerning the three hundred drachmas under this agreement.

Year 17 of Caesar, Pharmouthi 7.

Year six of Imperator Caesar Nerva Trajan Augustus Germanicus Dacicus, month Xanthicus = Mecheir, at Hermopolis in the Thebaid. Areius son of Sarapion grandson of Hermaeus alias Areius, his mother being Tanemis, of Hermopolis, a minor registered in the quarter Phrourion East, aged about 6, honey-coloured, with as guardian his own father Sarapion son of Hermaeus alias Areius, aged about 46, of medium height, long-faced, straight-nosed, scar in the middle of the forehead, has lent further to Dioscorus alias Hermaeus son of Harpaesion grandson of Theon, his mother being Artemisia alias Taumesis daughter of Epimachus, of Hermopolis, registered in the quarter City West, Persian of the epigone, aged about 30, of medium height, honey-coloured, long-faced, straight-nosed, scar on the left shin, another five hundred drachmas of silver of imperial coinage, as capital, which he has received from him through the bank of Eudaemon, at interest of one drachma per mina per month from Phamenoth of the present year until the repayment set out below, five months, the interest amounting to twenty-five drachmas; all on the security which he previously mortgaged to him under other loan contracts through the agoranomeion in Hermopolis, one on the epagomenal days of the past fifth year of Imperator Caesar Nerva Trajan Augustus Germanicus Dacicus, the other in the month Tybi of the present year, for the debts owed under each of them, namely five and a half arouras of his maternal land, of the land around the court (peri aulen), in Upper Patemit near Mennis, from the allotment of Philon son of Onarasis, within their existing boundaries, and (now also for) this present loan, the five hundred and twenty-five drachmas of capital and interest together. English translation:
Choiak 11. Debt.

In the second year of Imperator Caesar Nerva Traianus Augustus Germanicus, Choiak 11, at Tebtunis in the Polemon division of the Arsinoite nome. Petesuchus son of Onnophris, of those from Talei, Persian of the epigone, aged about forty-five, with a scar on the little finger of the left hand, acknowledges to Zoilus son of Harmiusis, aged about forty-eight, with a scar on the right forearm, that he has received from him, Zoilus, from hand to hand out of the house a loan of one and one-sixth artabas of new, pure, unadulterated wheat and eight silver drachmas and one-third artaba of lentils, by the six-choenix measure of Talei; and the acknowledging party is obliged to repay to Zoilus all the aforesaid in the month Payni of the present second year, without any delay or evasion, Zoilus having the right of execution upon the acknowledging party and upon all his property. Subscriber: Lysimachus son of Cronion, aged about 58, with a scar on the little finger of the left hand.

I, Petesuchus son of Onnophris, of those from Talei, acknowledge that I have received from Zoilus son of Harmiusis a loan of one and one-sixth artabas of wheat by the six-choenix measure of Theogonis and eight silver drachmas and one-third artaba of lentils, which I shall also repay in the month Payni of the present second year, as stated above. Lysimachus son of Cronion wrote for him as he does not know letters. I, Zoilus son of Harmiusis: the agreement has been made with me as stated above.

Registered through the record-office in Tebtunis.

Year six of Imperator Caesar Nerva Trajan Augustus Germanicus Dacicus, month Xanthicus = Mecheir, at Hermopolis in the Thebaid. Areius son of Sarapion grandson of Hermaeus alias Areius, his mother being Tanemis, of Hermopolis, a minor registered in the quarter Phrourion East, aged about 6, honey-coloured, with as guardian his own father Sarapion son of Hermaeus alias Areius, aged about 46, of medium height, long-faced, straight-nosed, scar in the middle of the forehead, has lent further to Dioscorus alias Hermaeus son of Harpaesion grandson of Theon, his mother being Artemisia alias Taumesis daughter of Epimachus, of Hermopolis, registered in the quarter City West, Persian of the epigone, aged about 30, of medium height, honey-coloured, long-faced, straight-nosed, scar on the left shin, another five hundred drachmas of silver of imperial coinage, as capital, which he has received from him through the bank of Eudaemon, at interest of one drachma per mina per month from Phamenoth of the present year until the repayment set out below, five months, the interest amounting to twenty-five drachmas; all on the security which he previously mortgaged to him under other loan contracts through the agoranomeion in Hermopolis, one on the epagomenal days of the past fifth year of Imperator Caesar Nerva Trajan Augustus Germanicus Dacicus, the other in the month Tybi of the present year, for the debts owed under each of them, namely five and a half arouras of his maternal land, of the land around the court (peri aulen), in Upper Patemit near Mennis, from the allotment of Philon son of Onarasis, within their existing boundaries, and (now also for) this present loan, the five hundred and twenty-five drachmas of capital and interest together. Let Dioscorus repay to the lender or his successors on the thirtieth of Epeiph of the present sixth year in approved, current, acceptable silver. If he does not repay, as soon as the due date arrives, let the lender or his successors be permitted, without requiring renewal or a notice (diastolikon) or anything else at all, after paying the dues owed for the enkyklion tax, to make foreclosure (epikatabole) on the mortgaged five and a half [arouras], and let the lender and his successors possess them with full ownership in place of what is owed, and enter upon [them and take their produce and] lease them out [and carry off what] accrues [from them] annually [...] all, and use [and] manage them in whatever [way] they choose [for all time], no [claim] or pretext being left [hereafter to the borrower or] to others on his behalf [concerning these]. [If] they do not repay within the term, they shall pay to Aurelius on the drachmas the accruing interest of one drachma, and for the barley the highest price that it shall fetch at the time, and on demand Aurelius Demetrius shall have the right of execution upon the acknowledging parties and upon whichever of them he chooses and upon all their property, as if by legal decision. Concerning these things having been thus rightly [and duly] done, the aforementioned parties, having been asked by one another, have agreed.

We, Plution and Apianus, both sons of Heron, and Aphrodisius son of Sarapion, from the quarter of Apollonius Hierakeion, have received [from Demetrius] son of Nilus two hundred and forty drachmas of silver [and four artabas of barley] and will repay at the term, as aforesaid. Choiak 11. Debt.

In the second year of Imperator Caesar Nerva Traianus Augustus Germanicus, Choiak 11, at Tebtunis in the Polemon division of the Arsinoite nome. Petesuchus son of Onnophris, of those from Talei, Persian of the epigone, aged about forty-five, with a scar on the little finger of the left hand, acknowledges to Zoilus son of Harmiusis, aged about forty-eight, with a scar on the right forearm, that he has received from him, Zoilus, from hand to hand out of the house a loan of one and one-sixth artabas of new, pure, unadulterated wheat and eight silver drachmas and one-third artaba of lentils, by the six-choenix measure of Talei; and the acknowledging party is obliged to repay to Zoilus all the aforesaid in the month Payni of the present second year, without any delay or evasion, Zoilus having the right of execution upon the acknowledging party and upon all his property. Subscriber: Lysimachus son of Cronion, aged about 58, with a scar on the little finger of the left hand.

I, Petesuchus son of Onnophris, of those from Talei, acknowledge that I have received from Zoilus son of Harmiusis a loan of one and one-sixth artabas of wheat by the six-choenix measure of Theogonis and eight silver drachmas and one-third artaba of lentils, which I shall also repay in the month Payni of the present second year, as stated above. Lysimachus son of Cronion wrote for him as he does not know letters. I, Zoilus son of Harmiusis: the agreement has been made with me as stated above.

To Protarchus, from Apollonia daughter of Dionysius, with her guardian Demetrius son of Horion, of the deme Althaieus, and from Taphasies daughter of Sarapion, of Rhakotis, with her guardian, the son of her sister, Nitoitis son of Hermias, grandson of Psammetichus. Year 17 of Caesar, Pharmouthi 8.

Whereas by the four synchoreseis completed through the court by Ammonius and also by Alexander's deceased brother Theodorus son of Nicodemus it is shown, by the first, made in Thoth of the 15th year of Caesar, that Ammonius, for the 500 drachmas which he lent to Theodorus under a memorandum-contract and by a bank order through the bank of Marion and Theogenes, and for interest, had been assigned through the collectors (praktores) Theodorus' property in the Aurinites district of the territory of the Alexandrians near the village of the Syrians, in field 6, with the landmark of Paideros and Abrytanes: dry land that has been flooded, of 9 1/4 1/16 1/32 arouras held in common, the half share remaining to him; and that the same Ammonius had received from Theodorus, of the 500 drachmas of silver, 200 drachmas, and had been paid in full the interest on the 500 drachmas up to the stated time; and further had received ⟦the same Ammonius from Theodorus⟧, on account of the assignment of the property of Aristion which he had ceded to him, [...] drachmas of silver; and by the second, made in Phaophi of the same year, it is shown both the aforesaid and that, since 300 drachmas of the 500 drachmas of silver remained owing by Theodorus, he borrowed in addition from Ammonius through the same bank another 500 drachmas of silver, so that Theodorus owed 800 drachmas, for which he also submitted to Ammonius in the same synchoresis a synchoresis of loan; and by the third, made in Hathyr of the 16th year of Caesar, it is shown that the earlier synchoreseis were referred to, and that Theodorus borrowed in addition from Ammonius through the same bank of Marion and Theogenes, in Hathyr [200 drachmas, and] in Pachon another 200 drachmas, so that within [27 months] the total came to 1,200 drachmas of silver, which also [...] paid out [... the aforesaid synchoreseis] to Theodorus [...] synchoresis; and by the fourth [synchoresis, made] in Payni of the same 16th year of Caesar [...] [...]

(Fragment) [...] the guarantee of the aforesaid assignment to Ammonius through the synchoresis made through the collectors not being (valid) [...].

To Lucius Iulius [...], from Apollonius [son of ...], of those from Oxyrhynchus [city] in the Oxyrhynchite [nome]. I borrowed, together with Theon son of Hasychis, from Theon's brother Harsiesis 200 drachmas of silver, the yearly interest on which I paid to Harsiesis and his wife Teteuris. But now Harsiesis, having cast an envious eye on the share of a house belonging to me, of which he is my partner, has dared to execute against it documents of distraint, wishing to take possession of a share of a house worth not less than 2,000 drachmas of silver in return for the two hundred drachmas of the loan, of which half falls to Theon. [Moreover], although the strategus of the nome, on the petition I made, forbade Harsiesis to take any action, he has disregarded the order, being a violent man. Therefore I ask you, my lord, if it seems good, to write to the strategus of the nome to send up to you Theon and Harsiesis and Teteuris, who received the interest, so that I may obtain justice from you and be benefited. Farewell.

I lent to Harpagathes son of Panephremmis, of the same village, under a contract of loan, 325 drachmas of silver at the agreed interest, Harpagathes having agreed under the contract of the loan not to touch the [...] given [to him] from the temple, which are pledged, and the benefactions of the distribution, unless he first [repays me] the loan and the interest. (Recto) In the twelfth year of Tiberius Caesar Augustus, on the twenty-sixth of the month Panemos, Pachon 26, at Tebtunis in the division of Polemon of the Arsinoite nome. Chaeremon son of Horus, about twenty-nine years old, with a scar on the forehead on the left, and Herodes son of Herodes, about forty-five years old, with a scar on the right forearm, and Patynis son of Marepsemis, about thirty years old, with a scar below the left eyebrow, acknowledge to Papnebtynis son of Petesis, Persian of the epigone, about forty-five years old, with a scar on the right shin, that they have given him a partnership for the fourth part of the catoecic kleros of forty arouras, or as many as there may be, near the village, which they hold on lease from Chaeremon son of Penkius, for four years from the current twelfth year of Tiberius Caesar Augustus, the rent fixed by the lease each year, including the seed which Chaeremon will supply, thirty-five artabas of seed-wheat and five artabas of barley, being in all one hundred and ninety-seven and a half artabas of wheat and fifty artabas of barley, and two artabas of bread as a gift, and a bonus of 5 drachmas of silver; and that he himself will take care of what he owes by a loan of twenty-three artabas of wheat, and shall without fail comply with the terms of the lease, and it shall not be permitted to him to abandon the partnership. Signatory for Papnebtynis: Eutychus son of Maron, about 60 years old, with a scar on the chin on the left. We, Chaeremon son of Horus and Herodes son of Herodes and Patynis son of Marepsemis, acknowledge that we have granted the partnership as stated above. I, Herodes, have written for them. Chaeremon son of Horus ordered (me) to write. I, Papnebtynis son of Petesis: it has been made with me as stated above, and the rest accordingly. Eutychus son of Maron wrote for him because he does not know letters. A copy of the partnership has been filed. Year 12 of Tiberius Caesar Augustus, Pachon 26.

Year seven of Tiberius Claudius Caesar Augustus Germanicus Imperator, month Phamenoth 4, at Soknopaiou Nesos of the Herakleides division of the Arsinoite nome. Stotoetis son of Horus, aged about forty-six, with a scar on the right wrist, has lent to Soueris daughter of Satabous, Persian woman, aged about twenty-eight, with a scar on the left shin, with her guardian, her husband Onnophris son of Harpagathes, aged about forty-two, with a scar in the middle of the forehead, and to Aunes son of Onnophris, Persian of the descent, the two being mutual sureties for payment, a capital of eighty-four drachmas of coined silver, which they have also received from him on the spot, from hand, out of his house, at interest at the rate of one drachma each month; which the borrowers shall also repay, as aforesaid, [...] of the capital and the interest to Stotoetis in the month Mecheir of the coming ninth year of Tiberius Claudius Caesar Augustus Germanicus Imperator. English translation:
To Tiberius Claudius Cronius, exegetes of the city of the Alexandrians, from Demetrius son of Aristomenes, of the Hermopolite nome above Memphis. It happens that I, together with my paternal uncles Dionysius and Demetrius the elder, both sons of Demetrius, on behalf of ourselves and of Philotera daughter of Dionysius, had a case decided by his excellency the prefect Gaius Caecina Tuscus in the 12th year of the deified Claudius Caesar Augustus Germanicus Imperator, when he was iuridicus, against our creditor Musaeus son of Hermophilus, gymnasiarch, concerning an accounting of the mortgage of eighty-three and a quarter arouras which he holds from us, and concerning the excess rents which he took from them beyond double the capital, apart from the other rents of 5,000 drachmas which had been placed under embargo. He decided that we should repay the capital and recover the mortgage, and that Musaeus should be released from the rents which he had already received. But when, in accordance with his minutes, we approached Musaeus (asking him) to give us a part of the mortgage for sale, so that the capital might be repaid to him, since we have no resources other than the mortgage, he did not consent, having become covetous of it because of the great quantity of its yearly produce, the rent being ten artabas of wheat a year; moreover he also seized the rents of the 10th and 11th years which were lying with the cultivators under embargo in accordance with a letter of Tuscus himself, and up to now he enjoys the produce of the same mortgage, from which he has taken to the amount of 5 talents of silver in place of a capital of 4,800 drachmas. Robbed therefore in every way by this man, against whom we made very many petitions and presentations of reports, and of which he took no account, since he overpowers us in the locality, (and) having served on him and his sons Hermophilus and Castor a summons to come down to the assize, (and) the sons, disregarding it, did not appear: for these reasons we ask you to decide about all these matters, so that we may obtain our rights from you and be benefited.
Hermopolites Demetrius son of Aristomenes and Philotera daughter of Dionysius, for whom her husband Eudemus son of Metocus was appointed (representative), against Musaeus son of Hermophilus, creditor, and his sons Hermophilus and Castor, concerning the recovery of the mortgage of 83 1/4 arouras and of their produce exceeding the capital, 5 talents.

English translation:
Horus to his most esteemed Apion, greeting. To Lampon the mouse-catcher I gave on your account an earnest of 8 drachmas, so that he may catch mice at Toka. Please send them to me. I have also lent 8 drachmas to Dionysius, the chief man of Nemerai, and he has not sent them back, so that you may know. Farewell. Payni 24.

[...] ... having spent [...] (Heron) agreed that Zenarion would repay after five years to Heron's mother Philumene daughter of Heron the [...] which Philumene lent to me and my mother Thaesis under a contract completed through the record office in Oxyrhynchus city in the ninth year of the deified Vespasian, Pharmuthi, two thousand drachmas of silver of capital, and their interest from the beginning until the repayment, and would keep me and my mother Thaesis free from trouble and from exaction in every way, or pay whatever we are made to pay or whatever damage we suffer on this account, with half as much again, in addition to the other terms which the security contains. Since Philumene is continually pressing me, I have been compelled to come forward, and I ask you to order a letter to be written to the collector of foreign debts of the Oxyrhynchite nome to serve Zenarion and Heron with a copy of this memorandum, so that they may keep us undisturbed and free from trouble in respect of the aforesaid debt and repay it, or know that, if I am made to pay anything for it, I shall have the right of execution against them and against whatever property of theirs I find in the locality, both grain-land and other (property). For I hold and will hold to the other claims which I have on my own account and which I have against them, and to all my rights, being prejudiced in nothing. For the completion of the transaction I have dispatched Heraclides son of Heraclides, aged about 30, as is proper. Year one of Imperator Caesar Domitianus Augustus, month Germanikeios 22.

English translation:
Year fifteen of Imperator Caesar Domitianus Augustus Germanicus, month Peritios 1 = Choiak 1, at Karanis of the Herakleides division of the Arsinoite nome. Marcus Sempronius Gemellus, soldier of the third legion Cyrenaica, century of Pomponius Severus, aged about forty, with a scar on the ankle of the left foot, acknowledges to Miccalus son of Ptolemaeus, aged about forty-five, with a scar in the middle of the forehead under the hair, that he has received from him on the spot, from hand, out of his house, one thousand two hundred and forty drachmas of silver and their interest, which Miccalus owed him under a loan contract completed through the grapheion in Alexandria in the thirteenth year of Imperator Caesar Domitianus Augustus Germanicus, Pharmuthi 9; and Marcus Sempronius Gemellus has handed it back to him for cancellation; and neither Marcus Sempronius Gemellus himself nor his representatives will proceed against Miccalus or his representatives, either concerning what he has received, as aforesaid, the one thousand two hundred and forty drachmas of silver, or concerning their interest, or concerning any other matter or debt or any transaction at all, written or unwritten, from past times up to the present day, in any way. The contract is to be valid everywhere, just as the terms agreed are valid.
(2nd hand) I, Marcus Sempronius Gemellus, soldier of the third legion Cyrenaica, century of Pomponius Severus, acknowledge that I have received from Miccalus son of Ptolemaeus the one thousand two hundred and forty drachmas of silver and the interest, which he owed me under a loan contract completed through the grapheion in Alexandria in the thirteenth year of Domitian the lord, in the month Pharmuthi, which I have also handed back for annulment and cancellation, and I will not proceed concerning any matter at all, written or unwritten, as aforesaid.
(3rd hand) I, Miccalus son of Ptolemaeus: the receipt has been made to me as aforesaid.
It has been registered through the grapheion in Karanis.

English translation:
Year thirteen of Imperator Caesar Domitianus Augustus Germanicus, Mecheir, at Oxyrhynchus city of the Thebaid. Lucia alias Thaisas daughter of Lucius, her mother being Sinthonis daughter of Theon, Persian woman, with her guardian, her second cousin Heras son of Heraclides son of Heraclides, his mother being Plutarche daughter of Sarapion, acknowledges to Sarapion alias Clarus son of Sarapion son of Heraclides, his mother being Clara daughter of Narcissus, all of Oxyrhynchus city, in the street, that she will keep Sarapion alias Clarus and his representatives free from trouble and from exaction in every way in respect of the surety which the same Sarapion alias Clarus has given to Heraclides son of Apollonius son of Chaeremon, his mother being Herais daughter of Didymus, of the same city, under an agreement through the same record office in the present month Mecheir, for the three thousand five hundred drachmas of silver of capital which the acknowledging party has borrowed from him under a loan contract through the same record office in the same month Mecheir, at interest of one drachma per mina per month from the same month, on the security of the following arouras belonging to her: near Seryphis, from the cleruchy of Demetrius son of Milesius, 3 1/2 arouras of catoecic and purchased land; and from the same cleruchy, of 12 arouras of catoecic and purchased land, after the 7 arouras which she mortgaged to Taaphynchis daughter of Thonion, the remaining 5 arouras; and from the (cleruchy) of Callias, a third share of 8 arouras of catoecic and purchased land, that is 2 2/3 arouras; and near the village of Syron, from the (cleruchy) of Heraclides with that of Alexander, 6 1/2 1/4 arouras of catoecic land; and from the (cleruchy) of Alexander and others, of catoecic and purchased land, 6 1/2 arouras; in all, of catoecic and purchased land assigned to the katoikia, 24 1/3 1/12 arouras; with a term of the thirtieth of Tybi of the fifteenth year of Imperator Caesar Domitianus Augustus Germanicus. If, when the term arrives, the acknowledging party does not repay to Heraclides the capital and the interest, and Sarapion alias Clarus is asked to pay on her behalf, Sarapion alias Clarus shall own the aforesaid 24 1/3 1/12 arouras for all time, as if a sale had been made to him, and shall carry off their produce and sell them to others and use them as he chooses, no claim being left to the acknowledging party or her representatives against Sarapion alias Clarus or his representatives or against the aforesaid arouras or any part of them or their produce in any way; and she must guarantee these to him and his representatives at all times against all claims with every guarantee, and free from all public charges and taxes up to the term and of the term itself. If the acknowledging party contravenes any of these terms, (the contravention) shall be invalid, and she shall pay in addition to Sarapion alias Clarus or his representatives, for each kind of contravention, the damages and a fine of one thousand drachmas of silver, and the same amount to the public treasury, and the terms agreed shall be nonetheless valid, Sarapion alias Clarus having the right of execution against the acknowledging party and the aforesaid arouras and all her other property. The agreement is valid.

Orsenuphis son of Patynis son of Mesoeris, aged about forty-five, with a scar on the right forearm, and Cronion son of Cheos son of Harmiusis, aged about fifty, with a scar on the little finger of the left hand, both Persians of the descent, mutual sureties for payment, acknowledge to Didymus son of Didymus son of Maron, aged about thirty-four, with a scar on the right shin, that they have received from Didymus himself as a loan twenty artabas of new, clean, unadulterated wheat and twenty artabas of new, clean, unadulterated barley, all by the private four-choinix measure of Didymus himself, and that the acknowledging parties Orsenuphis and Cronion must repay to Didymus the twenty artabas of wheat and twenty artabas of barley of the loan in the month Payni of the present fifteenth year of Trajan Caesar the lord, without any delay or evasion, Didymus having the right of execution against the acknowledging parties, against one (of them) and whichever he chooses, and against all their property. Subscriber: Marepsemis son of Pakebkis, aged about 53, with a scar on the nose on the left.
(2nd hand) We, Orsenuphis son of Patynis and Cronion son of Cheos, the two mutual sureties for payment, acknowledge that we have received from Didymus son of Didymus as a loan [twenty] artabas of new, clean, unadulterated wheat and twenty artabas of barley by the [four-choinix] private measure [of the same] Didymus, which we [will also repay] in the month Payni of the present [15th year], as aforesaid. (3rd hand) I, Didymus son of Didymus: the agreement has been made to me as aforesaid.
It has been entered through the grapheion of the village of Tebtunis.

English translation:
Year fifteen of Imperator Caesar Nerva Traianus Augustus Germanicus Dacicus, month Neos Sebastos 25, at Tebtunis of the Polemon division of the Arsinoite nome. Orsenuphis son of Patynis son of Mesoeris, aged about forty-five, with a scar on the right forearm, and Cronion son of Cheos son of Harmiusis, aged about fifty, with a scar on the little finger of the left hand, both Persians of the descent, mutual sureties for payment, acknowledge to Didymus son of Didymus son of Maron, aged about thirty-four, with a scar on the right shin, that they have received from Didymus himself as a loan twenty artabas of new, clean, unadulterated wheat and twenty artabas of new, clean, unadulterated barley, all by the private four-choinix measure of Didymus himself, and that the acknowledging parties Orsenuphis and Cronion must repay to Didymus the twenty artabas of wheat and twenty artabas of barley of the loan in the month Payni of the present fifteenth year of Trajan Caesar the lord, without any delay or evasion, Didymus having the right of execution against the acknowledging parties, against one (of them) and whichever he chooses, and against all their property. Subscriber: Marepsemis son of Pakebkis, aged about 53, with a scar on the nose on the left.
(2nd hand) We, Orsenuphis son of Patynis and Cronion son of Cheos, the two mutual sureties for payment, acknowledge that we have received from Didymus son of Didymus as a loan [twenty] artabas of new, clean, unadulterated wheat and twenty artabas of barley by the [four-choinix] private measure [of the same] Didymus, which we [will also repay] in the month Payni of the present [15th year], as aforesaid. [Pakeb]kis son of Psoiphis wrote on their behalf, as they do not know letters.
(3rd hand) I, Didymus son of Didymus: the agreement has been made to me as aforesaid.
It has been entered through the grapheion of the village of Tebtunis.

English translation:
Year nine of Imperator Caesar Traianus Hadrianus Augustus, Mecheir 27.

[Year nine of Imperator] Caesar Traianus Hadrianus Augustus, month Xandikos 27 = Mecheir 27, at Ptolemais Euergetis of the [Arsinoite nome]. [The following] dispositions were made, [being sane and in his right mind], by Ammonius son of Apion son of Theon, his mother being Isarous daughter of Horion, registered in the [...] quarter, aged about [...]. [...] May I, [while in good health], have power over my own property, selling, mortgaging, altering my dispositions and managing [my property as I choose]. [But if I die, ...] my children by [my ...] wife Aphroditous daughter of Nilus [...] in the metropolis in the quarter [of the Bithynians] Other Places a house and courtyard, near the village of Kerkesoucha [... five arouras and] one aroura of olive-orchard and half an aroura of palm-grove, in all six and a half arouras [or however many] they may be [...] and whatever property I leave and what shall come to me in any manner whatever. Further [...] and [to my wife] Aphroditous the furniture to be left by me, and equipment, household goods and clothing, and also the habitation, [for as long as she] lives [and remains unmarried], of the house and courtyard in the quarter of the Bithynians Other Places left by me to the children as stated above [...] my wife [...] guardian [...] of our minor children by one another until they come of age, she being not subject to a guardian and not liable to render account [...] in every way, but not alienating anything at all nor disposing of any of the belongings [...]. To the children [...] their mother Aphroditous shall hand over the property free of all public charges and of all expense [...]. [The] wife [shall perform] my funeral, burial and local rites, for which she shall spend four hundred silver drachmas, to the [priesthood]. The three thousand two hundred silver drachmas which I have [on deposit at the bank of Pappus], I wish to be laid out for a satisfactory purchase in the name of my children [...], my brother Theon alone overseeing everything that concerns the guardianship and the purchase. Among the debts owed (to me) there is also a loan of my mother Isarous of one thousand silver drachmas, made in trust in the name of my brother Theon. To no one else do I leave anything.

Theon son of Petermuthion, aged about thirty, scar on the left eyebrow; Mystharion son of Zoilus, aged about sixty-nine, without distinguishing mark; Epimachus alias Getas son of Demetrius, aged about twenty-five, scar on the first finger of the left hand; Didas son of Ptolemaeus, aged about thirty-eight, scar on the right cheek; Heron son of Harpocration, aged about [...]ty, scar between the eyebrows; Ptolemaeus son of Apollonius, aged about forty-five, scar on the first finger of the left hand: the six witnesses.

I, [Ammonius] son of Apion, have made the will, leaving to my children Apion and Aphroditous in equal shares all my property and the debts owed to me, and to my wife Aphroditous the household goods and clothing and habitation of the house and courtyard [...] children [...]; I have agreed to what is written above. The three thousand two hundred silver drachmas which I have on deposit at the bank of Pappus I wish to be laid out [...] for my children, my brother Theon overseeing the guardianship and the purchase, as stated above; and I shall seal with a seal-engraving of Sarapis. Among the debts owed to me there is also my mother's loan of one thousand drachmas, made in trust in the name of my brother Theon.

I, Theon son of Petermuthion, bear witness and shall seal with a seal-engraving of Mesthasythmis. I, Mystharion son of Zoilus, bear witness and shall seal with a seal-engraving of Hermes. I, Epimachus alias Getas son of Demetrius, bear witness and shall seal with a seal-engraving of Harpocrates. I, Didas son of Ptolemaeus, bear witness and shall seal with a seal-engraving of Isis. I, Heron son of Harpocration, bear witness and shall seal with a seal-engraving of Ammon. I, Ptolemaeus son of Apollonius, bear witness and shall seal with a seal-engraving of Agathos Daimon. Lucius alias Hermias and the [...]. Year 9 of Imperator Caesar Traianus Hadrianus [Augustus, Mech]eir 27 [...] the aforementioned will [...].

English translation:
[...] of the city of Oxyrhynchus. [Since] Theon son of Pausiris, [of] the same city of Oxyrhynchus, has served on me through [the] strategus of the nome a copy of a memorandum which he wrongfully executed at the record office, by which he made a demand for capital sums of money which he alleged were owed to him by the maternal grandfather of my minor son Sarapion, Sarapion, and by his brother Dionysius, from times long past, I make the necessary counter-statement, declaring that I suspect that the security of the loan which he claims was made has become void, both because of the length of time and because Sarapion lived on for two years and after his death his daughter Eubulia, who became my wife and the mother of the minor Sarapion, likewise lived on for eleven years, and after her death too another five years elapsed, and Theon did not dare to come forward; and further that Eubulia, while she was alive, sold to the aforementioned brother of Sarapion, Dionysius, property of Sarapion for six talents of silver, and in addition on condition that he should pay to Sarapion's lenders what was owed by him, and that Theon, being Sarapion's lender of other capital sums, received those from Dionysius but made no mention at all of this one. I therefore ask you to give orders to write to the strategus of the Oxyrhynchite nome to serve on Theon a copy of this memorandum, so that he may know that the notice which he wrongfully served on me is void, together with whatever he may add in counter-pleas, the trial against him remaining open to me on the points where it is needed, as I rest content with this declaration, as is proper. Year 15 of Imperator Caesar Traianus Hadrianus Augustus, Epeiph 1. Signed by me, Epeiph 1.

English translation:
To Iulius Varianus, epistrategus of the Seven Nomes and the Arsinoite, from Dionysia daughter of Chaeremon, her mother being Hermione daughter of Chaeremon, of the metropolis of the Oxyrhynchite nome. A dispute having arisen between me and a certain Sarapion son of Mnesitheus, who, with regard to a vineyard estate and corn-land which I bought from his father as long ago as year 11 of Hadrian Caesar the lord, having paid both to the father himself and to a certain creditor (lender) of his the agreed price and having received the proper public deed of the sale, claimed that I held them in trust (as security), Claudius Quintianus, the former epistrategus, having heard the case, referred it to his excellency the prefect. And I since then have been attending the prefect's tribunal, and as my opponent paid no attention and did not appear, I submitted to his excellency the prefect a petition, a copy of which I have appended, setting out the state of the matter, and he sent me on to you, my lord, for judgement. Since, then, my opponent is not present even now, and the sowing is pressing and the care of what has been swept away by the river requires my presence, I ask you, if you think fit, to allow me to sail back and to be judged by you on the spot, so that I may obtain redress. Farewell.

The copy of the petition which I submitted to his excellency the prefect is as follows: To Titus Flavius Titianus, his excellency the prefect, from Dionysia daughter of Chaeremon, her mother being Hermione, of the city of Oxyrhynchus. A certain Sarapion son of Mnesitheus, of the same city, before Claudius Quintianus, the former epistrategus of the Seven Nomes, accusing my mother Hermione of poisoning, also made up a story about certain property, as if he had been defrauded of what I, Dionysia, bought by public deeds, having paid the price of it to his father while he was alive and to the creditors (lenders) of the same father, by whom the said properties were held in mortgage, alleging that it had been registered in trust; and when the epistrategus referred the whole matter to you, the benefactor, it happened that my mother died before the trial, and I since then, ordered by the letter of the epistrategus to sail down here together with Sarapion, came here, while Sarapion paid no attention so as to sail down. Since, then, while I am staying here, it has been reported to me that all my property, both farm-buildings [and land] and dykes, has been lost through the excessive rise of the most sacred Nile, I beg you, lord prefect, as my opponent [is not present even now], to allow me to sail back so that I may [obtain] my rights and not perish of hunger together with my property, [so that I may obtain redress]. Farewell. Year 16 of Hadrian Caesar, Phaophi 12.

[If the matter is as] it stands, apply to the epistrategus. Deliver.

Year 15 of Imperator Caesar Traianus Hadrianus Augustus, Pachon 21, in the camp of Syene of the Thebaid. Mutual agreement between Asclepias daughter of Dadas, with her guardian Pindarus son of Harsynius, heiress of her husband [...]us Valens, deceased cavalryman of the cohort II of Thracians, of the turma of Kartilianus, and Aemilius [...], cavalryman of the same cohort, absent, through his agent Iulius Apollinarius, cavalryman, armicustos of the ala Gallica, and Cassianus Gemellus, curator of the turma of Kartilianus, lenders of the same Valens, having agreed among themselves that, from all the camp property of Valens that is found, collected together and sold, after deduction from it of (what is due to) the batman (focarius) and the legacy of Pamonius the procurator and what Asclepias advanced, and apart from one hundred and forty-four drachmas, each shall receive from what remains: Asclepias one share on account of the inheritance and of the funeral of Valens' body, Aemilius two shares for what is owed to him, and Cassianus the remaining fourth share, also for what is owed to him. The loan contracts, crossed out, shall be given back to Asclepias. Written in triplicate, and [each has received] one.

I, Asclepias daughter of Dadas, have agreed [to the above and have received] one share of the inheritance and shall [...].

English translation:
To Maximus alias Nearchus, strategus of the Arsinoite nome, Heraclides division, from Stotoetis son of Stotoetis, from the village of Soknopaiou Nesos. My aforementioned father Stotoetis, while he was alive, lent to Stotoetis and Pekysis, both sons of Pakysis, under a cheirographon made in the 18th year of the deified Hadrian, in the month Epeiph, one thousand five hundred drachmas of silver. Since I have been occupied with demanding these back, because they have paid neither interest nor anything of the capital, and because one of the two debtors, Stotoetis, has died and Pekysis despises my youth, I have taken refuge with you and ask, if it seems good to you, that you summon Pekysis, so that with your help I may be able to recover what is mine and to live on it, since I am also a camel-keeper.

Year 9 of Imperator Caesar Titus Aelius Hadrianus Antoninus Augustus Pius, Pachon 8.

English translation:
Column i: His excellency the dioiketes Iulianus, administering the office of iuridicus, wished you to become mediator and judge for us concerning the matters we have against our opponents. Our case was this: my father Iulius Agrippianus became lender to the husband of the present opponent Drusilla, the father of this [...]dentius Philippus and of his minor brother, as long ago as year 13 of the deified Hadrian; and as he was not recovering what was owed, he had recourse, while (the debtor) was still alive, to the legal remedies, the intermediary surety (mesengyos) objecting. When he in turn died, his wife Drusilla, the opponent, acting as representative of his children, Philippus the opponent and the one then a minor, not yet of age, disputed with my father before Asclepiades, the former [...], claiming a dowry [...] owed to herself by Apollinarius, and assisting the minors and alleging that they were their father's heirs, and blaming the guardians of their orphanhood appointed by their father by will, Gemellus and Sempronius [...], for having neglected the interests of the minors. And Asclepiades wished the guardians to be present, and my father not to [manage] anything regarding the property. [Deleted lines.]

Column ii: [... Anthestius(?)] Gemellus, Drusilla petitioned Iulius Maximianus, the former iuridicus, and he wrote a letter to Cerealis, former strategus of the division of Heraclides of the Arsinoite nome, to take the minutes, examine them, and send up the persons concerned. And after this the same Maximianus, a hearing likewise being held before him for Drusilla against Gemellus and Sabinus and against my father, and Drusilla blaming the guardians, Maximianus declared as follows: "I shall write to the strategus of the nome so that two guardians are appointed for the children. If any [...] the cases [...] of the deceased and [...] in the time after he died, (they are) to be referred to your risk and you are liable for the loss. The same guardians shall plead also against the lender [...] the other matters, both against the guardians and against the lender, I shall hold over, so that your [...] until it is examined up to a preliminary judgement; likewise [...] what the lender appears to have managed shall remain, so that, if he is shown to be a lender, his legal rights remain to him, but if he is not shown to be one and has received anything improperly by his management, he shall pay it back twofold. The same guardians shall plead also against the woman concerning the dowry. They shall be appointed within 20 days by the strategus of the nome, and after the appointment they shall complete the lawsuits within 5 days." Iulius Gemellus and Longinus Apollinarius having then been appointed by the strategus of the nome, a hearing was also held before Maximianus in their presence, and in accordance with his minutes it was decided that the strategus of the nome should examine the whole means of the debtor and in what items the debts consist, and report to him. The strategus having heard (the case) and having given accountants whom they chose, Alcimus for Drusilla, former gymnasiarch of the city of the Arsinoites, and Ptolemaeus for my father, likewise former gymnasiarch, my father accordingly delivered to the accountants, through a local assistant, the accounts of the capital sums and interest owed to him and of the revenues he had received. But Drusilla and the guardians, knowing that the accounting was of no use to them, kept obstructing the accountants until my father died; and as I was still young and ignorant of my father's affairs, she disputed with me before the strategus of the nome, who, having learned what had been decided, sent us back to the same accountants and ordered the produce of one year to be turned into money until the completion of the accounting. When the produce had been turned into money, it was deposited; and as the opponent Drusilla was obstructing the accounting, likewise the revenues of the following years were deposited, while I was in military service. My mother [Herais(?)] [...] of Drusilla [...] before Herodes the [appointed] judges [...] the receipt of the produce, and in accordance [...] all your [...] Phamenoth, minutes [...]. Maximianus, who wrote the letter about the produce, declared as follows, discussing [...] about the matter, and after that Celer, strategus [...], then also [Neokydes], the most excellent iuridicus, [...] judged about the produce: "Drusilla can petition the strategus of the nome about this [...]. The accounting shall be completed at once in accordance with what has been judged, and Apollinarius, the strategus of the nome, shall see to it that the accounting takes place within 30 days, assigning an assistant for this, so that it is not protracted any further." After this, a hearing having been held for us before Sentius Maximus, chiliarch in charge of the [...],

English translation:
To Publius Marcius Crispus, vir egregius, epistrategus, from Ptolemaeus son of Diodorus alias Dioscorus, of those from the Arsinoite nome. The most shameful of all wrongs in life is that free men should be beaten and insulted, and above all by cheap slaves or by hired men. This is worse than incurable insolence. Often, then, lord, wishing to obtain justice, we are at a loss because justice here is far away. Among these is Ptolemaeus, son of a certain Pappus, former gymnasiarch, from the same Arsinoite nome, self-willed in his ways and violent, living the life of a moneylender and doing unholy things, demanding, contrary to what is forbidden, interest at a stater (per mina per month) through the power he has in the nome, disregarding the decisions of the prefects and the commands of the Emperors; among those (wronged) he has done the same to me too, and he exacts interest at a stater, descending on the villages with a crowd and inflicting very many insults on the people. Often, then, having done the same to me, lord, I have suffered unreasonable insults from him; if we wish to petition the strategus about his violence, he drags his associates along to the strategus' office and they sit in council with the judge. As a result we do not obtain justice. I shall prove that in one village he lent three and a half talents, taking interest at a stater bit by bit, so that it amounts each year to half as much again; and you will find that he has received from some people eight times the capital in a few years, whereas it is forbidden for anyone to exact interest greater than the equal of the capital over the whole period. Since such men ought to meet with correction, I have taken refuge with you, the benefactor of all, so that in the most gracious times of our lord Antoninus ⟨I may be able⟩ to remain in my own home, ⟨and⟩ that you order it to be written to the strategus of the Heraclides (division) that I be kept unharmed and uninsulted by Ptolemaeus, and that ⟨what⟩ I have paid as interest in excess of the drachma rate be credited to me against the capital; and if after this I appear to owe him anything, I shall be able to repay him fairly; and, for proof of the aforesaid, that the strategus order a certain Aphrodisius and Zoilus, who are paid by him, to be brought before him together with those innocent of the exaction of the interest, taking sufficient security from them for your inquiry; and from this his violence in action will become evident, so that I may be helped by you. Farewell.

Year 11, Phaophi 21.

Petition the strategus. Deliver.
