English translation:
Registered in year 6, Mecheir 29; 5 (copies) were issued, one to each.

In the sixth year of Emperor Caesar Lucius Septimius Severus Pius Pertinax Augustus Arabicus Adiabenicus and of Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Caesar Augustus, emperor designate, in the month Xandikos, Mecheir 29, at Ptolemais Euergetis in the Arsinoite nome. Tyrannis daughter of Sarapion, former exegetes of the city of the Arsinoites, about twenty-eight years old, without a scar, with as guardian, whom she has chosen of her own will through Serenus alias Harpocration, priest, exegetes, according to the instruction sent by him, under which also stands the application submitted by her (copies of all of which are appended), Cronion son of Heron son of Zosimus, from the quarter of the Treasuries, about fifty years old, with a white spot on the left eye, acknowledges to Turbon son of Harpocration son of Heraclides, from the metropolis, about fifty-five years old, with a bent little finger of the left hand, and to Melanous daughter of Harpocration son of Chaeremon, from the Syrian quarter, about nineteen years old, without distinguishing mark, and to Taopis daughter of Heron son of Paopis, about forty years old, without distinguishing mark, and to Polion son of Heracles son of Sarapas, about forty years old, without distinguishing mark, and to Heraclia, about twenty years old, without distinguishing mark, and Serenus, about thirty years old, without distinguishing mark, both children of Saturnilus son of Tyrannus, the four from the village of Tebtunis of the division of Polemon, the women each with a guardian, Taopis with Pansylas son of Cronion son of Zoilus, about fifty years old, without distinguishing mark, Heraclia with her aforementioned brother Serenus, and Melanous with Cronion son of Heron son of Heron, about thirty-five years old, without distinguishing mark, that she, Tyrannis, the acknowledging party, has received from them by hand one thousand and forty drachmas of silver, equal to what was owed by Turbon's father Harpocration son of Heraclides, and by Saturnilus son of Tyrannus, father of both Heraclia and Serenus, and by Heron son of Paopis, father of Taopis, and by Sarapas, paternal grandfather of Polion, and by Poueris son of Paopis, maternal grandfather of Melanous, together with Orsenuphis, of unknown father, his mother being Taorsenuphis, and Protas son of Amaeis and Hartes son of Sarapas and Apynchis son of Orsenuphis, to Tyrannis' late father Sarapion, former exegetes, according to an agreement made in the thirteenth year of the deified Aelius Antoninus, in the month Mesore, on the eighth, through the record office of the village of Euhemeria of the division of Themistes, which she has also handed back to them for annulment and cancellation; and that she has further received from them by hand for interest, in place of more, the equal of the aforesaid capital, one thousand and forty drachmas, making together two thousand and eighty drachmas of silver, which are being paid into the public (bank) for the price of wheat of the supervision of the abundance (euthenia) in the seventeenth year of the deified Aelius Antoninus, which was supervised by Tyrannus alias Diogenes, former cosmetes, father of the acknowledging party's husband Ptolemaeus; and that neither Tyrannis herself, the acknowledging party, nor her successors shall proceed against Turbon and the others, nor against either of them, nor against their successors, nor against those who borrowed together with the persons whose heirs they are, Orsenuphis and the others, since Turbon and the others have paid their share from their own means, nor concerning any other matter whatever, on the basis of any right or document or other contract, written or unwritten, from past times up to the present day, in any way; and that Tyrannis will repel at her own expense anyone who proceeds against them, the fee fixed for the instruction having been paid.

The copies are, of the instruction: Serenus alias Harpocration, priest, exegetes and chief prytanis and in charge of the distributions of seed and of the abundance, to the officials of the record offices, greeting. A copy of the petition submitted to me in the name of Tyrannis is sent to you through Demetrius, assistant of the office, so that, if nothing at all stands in the way, you may draw up the document with her for the transaction set out below, Cronion son of Heron being registered as her guardian as she requested. Take care of this as is proper. I pray for your health. Year 6 of Lucius Septimius Severus Pius Pertinax Augustus and of Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Caesar Augustus, emperor designate, Mecheir 27.

And of the application: To Serenus alias Harpocration, priest, exegetes, from Tyrannis daughter of Sarapion, former exegetes of the city of the Arsinoites, with as guardian, whom I choose of my own will through you, Cronion son of Heron son of Zosimus, from the quarter of the Treasuries. Receiving from Taopis daughter of Heron son of Paopis and from Polion son of Heracles son of Saras and Turbon son of Harpocration son of Heraclides and Heraclia and Serenus, both children of Saturnilus son of Tyrannus, and Melanous daughter of Harpocration son of Chaeremon, from the Syrian quarter, by hand one thousand and forty drachmas of silver, equal to what the persons whose heirs they are owed to my aforementioned father Sarapion, and in place of more the equal amount for interest, making together two thousand and eighty drachmas of silver, and issuing to them a receipt in full discharge, I am hindered by not having the guardian to be registered for me, because my husband Ptolemaeus who lives with me is abroad, and I have no father living, nor father's father, nor do I have a brother or son. Therefore, choosing the aforementioned Cronion through you, I submit (this) and ask you to instruct the officials of the record offices to draw up the document with me as I issue the receipt to them, so that I may have received your benevolence, the drachmas going to the public (bank) for the price of wheat of the supervision of the seventeenth year, which was supervised by Tyrannus alias Diogenes, father of my aforementioned husband Ptolemaeus, former cosmetes of the city of the Arsinoites, supervision of the abundance. I have read it. I, Demetrius, assistant of the prytanis and exegetes, have transferred it; the date is the same.

Subscriber for the acknowledging party and her guardian, who state that they do not know letters: Heraclides son of Ptolemaeus, about 45 years old, with a scar on the left shin. I, Tyrannis daughter of Sarapion, former exegetes, with as guardian, whom I have chosen of my own will according to the aforesaid instruction of the exegetes, Cronion son of Heron, acknowledge that I have received from Turbon and Melanous and Taopis and Polion and Heraclia and Serenus the one thousand and forty drachmas of the capital and the same amount for interest, making together two thousand and eighty drachmas, equal to what was owed with the others aforesaid in the aforesaid manner, and I make no claim concerning anything whatever, but I will repel at my own expense those who proceed against them, the drachmas being paid to the public (bank) on behalf of my aforementioned husband Ptolemaeus, as stated above. I, Heraclides son of Ptolemaeus, wrote for them, who are illiterate. We, Turbon and Melanous and Taopis and Polion and Heraclia and Serenus: the receipt has been made to us as stated above. English translation:
To Theon, strategus, from Serenus, freedman of Apollonianus son of Sarapion, of the city of Oxyrhynchus. Of the instrument which I obtained from the katalogeion the copy is as follows: Antoninus alias Pudens, priest and chief judge, to the strategus of the Oxyrhynchite nome, greeting. Let a copy of the memorandum submitted be served, as set out below. Farewell. Year 19 of the Aurelii Antoninus and Commodus, the lords Augusti, Phaophi 7. I, Sarapion [...], have signed. I, Hephaestion alias Sarapion, wrote.

To Antoninus alias Pudens, priest, chief judge and in charge of the chrematistae and the other courts, from Serenus, freedman of Apollonius son of Sarapion, of the city of Oxyrhynchus. I lent, by a public instrument written through the record office in the same city of Oxyrhynchus, in the past 18th year, in the month Sebastos, on the 11th, to Sarapias daughter of Podon son of Horus, her mother being Thaesis, from Psobthis, the metropolis of the Small Oasis, nine hundred drachmas of silver as capital, at interest of one drachma per mina per month, the capital (to be repaid) on the 30th of the month Kaisareios of the same past 18th year, it being stated that, if she did not repay within the term, there should remain with me and those who succeed me, in place of the capital and of whatever interest she did not repay, the possession and ownership of the slave Sarapias belonging to her, then about 25 years old, on the other terms which the loan contains and which the provisions written in it concerning flight and death of the slave, for my security, contain. Since the term has passed and repayment has not been made to me, I ask you to order that the strategus of the Oxyrhynchite nome be written to, to serve a copy of this on Sarapias if she is alive, or if not, on her heirs of full age, or if they are minors, on their legal guardians, whose names will be made known on the spot, so that they may know and make repayment to me, or know that I shall make use of the laws applying to entry into possession, as is proper. Year 19 of the Aurelii Antoninus and Commodus, the lords Augusti, Phaophi [.].

[...] strategus. This being so, I ask that service be made on Sarapias, as is proper. [Year 19 of the Emperors] Caesars Marcus Aurelius [Antoninus and Lucius] Aurelius Commodus Augusti [Armeniaci] Medici Parthici [Germanici Sarmatici] Maximi, Hathyr 19.

[I, Sarapias daughter of Podon], have received a copy of this [memorandum. Year 19 of the Aurelii] Antoninus and Commodus [the lords] Emperors, month [Hathyr ...]. I, [Mu]saeus alias Pausirion [son of ...], have been registered as her guardian in place of [...] through the strategus, and I wrote [for her] because she does not know letters.

I, Syrion, assistant, served the memorandum on Sarapias as is proper. [Year 19], month Hathyr [..].

(Column 1) To [...] alias Serenus, priest, archidikastes and in charge of the supervision of the chrematistai [and the other] courts, [from Aurelia Aretous] alias Herounous daughter of Heron, citizen. A copy is appended of the threefold security issued to my father Heron [son of Antonas, grandson of Paniscus], of the Archistrateian tribe and Althaean deme, with the [writings] after the term [and the] subscription beneath it:
Sarapous daughter of Pauseiris the elder, [her mother being ...], from the village of Moirai in the [upper] Koussite (toparchy), with as guardian her brother by the same [parents, from] the same village, to Heron son of Antonas, grandson of Paniscus, of the Archistrateian tribe and Althaean deme, [his mother being Are]tous alias Herounous, citizen, greetings. I acknowledge that I have received from you by [hand from the house as a loan (chresis)] a capital of one talent [and] two thousand silver drachmas, total 1 talent and 2,000 drachmas, which I will also [repay to you within ten months] from the present month Mesore of the current year 18 of Marcus Aurelius [Antoninus and Lucius] Aurelius Commodus, Caesars the lords, without delay; and for the [security of the aforesaid capital] I mortgage to you by this cheirographon the half [share] belonging to me of the catoecic arouras written below, 41 1/4 (?), that is 20 1/2 1/8 arouras (?), lying [in ...] [...] basins, [of which one ...] on the north [...] of the kleros of [Doro]theus near Lysimachis [...] neighbours of the whole joint holding: on the south [...] kleros, on the west unproductive land [...] of Paniscus [... on the east] and north public land, and [...] formerly of Tereus son of Psenanoupis [...] of Phibis and of the kleros of Artabazus, 2 1/2 [arouras], of which the neighbours: on the south [...] and from the [...] [... arouras], on the north the heirs of Dius son of Heras [...] of Achilles and [...], on the remaining [sides ..., and from the kleros of Gl]aucias 1/2 1/8 aroura, of which [the neighbours ...] and on the west the heirs [...], and from the kleros of Chrestus [...] arouras [...] canal, and from the kleros of Dositheus [... arouras ...] of Pauseiris [...], on the north [...] formerly of Posidonius [...] 1 aroura, of which the neighbours [...], of which the neighbours on the south [...] kleros, and from [... formerly] of Hermaeus son of Cassander, [...] of Fronto, on the east [...], and from the kleros of Callistratus [...] on the west the boundary of the heirs [... on the remaining sides] unproductive land, and from the kleros of Dorotheus, 10 arouras held in common, of which [the neighbours: on the south ...] of Herounous daughter of Paniscus, citizen, and others, on the north of Sarapion the elder, [...] kleros, on the west formerly of Nearchus son of Hermodorus and of Psenanubis, [... of the] aforesaid 41 1/4 arouras, and in the same area within the boundaries [...] the entire fourth share of a garden with all the trees in it [...] with a sowing capacity of one and a half and a quarter aroura, of which the neighbours on the south and east [...] ownerless plots, on the two remaining sides the boundary of the channel; and in place of the interest [for the period that has elapsed] at one drachma per mina each month, the [...] of the half share of the 41 1/4 arouras and of the fourth share of the garden [...] the usufruct and leasing and all revenue; or (you are) to have execution [against me and against the] mortgaged security and against all my other property [as if by legal judgment]; and henceforth I will keep the aforesaid security unalienated to others [and not mortgaged for another loan] until I repay or am made to pay the aforesaid money [within the]
(Column 2) fixed term, and I will guarantee it with every guarantee against public [and] private (claims) and against everything whatsoever. The mortgage is valid as if registered in a public archive; I have issued it to you in three copies, free from erasure, insertion and scratching-out. Year 18 of the Imperatores Caesares Marcus Aurelius Antoninus and Lucius Aurelius Commodus Augusti Armeniaci Medici Parthici Germanici Sarmatici Maximi, Mesore 15. I, Hermammon son of Sarapammon, wrote the body. I, Sarapous daughter of Pauseiris, have received the one talent and two thousand silver drachmas and will repay you, and I have mortgaged and will provide (the property) by way of usufruct (misthokarpeia) as aforesaid. I, Sarapion son of Pauseiris, am registered as guardian of my sister and wrote on her behalf, as she does not know letters.
This being so, and my father Aurelius Heron having died leaving as heirs, by the Roman will which he left in year 5 of the deified Severus Alexander, Mecheir, which was also lawfully opened in year 13 likewise in the month Mecheir, me his daughter for a share of one half, one third and one twelfth, and his adopted son Marcus Aurelius Serenus son of Isidorus for the remaining share of one twelfth; and having since then laid claim to my share of one half, one third and one twelfth of the usufruct of the aforesaid arouras and of the garden in place of the interest on the capital, according to the term stated above, I wish a single copy of the threefold security to be made public, paying to the city the 12 drachmas fixed for a single copy and the dues on the assessment, and I ask that you take it, subscribed by Aurelius Heron, appointed by me, (attesting) that the subscription beneath it is in the own hand of the guardian who wrote on behalf of Sarapous, her brother Sarapion, who signed as guardian, and register it together with this memorandum in the Hadrianic library, and the same memorandum also in that of Nanaeum, so that the rights from it may remain mine as from a public document, my claim remaining concerning the other sums which the same debtor Sarapous owes my father under a cheirographon of year 21 of the deified Commodus, Pharmouthi, of four thousand silver drachmas and an equal amount in lieu of greater interest, in which it was added that I shall not release the aforesaid usufruct unless she also pays what is due under the cheirographon. Those in charge of the diaologe of the city: through me, Aurelius Sarapammon, acting. Year 4 of Marcus Antonius Gordianus Caesar the lord, Choiak 28.

I, Paaus, of unknown father, my mother being Thermuthis, acknowledge that I have from Sisois the one thousand two hundred drachmas of silver of the loan, at interest of one drachma (per mina per month), which I will also repay in the month Mesore, as stated above. (2nd hand) I, Sisois son of Nilus: (the agreement) has been made with me as stated above.

To [Pomponius Faustian]us, prefect [of Egypt ...] [...] [...] [...] the proper [...] [...] summoned through [...] [...] ordered by you [...] [...] council, whether the fiscus [...] you, most illustrious prefect, [...] at the conventus [...] of our lord [...] [... of the most illustrious] Longaeus Rufus [...] ordered [...] of old produce [...] from the new crops [...] from those who handed them over [...] measurers and strategi [and royal scribes] who succeeded to the strategiai [...] adding [...] at the risk of all the [...] two harvests, and you, lord, [...] in the 26th year you order by your sacred letter to Damarion the strategus that an examination be made of this quantity and that he see to the exaction and learn whether the sitologi embezzled first or the archons and the measurers also embezzled with them; he, in accordance with his diligence, reported first to Longaeus Rufus that the embezzlement was by the measurers and archons, on the basis of deposits shown to him. [...] [...] buyers the resources of the sitologi [...] first, lord prefect, I take refuge [...] beseeching him that [...] the exaction ordered to be made by him from those very men who succeeded to their strategiai. A[urelius S]arapion to [Aurelius] Claudius, his father, [many] greetings. As I asked you face to face when you were present, for the days on which I am about to anoint, forty metretes of oil, which you also promised in accordance with the good disposition you have towards me: now therefore, since need pressed me, relying on you I obtained from friends as a loan the forty metretes, on condition of restoring them. Necessarily, therefore, if you still have oil with you, instruct either your son or whomever you wish to provide them to me quickly, so that I too may restore them to the friends who obliged me, the price being paid over by me at once to whomever you approve. But see that you do not neglect it, lest I seem to deceive the people. I pray for your health and prosperity.

Year twenty of Imperator Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Parthicus Maximus Britannicus Maximus Pius Augustus, month Panemos = Pharmouthi 4, through the bank of business documents of Anubion son of Ammonius, of the Matidian tribe and Kalliteknean deme, at Antinoopolis. Polis son of Castor, grandson of Dioscorus, his mother being Theus, from the hamlet of Chairephanes in the Hermopolite nome, (pays) to Eudaemon son of Ammonius, grandson of Ammonous, of the Sabinian tribe and Trophonian deme, aged about 49, with a scar on the left knee, (namely) that Eudaemon has received from Polis by this bank payment the two thousand and eighty drachmas of silver capital, (total) 2,080 silver drachmas, which he lent to him in the present year 20 on Phamenoth 9 at Memphis by payment through the bank of Bernikianus son of Methysion in the same Memphis; and Eudaemon declares that he has received from him the interest on them at one drachma (per mina per month) up to the present day, in instalments, by hand, all of it, in full discharge; and that neither Eudaemon nor his representatives nor others on his behalf have or will have any claim against Polis or his representatives concerning the aforesaid capital or its interest or anything else whatsoever, written or unwritten, up to the present day, because he has received everything in full; and [...] the aforesaid bank payment of the loan is to be invalid both for him and for anyone producing it, the copy of which he has handed back to him likewise for cancellation and annulment.
I, Eudaemon son of Ammonius, grandson of Ammonous, have received the two thousand and eighty drachmas and make no claim, as aforesaid. [...] alias Aurion son of Herminus, grandson of Euporus, of the Matidian tribe and Demetrian deme, read to Eudaemon the bank document of the discharge as it stands. I, Nilus son of Kephalion, of the Matidian tribe and Marcianian deme, witness the discharge. I, Apollon son of Apion, of the Sabinian tribe and Gamelian deme, witness. I, Didymus son of Hephaestion, of the Athenaean tribe and Salaminian deme, witness. I, Theon alias Tiro son of Harpocration, of the Trajanean tribe and Ktesian deme, witness. I, Polis son of Castor, have paid as aforesaid. I, Hermias son of Hermias, of the Sabinian tribe and Gamelian deme, wrote on his behalf, as he does not know letters.

To [...] Marcellus, vir perfectissimus, administering the functions of the governorship, from Rostamos [son of ...], of those from Birtha Okbanon. Suffering misery, lord, I take refuge with you and ask you to receive my petition kindly. For when my father, who is declared (above), died, lord, he left me a vineyard [in] Birtha, when I was very young. It happened that the (invasion) of the Persians took place and [...] I barely escaped and came to Appadana, providing my daily food [...]. After this, when I was in Birtha and wished to enjoy the fruits of the same vineyard left to me, a certain Barsemaias son of Thaimos, a very violent and arrogant man and very powerful in the area, using I know not what reason or what right, has occupied the same vineyard for about six years up to [today], despising my modest station, because I have no one, and paying no attention to the petitions submitted by me to the local centurion. Since, therefore, lord, I can obtain justice from nowhere unless your Fortune assents to me, for I am also harassed by Bathsabbatha, who was the creditor of my same father, to whom the same vineyard is also mortgaged, I ask and beg, if it seems good to your Fortune, that you order by your subscription the procurator in Appadana, Claudius Ariston, or whomever your Fortune thinks fit, (to ...) the [...] of the same Barsemaias, and to order him to pay me the revenues for the time he has enjoyed its fruits. For thus, through your Fortune, as a man of modest station not deprived of what is mine and remaining unharmed, I shall be grateful to you for [ever]. I, Clatius [...], having been asked, wrote on behalf of Rostamos, who is illiterate, who sent the notes. [...]

English translation:
Recto
1 To King Ptolemy, greetings, from Antipater, one of those from Philadelphia. I am wronged by Nicon.
2-4 For having lent to my wife Simon 70 drachmas of silver at interest of six drachmas per mina for each month, and having capitalised (it) together with the principal, he drew up with her a contract of loan for 115 drachmas, on which I was registered as guarantor.
4-7 When I had left Philadelphia because of being slandered by Artemidorus, the agent of Apollonius the dioiketes, and had opened a tavern in Upper Hermopolis, Nicon wrote a letter to Philadelphia to a certain Menestratus, our servant, in which he also writes that he will draw up a royal oath against us concerning his principal of the 70 drachmas.
7-10 When Menestratus wrote to me at Hermopolis to come, and I had sailed down to Philadelphia, Nicon sailed up to Hermopolis and said that he would hand my wife over to the collector (praktor) for the loan unless she followed him willingly.
10-13 Simon, being afraid, sailed down with Nicon together with the child; he took them to Heracleopolis and shut them up with certain people, each separately. Simon escaped unnoticed; but the child he still keeps shut up even now, and when we ask him to give it back, at one time he admits that he holds it as a pledge for the loan, at another he denies it.
13-17 I beg you therefore, O king, to send my petition to the chrematistai, and, if I show that what is in the petition is true, that Nicon receive the fitting punishment both for the interest which has been written contrary to the diagramma and because he has confined the free (child) and keeps it with him, and that the child be given back to me, so that, having taken refuge with you, O king, I may obtain justice.
18 Farewell.

1 To King Ptolemy, greeting, Dioscurides and [Nica]nor. We are wronged by Nephorsuchis.

Farewell.

1-5 In the reign of Ptolemy son of Ptolemy and Berenice, the Benefactor Gods, in the first year, in the priesthood of Nicanor son of Bacchius of Alexander and the Sibling Gods [and the Benefactor Gods], while [Aristomache daughter of Ptolemaeus] was basket-bearer of Arsinoe Philadelphus, on the eighteenth [of the month Gor]piaios, in the village of T[akona in the Oxyrhynchite] nome.

1-4 [To Agathis(?), stra]tegos and hipparch, from Theambesis daughter of Onnophris, wine-seller. Being wronged by Helio-
4-8 dorus son of Bromius, one of those living in the same Oxyrhyncha as I, of the division of Polemon,
8-16 I submitted to you a memorandum making clear to you that it is within his knowledge that I gave him by hand 1264 drachmas of copper and 1 1/2 artabas of wheat in Tybi of year 5, on condition that he would pay me interest on the copper until Phamenoth 30 of the same year;
17-24 and when the time had passed, being asked by me for payment, he gave me a cloak in Pharmouthi of the same year on condition that he would recover it by the 30th of the same month, though it was not worth the above-written amount.

33-39 I ask you to write to Chairephanes more urgently to take a pledge from him and send him to you, so that I may not trouble you about the same matters but may obtain help through you. Farewell.
40-42 To Chairephanes. Send the accused to us. Year 7, Thoth 22.

Recto
1-3 To Boethus, kinsman and epistrategos, from Euthaeus son of Ammonius, Libyan of the epigone.
3-11 In year 26 I lent to Zenon son of Thaliarchus, Libyan, and Polemon son of Dionysius, Persian, both of the infantry soldiers on fixed pay of Theodorus (5a, added above: living in Phebichis of the Koite), jointly, 10 1/2 artabas of solid wheat, by a contract of loan through which they stand surety for each other and agree that I may exact payment both from both of them and from whichever of them I choose.
11-27 But since the time of repayment has passed and more time besides has elapsed and they have not repaid, and one of them, Polemon, departed this life before the repayment, I ask, if it seems good, since I wish to exact payment from Zenon in accordance with the contract, that you give instructions to write to Euphranor, of those equal in rank to the first friends and strategos, to compel him to repay me the 10 1/2 artabas of wheat, and if he disobeys, to send him up to you. If this is done I shall obtain justice. Farewell.
28-31 To Euphranor: compel him to do what is just at once or send him up [...]. Year 33, Payni 14.
32-35 To Hagnesimenes: compel him to do what is just or send up the accused. Year 33, Payni 14.
Verso
36-37 Of Euthaeus son of Ammonius. To Euphranor.

English translation:
Column i. Sheet. To Protarchus from Gaius Iulius Philius and from Lycarion son of Apollonius and Ptolemaeus son of Ptolemaeus, both Persians of the epigone, and Lycarion's wife Erotarion daughter of Achilles, Persian, with her husband as guardian. Concerning the points at issue, Lycarion and Ptolemaeus and Erotarion agree that they have received from Gaius Iulius Philius a loan through the money-changing bank of Castor of 300 drachmas of Ptolemaic silver without interest, which they will also repay within 10 months from the first of Pachon of the present [17th year] of Caesar, paying each day from the same first of the month Pachon one drachma, skipping no day; and they will do this without any delay, or else, on whatever day they skip, they shall immediately be liable to seizure and be held under arrest until they have paid, without waiting for the time apportioned to them, the whole principal or what will remain owing, plus half as much again, and for the time exceeding (the term) the two-drachma interest according to the ordinance, the right of execution belonging to Gaius Iulius Philius both from the three, who are mutual sureties for payment, and from one, and from whichever of them he chooses, and from all their property, as if by a legal judgment, and further also from the woodselling workshop belonging to Lycarion, which is near the Syrion in the property of Dorion; and until they have paid off (the debt) they shall keep it unalienated and unencumbered, and if some risk should

Column ii. Sheet. befall it, even so the loan shall be free of all risk; and they shall not take refuge in safeguards, nor in a sacred share (?), nor in a suppliant's petition, nor in a decree of benefactions or of labour, nor at a place of asylum, nor in private help, nor in any other protection whatsoever, or whatever they resort to shall be invalid. And Gaius Iulius Philius for his part agrees that he will invalidate the two loan agreements, of 120 drachmas of silver each, which the same debtors made with him through the same court, because he has been paid in full by them the 240 drachmas of silver in all, in cash, and that he will not proceed against them concerning these, but only concerning the three hundred drachmas under this agreement.

Year 17 of Caesar, Pharmouthi 7.

(1) Since Numerius and Marcus Cloatius, sons of Numerius, Romans, (2) the proxenoi and benefactors of our city, have from the beginning (3) continued doing what is right both for the city and privately (4) for those of the citizens who approach them, falling short in nothing (5) of zeal and generosity; on account of which, at the very (6) occasions, the city, being grateful, made mention of them and honoured them with the (7) fitting honours, both in the year of Lachares, (8) when they made the settlement concerning the first loan, (9) and in the year of Phaeinus, when, concerning the other (10) loan, that of the three thousand nine hundred and sixty-five (11) drachmas, which the city borrowed in the year of Damarmenus, (12) having obtained in the time of Marcilius the people of the Athenians as judge, (13) being urged by the citizens they agreed (14) to receive as much as the citizens persuaded them; and in the (15) year of Biadas, when, having asked as a personal favour of (16) Publius Autronius and Lucius Marcilius, who were their (17) guest-friends, whom they also received at their own expense, (18) they begged off the soldiers and the rest of the (19) requisitions to be imposed by them, which were considerable, by which they relieved the city entirely, (20) the aforesaid men having granted them the favour; (21) and they have received, for the favour and the joint entertainment (?) of the city, (22) also many times many of the commanders, Gaius Julius, (23) legate, and Publius Autronius, legate, and Fulvius, (24) legate, doing all these things for the sake of their goodwill towards the (25) city and the citizens; and when (26) Gaius Gallius imposed on our city (a levy of) grain and Quintus Ancharius of cloaks, according to the share (27) falling on our city, having applied all zeal and generosity, (28) they petitioned that our city should not give but be (29) relieved, which they also obtained, and we did not contribute; and for the citizens (30) privately, as many as have approached them or had some need, (31) they have done everything for all, showing themselves unhesitating (32) on every occasion; and in the year of Timocrates, (33) when Antonius arrived, when the city was in need of (34) funds and no one else was willing to make a contract, they lent (35) us four thousand two hundred drachmas on a contract (36) at four-drachma interest; concerning which, being urged (37) by the people in the year of Nicaretidas, they conceded simple (38) interest of two drachmas, and granted to the (39) city, from the money owed, more than one thousand five (40) hundred drachmas; on account of all the aforesaid it was resolved (41) by the people at the great Apellai: to praise Numerius (42) and Marcus Cloatius, sons of Numerius, Romans, for (43) all the aforesaid towards the city and those of the private (44) citizens who have approached them, and for the goodwill which they have continued (45) to hold towards our city; English translation:
(1) [To Aurelius Antonius, the most perfect] prefect of Aegyptus Herculia, (2) [from Aurelius Isidorus son of Ptolemaeus, from the village of Kar]anis in the Arsinoite nome. Your solicitude in all things is accustomed to [help] everyone, lord prefect, (3) [and especially us, the people of modest means who] live well and honestly. My case is as follows. Having suffered violence and unfairness, lord, (4) [at the hands of Castor and Ammonianus from the same] village, concerning these men who act unlawfully and have shown the greatest unfairness (5) [to me: since, master, I leased from C]astor and Ammonianus twenty-five arouras of grain land, or however many they may be, in partnership for a half share, (6) [for the sowing of the current year only], I doing all the work [on the arouras] for the most part until the harvest, the seed being provided by (7) [me, Isidorus, as an advance, that is,] I provided them for sowing 20 artabas of wheat, 6 artabas of barley and 3 artabas of beans, and moreover for (8) [... sixty pairs of hired four-footed animals] fifteen talents of silver, and for the price of ... two talents; and having received as a loan (9) [from me, with and without a written contract, for their own] need, [another eight] talents [of silver], one empty sack of hair, another 22 1/2 artabas of wheat, and (10) [18 artabas of beans, and what was spent by me from] our own [for] wages for the harvesters, likewise another 24 artabas of wheat, I (11) [expecting] to suffer no harm [from them, thinking that they] would keep faith with me; but they, behaving arrogantly, unreasonably and recklessly, against the (12) [laws, without regard for fear of you, my] master, went off without my consent and (13) [carried off to their own house] all the threshing floors which I hold [in partnership] with them; and indeed, when I learned this, I came to one threshing floor of wheat and argued my case with (14) [Castor in the presence of witnesses]; he sent me away and gave me nothing, and I withdrew. Since therefore I advanced a great deal (15) [to them, with and without a written contract, and being unable (to deal)] with them, I submitted petitions to the strategus [of the nome] and to the praepositus of the pagus concerning (16) [their unfairness; I have therefore been compelled to take] refuge at the feet of you, my lord, begging and entreating, a man of modest means (17) [almost entirely] lacking [... necessary] sustenance, that you order by your most beneficent subscription that (18) [the aforesaid] be compelled [to restore to me] all the aforesaid, by the care of whomever your greatness may approve, so that with your help I may be able to (19) [enjoy my own and remain in my] own home; and having obtained this I will acknowledge to your fortune the greatest gratitude for ever. Farewell. (20) [I, Aurelius Isidorus, the aforesaid, submitted it.] [I, Aurelius Theon, wrote on his behalf], since he does not know letters. (21) [When our lords Constantinus and] Licinius Augusti were consuls for the 4th time, on the 6th day before the Kalends of January, Choiak 30. (22) [The exactor, in the presence] of the opposing party, having examined the matter between (23) [you] in accordance with the laws, will see to it that what just reason requires is done, provided that there are no (24) [other] impediments. (1) 643 (2) After the consulship of Flavius Troconda, vir clarissimus, (3) Pachon 9 of the 7th indiction. (4) Aurelius Abraham son of Ision and Sophia, from the village of Senokomis (5) of the Oxyrhynchite nome, to Aurelius Isak son of Nilus, from (6) the great city of Alexandria, merchant, greeting. (7) I acknowledge, my earlier note remaining valid and guaranteed, (8) that I have now also received from you as a loan, from (9) hand to hand, out of your house, for my own and pressing need, (10) imperial approved full-weight single gold solidi, (11) ten in number, total 10 gold solidi, of principal, and as interest on (12) them until the term stated below, of tow, (13) clean and satisfactory, by the weight of the village, (14) twenty bundles, total 20 bundles, which, being free from all risk, (15) I shall of necessity repay to you in the month of Phaophi of the current (16) year 161/130, at the beginning of the eighth indiction, without (17) delay and without any dispute, and in addition it shall not be (18) permitted to me to say that I have paid anything of the aforesaid debt (19) without a written receipt or joint receipt, or before the return (20) and redemption of this my note. And if, when the term (21) has arrived, I do not make the repayment to you and you wish, (22) having been asked, to grant me another term, I shall pay you these things (23) and for the time after that the interest on the same, the right of (24) execution being yours against both me and all my property. (25) The note, written in a single copy, is valid, and having been asked the formal question I consented. (26) I, Aurelius Abraham son of Ision, the aforesaid, have received (27) as a loan the ten gold solidi, apart from the (28) earlier note, of principal, and as interest on them (29) twenty bundles of tow as stated above. I, Banus, deacon, (30) son of Petrus, wrote on his behalf, as he does not know letters. (31) Written through me, Petrus.

Recto
(1) After the consulship of our lord Flavius Anastasius, eternal (2) Augustus, for the 2nd time, Tybi 20, indiction 6, in the city of Oxyrhynchus. (3) To Flavius Didymus, the respected eparchicus, son of Timotheus of most excellent memory, (4) from the illustrious and most illustrious city of the Oxyrhynchites, Aurelius (5) Theodorus son of the late Megas alias Didymus, nomikarios, from the (6) same city, signing below in his own hand, greeting. I acknowledge that I have received (7) from your respectedness on loan, from hand to hand, out of your house, for my own (8) urgent need, of gold simple imperial approved solidi, (9) in number six, by the private standard of the Oxyrhynchites, less six carats, total gold solidi 6 less 6 carats, (10) which, being free of all risk, I will of necessity repay (11) to your admirableness in the month Pachon of the current year 174 143 of the (12) present sixth indiction without delay. But if, when the aforesaid (13) term arrives, [...] I behave unreasonably about the (14) said debt (or) you wish to give me another (term) at our request, I acknowledge (15) that for the time elapsing after the term I will provide the lawful one-per-cent (16) interest until complete repayment of the same debt, which is to be repaid to you by me (17) after the term, if it so happens, [...] or the execution taking (18) place for you upon me and upon all my property, which is pledged (19) for the payment of this debt by way of pledge and under the law of mortgage. The contract, written in a single copy, (20) is valid, and having been asked I agreed. I, Aurelius Theodorus son of Megas, the aforementioned nomikarios, (21) received as principal six gold solidi less six carats and I will repay them at the term, (22) and all that is written is agreed by me as above, and having signed in my own hand, having been asked, I agreed. (23) I, Aurelius Philoxenus, his mother being Heraïs, witness the contract as above. (24) Written through me, Sarapammon.

Wherefore I too, the pitiable slave of my good master, (8) through this present petition of mine, wishing to obtain mercy, (9) want your lordship to know that from my fathers and forefathers I have served (10) my good master, paying the public dues every year; and by God's (11) will in the past eleventh indiction and the past (12) tenth my animals died, and I borrowed not a little gold, (13) 15 solidi, until I could buy the same animals. But when I approached (14) my good master and he had mercy on me (?), coming here, the agents (15) of my master did not consent to act according to the order of my good (16) master. For if, master, your mercy does not reach me, I cannot stand (17) on my estate and be of service to the landowner's affairs. And (18) I beseech and implore your lordship to order that mercy be shown (19) to me, since I have come to great ruin. For I have no other (20) refuge except that of the master Christ and of your eminence. (21) And I will send up immortal hymns to the master Christ for the (22) life of your lordship and of its most magnificent son, (23) the master Strategius.

(1) In the reign and consulship of our most divine lord (2) Flavius Justinus, eternal Augustus and Imperator, year (3) four, Pachon twentieth, at the beginning of the third indiction, in Antinoopolis the most splendid. (4) To Flavius Helladius, the most splendid scriniarius of the (5) splendid ducal staff of the Thebaid, son of (the man) of excellent (6) memory, originating from the (7) beautiful city of the Panopolites, from me, Martha, present, daughter of Menas, (8) mother Thecla, seller of salted fish, also originating (9) from Antinoopolis, acting without a husband as guardian, and providing (10) a subscriber on her behalf and witnesses, those signing below (11) this present mortgage contract on the terms set out hereafter, (12) agreed with all the stipulations it contains, greeting. My father (13) having fallen into the utmost poverty, and ... [...] (14) ... long ago, before he ended his life, (15) Menas by name, called Perichytes, and having of necessity pledged (16) at that time my younger orphaned sister called Procla to the (17) most splendid lord Nonnus for one solidus of gold, in accordance with the (18) mortgage note made by him at that time to the most splendid man, (19) and after his death, having in these circumstances acquired so far from my (20) handiwork half of the aforesaid one solidus, I paid it back to the (21) said man, wishing to ransom my distressed (22) sister, I the aforewritten Martha; and not being able to afford its (23) completion, but having had the good fortune to find your splendour (24) moved by love of God, I brought requests to it to (25) lend this remainder for the ransom of the same orphaned sister; (26) accordingly I, the same Martha, acknowledge that through your hand into my hands (27) I have received and borrowed from you, at the same time as the making of the security, (28) nine carats of gold by the public standard of Antinoopolis, total 9 carats of gold by the public standard of Antinoopolis; and as a deposit (29) of good faith and security and of clean and absolute repayment (30) I pledge to you from now and have pledged, by way of pawn and by right of mortgage, (31) my said sister Procla, being fifteen years old, more (32) or less, on condition that she is in your house serving in all (33) your slavish services and needs without leaving, in a free manner and (34) submissively and obediently, doing everything without guile, without any (35) flight and theft and any wrongdoing whatsoever, at my risk and resources (36) for all these things until the discharge of the aforementioned debt of the nine carats of gold, (37) being fed, however, and clothed, and that she be with you (38) without being treated with contempt until their repayment; and for your security I have made (39) this friendly note on all the terms written in it, and I have issued it, and having been asked I gave my assent. (40) I, Aurelia Martha daughter of Menas son of Perichytes, the aforewritten, made this mortgage of Procla my (41) sister for the nine carats of gold, and I shall repay as set out above. I, Aurelius Victor son of Ioannes, from Antinoopolis, wrote (42) on her behalf as she does not easily know letters. I, Aurelius Colluthus son of Callinicus, with God notary, witness the mortgage, having heard (it) (43) from the one who made it.

[...] ℎελλενοταμίαις καὶ παρέδροις ἐδανείσα[μεν ․․․․․․15․․․․․․․] Ἀριστοκράτει Εὐονυμεῖ καὶ χσυνάρχοσι 𐅈ΤΤΤΤ, οὗτοι δὲ ἔδοσαν ἀθλοθέταις ἐς Παναθέναια [...] ἐπὶ τε͂ς Κεκροπίδος τετάρτες πρυτανευόσες ℎέ[κτει ℎεμέραι τ]ε͂ς πρυτανείας ℎελλενοταμίαις καὶ παρέδροις Ἀριστοκράτει Εὐονυμεῖ καὶ χσυνάρχοσι στρατιόταις ἐ[μ Μέλοι ․․․7․․․]ΔΔ [...] ἐπὶ τε͂ς Ἀντιοχίδος ὀγδόες πρυτανευόσες δεκ[άτει ℎεμέραι τε͂ς] πρυτανείας ℎελλενοταμίαις καὶ παρέδροις Ἀριστοκρ[ά]τει Εὐονυμεῖ καὶ χσυνάρχοσι στρατιόταις ἐμ Μ[έλοι ․․․․9․․․․]𐅄̣Δ̣ [...] ἐπὶ τε͂ς Ἀντιοχίδος ὀγδόες πρυτανευόσες τρίτε[ι ℎεμέραι τε͂ς πρυ]τανείας ℎελλενοταμίαις καὶ παρέδροις Ἀριστοκρ[άτ]ει Εὐονυμεῖ καὶ χσυνάρχοσι 𐅋𐅋𐅋, ℎοῦτοι δ’ ἔδοσαν [τε͂ι ἐν Σικελίαι σ]τρατιᾶι [...] ἐπὶ τε͂ς Ἀντιοχίδος ὀγδόες πρυτανευόσες εἰκοσ[τε͂ι ℎεμέραι τε͂ς πρ]υτανείας ℎελλενοταμίαις καὶ παρέδροις Ἀριστοκρ[ά]τει Εὐονυμεῖ καὶ χσυνάρχοσι ἐς τὰ<ς> ναῦς τὰς ἐς Σι[κελίαν διακομιόσα]ς τὰ χρέματα ΤΤΤΤΧΧ [...] ἐπὶ τε͂ς Ἀντιοχίδος ὀγδόες πρυτανευόσες δευτέ[ραι ℎεμέραι τε͂ς πρυτα]νεία[ς] ℎελλενοταμίαι καὶ παρέδροι Φιλομέ[λοι Μ]αραθονίοι καὶ στρατεγο͂ι ἐν το͂ι Θερμαίοι κόλπο[ι [...] ε͂ι αὐτε͂ι ℎεμέραι ℎελλενοταμίαι κ[αὶ παρέ]δροι Φιλομέλοι Μαραθονίοι καὶ στρατεγο͂ι ἐν Ἐφ[έσοι [...]

English translation:
[...] we lent to the Hellenotamiai and their assessors [...] Aristocrates of Euonymon and his colleagues, 9 talents, and these gave it to the athlothetai for the Panathenaea [...] In the fourth prytany, that of Cecropis, on the sixth day of the prytany, to the Hellenotamiai and their assessors Aristocrates of Euonymon and his colleagues, for the soldiers in Melos, [...] 20 [...] In the eighth prytany, that of Antiochis, on the tenth day of the prytany, to the Hellenotamiai and their assessors Aristocrates of Euonymon and his colleagues, for the soldiers in Melos, [...] 60 [...] In the eighth prytany, that of Antiochis, on the third day of the prytany, to the Hellenotamiai and their assessors Aristocrates of Euonymon and his colleagues, 300 talents, and these gave it to the army in Sicily [...] In the eighth prytany, that of Antiochis, on the twentieth day of the prytany, to the Hellenotamiai and their assessors Aristocrates of Euonymon and his colleagues, for the ships carrying the money to Sicily, 4 talents 2,000 drachmas [...] In the eighth prytany, that of Antiochis, on the second day of the prytany, to the Hellenotamias and assessor Philomelus of Marathon and to the general in the Thermaic Gulf [...] [...] on the same day, to the Hellenotamias and assessor Philomelus of Marathon and to the general in Ephesus [...]

[․]α ἐκκαθάρασι [— — — — — — — — — — — — — — — — — — — — — — — — — — — τὸν] Ἀρχη[γέ][τ]ην ∶Δ∶ μηνὸς Ἀρτεμισιῶνος [ἀρχι]τέκτο[νι? — — — — — —]νος πόδας· [․․․]ΙΜΟΥ[—c.10—] δικαστη[ρ]ίωι μισθὸς ἐπιτιμητῶν ∶Δ𐅂ΙΙΙΙ∶ [Δ]ημητρίωι τῶι ἀρχιτέκτονι σιτηρέσιον κατὰ τὸ ψήφισμα ἀπὸ δευ̣[τέρ]ας Ἀρησιῶνος ∶𐅄Δ𐅃· [ἐ]φό[δι]ον ἐπιτιμηταῖς ∶𐅄ΔΔΔ∶ Ἀριστοθέωι τοῦ θησαυροῦ [․]Ρ[․]Σ[․․․] ι∶ ∶𐅅̣Δ𐅃𐅂∶ Σωσανδρίδηι τὸν θησαυρὸν [ἐκ]καθάραντι ∶𐅂𐅂𐅂𐅂· [σ]τήλη ∶𐅄̣Δ𐅃𐅂𐅂· ναῦλον ∶𐅃𐅂∶ ἀνακομίσασι ∶𐅂∶ βατὴρ τῆι στήληι [∶․∶ τ]ὰ γράμματα τὰ ἐν τῆι στήληι ἐγκολάψαντι Δόνακι ∶𐅄ΔΔΔ· [τ]ὸμ̣ βατῆρα ὀρύξαντι καὶ τὴν στήλην προσκομίσαντι κ̣αὶ [στή]σαντι ∶ Νίκωνι ∶𐅃𐅂𐅂∶ μόλυβδος τῆι στήληι ∶𐅂̣𐅂̣𐅂𐅂∶ μισθωτοῖς λίθων [․․] [Ἡρ]ακλείδηι ὀβελίσκων ταλάντου τιμὴ ∶𐅄̣ΔΔ· Ἀρτίμαι ὀβελίσκων ∶ΔΔΔΙ̣Ι̣ΙΙ∶ τιμὴ ∶ΔΔΔΔ𐅂𐅂∶ δέλτ̣ο̣ς τῶι λόγωι ·𐅂𐅂𐅂𐅂· πέτευρα 𐅃[․]· στήλης τοῖς ἐνηροσίοις [∶]𐅃𐅂𐅂· λίθους λευκοὺς προσεπριάμεθα παρὰ Δεξιπό[λιος] εἰς τὴν [․․]χον̣ τὴ̣ν̣ ἐν τῶι Ἀρτεμισίωι 𐅄𐅂𐅂ΙΙΙ· σύμπαν κεφάλαιον ἀναλώματος· δραχμαὶ ΧΧΧΧΗΗ𐅄ΔΔ[— — —c.20— — —]. {²vac.}² καὶ ἄλλο ἀργύριον ἐξείλομεν μετὰ τῆς βουλῆς ὃ ἐδανείσατο ἡ πόλις κατὰ ψήφισμα τοῦ δήμου εἰς φυλακὴν τῶν Τυρρηνῶν δρα[χ]μὰς 𐅆 ἐπὶ ταῖς προσόδοις ταῖς τῆς πόλεως παρόντων τῶν γραμματέων. vac. [κ]αὶ ἄλλο ἀργύριον ἐξείλομεν μετὰ τῆς βουλῆς παρόντων [τῶν γραμμ]ατέων ὃ ἐδανείσατο ἡ πόλις κατὰ ψήφισμα τοῦ δήμου δραχμὰς ΜΧΧ ἐπὶ ταῖ̣ς προσόδοις ταῖ̣ς τῆς πόλεως. vac. {²vac.}² τὸ λοιπὸν ἀργύριον παρέδομεν τοῖς ἱεροποιοῖς τοῖς ἐπὶ Πυρρίδου ἄρχοντος [— c.10 —] ξένου, Δ[ι]ακρίτωι Ἕρμωνος, Δεξικράτηι Ἀλέξιος, Φίλλιδι Εὐέτου, παρόντων τῶν γραμματέων Διογνήτου τοῦ [Τι— — —], Θεογνώτου τοῦ Πατροκλέους ἀργυρίου δραχμὰς πεντα[κισ]μυρίας πεντακισχιλίας ἑπτακοσίας τριάκοντα. vac.

English translation:
Account of the hieropoioi who served in the archonship of Cleocritus: Eudemus son of Amnus, Xenon son of Pistus, Scymnus son of Phanodicus, Callisthenes son of Theorylus. We received the following from the hieropoioi who served in the archonship of Demonax, Menecleides son of Philocles, Apol[...] son of A[...], [...] son of Aristomachus, [...] son of Alcimides, in the presence of the councillors and [secretaries ...]: forty-six thousand nine hundred drachmas [...] [...] of Apollodorus [...] [...]. [...] we paid out [...] we paid out 16 drachmas [...] from [...] other works 150 drachmas [...] 24 drachmas 1 obol; pairs of roof tiles [...] to Kore (?) a pig 6 drachmas 3 obols; a pail [...] 2 drachmas [...] a cloak from [...] 8 drachmas; [...] to those who cleaned [...] the Archegetes 10 drachmas. Month of Artemision: to the architect (?) [...] feet; [...] to the court, pay of the assessors 11 drachmas 4 obols; to Demetrius the architect, his allowance for food according to the decree from the second of Aresion, 65 drachmas; travel money for the assessors 80 drachmas; to Aristotheus [...] of the treasury 516 drachmas; to Sosandrides for cleaning the treasury 4 drachmas; a stele 67 drachmas; freight 6 drachmas; to those who carried it up 1 drachma; a base for the stele [...]; to Donax for carving the letters on the stele 80 drachmas; to Nicon for digging out the base and bringing up and setting up the stele 7 drachmas; lead for the stele 4 drachmas; to hired workers for stones [...]; to Heracleides, the price of a talent of spits, 70 drachmas; to Artimas for 34 (?) spits, price 42 drachmas; a writing tablet for the account 4 drachmas; boards 5 [...]; for the stele for the Eneroseia (?) 7 drachmas; we bought in addition white stones from Dexipolis for the [...] in the Artemision 52 drachmas 3 obols. Total sum of expenditure: 4,270 [...] drachmas. And we took out other money with the council, which the city borrowed according to a decree of the people for the defence against the Tyrrhenians, 5,000 drachmas, on the security of the revenues of the city, in the presence of the secretaries. And we took out other money with the council, in the presence of the secretaries, which the city borrowed according to a decree of the people, 12,000 drachmas, on the security of the revenues of the city. The remaining money we handed over to the hieropoioi who served in the archonship of Pyrrhides, [...]xenus, Diacritus son of Hermon, Dexicrates son of Alexis, Phillis son of Euetes, in the presence of the secretaries Diognetus son of Ti[...] and Theognotus son of Patrocles: fifty-five thousand seven hundred and thirty drachmas of silver.

[...] τῶι ἀργυρίωι ὧι ἐδανείσαμεν τοῖς ἐ[πι]μεληταῖς τῆς στοᾶς δραχμὰς [∶]ΧΧ̣Η̣Δ [...] καὶ τόδε ἀργύριον ἐδανείσαμεν κατὰ ψήφισμα [τ]οῦ δήμου καὶ κατὰ τὸν νόμον <καὶ> κατὰ συγγραφὰς τῆι πόλει καὶ προδανεισταῖς Πίστηι Ξένωνος, Πολύβωι Διοδότου ∶𐅅ΗΗ∶ κατὰ συγγραφὴν τὴγ κειμένην παρὰ Ἀντιγόνωι τῶι Χαρίλα [...] Γαλαξιῶνος Δημέαι καὶ Θεωρύλωι καὶ ἀναδόχοις Δημέου Καλλισθένει Θεωρύλου, Ξενοκλείδει Ἀφθονήτου ∶ΧΧΗΗΗΗ∶ κατὰ συγγραφὴν τὴγ κειμένην παρὰ Ἀντιγόνωι τῶι Χα[ρ]ίλα· τούτου ἀποδέδωκε Θεωρύλος τοῦ καθ’ αὑτὸν μέρους ∶Χ∶ [...] Ἑκατομβαιῶνος τῆι πόλει καὶ προδανεισταῖς Στησιλέωι Σκύμνου, Ἀντιγόνωι Ἀνδρομένους, Ἱερομβρότωι Εὐδήμο[υ] [κ]αὶ ἀναδόχοις Σκύμνωι Φανοδίκου, Δημόνωι Νίκωνος, Εὐδήμωι Ἄμνου ∶ΧΧΧ∶ κατὰ συγγραφὴν τὴν παρ’ Ἀνπυκίδει Κριτοβούλου κειμένην [...] τῆι πόλει καὶ προδανεισταῖς Μνησάλκωι Τ[ε][λ]εσαρχίδου, Πολύβωι Διοδότου, Δημέαι Αὐτοκλέους ∶ΧΧ∶ κατὰ συγγραφὴν τὴγ κειμένην παρὰ Πίστηι τῶι Ξένωνος· ἄρχει τοῦ τόκου μεὶς Ληναιὼν ὁ ἐπὶ Καλλίμου [...]

English translation:
[...] from the money which we lent to the overseers of the stoa, 2,110 drachmas [...] And we lent this money, according to the decree of the people and according to the law and according to contracts, to the city and to the pro-borrowers Pistes son of Xenon and Polybus son of Diodotus, 700, according to the contract deposited with Antigonus son of Charilas [...] [in the month] Galaxion, to Demeas and Theorylus, and as guarantors of Demeas, Callisthenes son of Theorylus and Xenoclides son of Aphthonetus, 2,400, according to the contract deposited with Antigonus son of Charilas; of this Theorylus has repaid, for his own share, 1,000 [...] [in the month] Hecatombaeon, to the city and to the pro-borrowers Stesileos son of Scymnus, Antigonus son of Andromenes and Hierombrotus son of Eudemus, and as guarantors Scymnus son of Phanodicus, Demon son of Nicon and Eudemus son of Amnus, 3,000, according to the contract deposited with Ampycides son of Critobulus [...] to the city and to the pro-borrowers Mnesalcus son of Telesarchides, Polybus son of Diodotus and Demeas son of Autocles, 2,000, according to the contract deposited with Pistes son of Xenon; the interest begins in the month Lenaeon in the archonship of Callimus [...]

[...] καὶ ἄλλας Αὐτοκλεῖ Τελ[έ]σωνος μηνὸς Ἀρησιῶνος δραχμὰς ΗΗ ἐ[π]ὶ ὑ[ποθ]ήκει τῆι οἰκίαι ἣν ἐπρίατο Νικάνωρ παρὰ Θεοδωρίδου ἧι γειτονεύει ἡ οἰκία ἡ Ξενοκλείδου καὶ ἡ 〚— — — — —〛 Ἄμνου, ἐπιχωρήσα[ν]τος Ξένωνος τοῦ Νικάνορος, καὶ ἀναδόχοις Ἀν[τ]ιγόνωι Δημέου, Τηλεμνήστωι Ἀντιγόνου· ἡ συγγραφὴ παρὰ Διονυσίωι τῶι Ἀγοράλλου. [...]

English translation:
[...] And we lent this money: in the month Lenaeon, by decree, to the city and to the pro-borrowers, the councillors, 3,000 drachmas, which Echenice daughter of Stesileos dedicated for a sacrifice to Apollo and Aphrodite, on the security of the public revenues; the contract is with Paches. [...] And for the grain purchase we lent from the sacred money, by decree, to the city and to the pro-borrowers Xenocrates son of Hierombrotus, Polyxenus son of Aresimbrotus and Sosidemus son of Nicon, 10,500 drachmas, on the security of the public revenues. [...] And we lent other money to the city and to the pro-borrowers, the councillors, by decree, for the sum paid to Cynon, 1,700 drachmas. [...] And we lent this other money from the sacred funds: to Autocles son of Teleson, in the month Aresion, 400 drachmas, on the security of the house in Thokos which belonged to Hierombrotus, adjoining the house of Satyrion, and on all the other property of Autocles, with the guarantors Antigonus son of Demeas and Telemnestus son of Antigonus; the contract is with Dionysius son of Agorallus. [...] And another sum to Autocles son of Teleson, in the month Aresion, 200 drachmas, on the security of the house which Nicanor bought from Theodorides, adjoining the house of Xenoclides and the [...] of Amnus, with the consent of Xenon son of Nicanor, with the guarantors Antigonus son of Demeas and Telemnestus son of Antigonus; the contract is with Dionysius son of Agorallus. [...] And to Diactorides son of Theorylus, in the month Apaturion, 400 drachmas, on the security of the estate adjoining the estate which belonged to Phereclides and which is called Phytalia, and on all the other property of Diactorides, with the guarantors Callisthenes son of Theorylus and Antigonus son of Didymus; the contract is with Epicharmus son of Theoprotus. [...]

[...] καὶ εἰς τὴν σι[τω]νίαν ἐδανείσαμεν τοῦ ἱεροῦ ἀργυρίου κατὰ ψήφισμα τῆι πόλει καὶ προδανεισταῖς Ξενοκράτει Ἱερομβρότου, Πολυξένωι Ἀρησιμβρότου, Σωσιδήμωι Νίκωνος δραχμὰς Μ𐅅̣ ἐπὶ ὑποθήκει τα[ῖς] προσόδοις ταῖς δημοσίαις. [...] καὶ ἄλλας ἐδανείσαμεν τῆι πόλει καὶ προδανεισταῖς τοῖς βουλευταῖς κατὰ ψήφισμα εἰς τὸ ἀποδοθὲν Κύνωνι δραχμὰς Χ𐅅ΗΗ. [...] καὶ τόδε ἄλλο ἀργύριον ἐδα[νεί]σαμεν τοῦ ἱεροῦ· Αὐτοκλεῖ Τελέσωνος μηνὸς Ἀρησιῶνος δραχμὰς ΗΗΗΗ ἐπὶ ὑποθήκει τεῖ οἰκίαι τῆι ἐν Θώκωι ἣ ἦν Ἱερομβρότου ἧι γειτονεύει ἡ οἰκία ἡ Σατυρίωνος καὶ ἐπὶ τοῖς ἄλ[λοις] τοῖς ὑπάρχουσιν Αὐτοκλεῖ πᾶσιν καὶ ἀναδ[όχοι]ς Ἀντιγόνωι Δημείου, Τηλεμνήστωι Ἀντιγόνου· ἡ συγγραφὴ παρὰ Διονυσίωι τῶι Ἀγοράλλου. [...] καὶ ἄλλας Αὐτοκλεῖ Τελ[έ]σωνος μηνὸς Ἀρησιῶνος δραχμὰς ΗΗ ἐ[π]ὶ ὑ[ποθ]ήκει τῆι οἰκίαι ἣν ἐπρίατο Νικάνωρ παρὰ Θεοδωρίδου ἧι γειτονεύει ἡ οἰκία ἡ Ξενοκλείδου καὶ ἡ 〚— — — — —〛 Ἄμνου, ἐπιχωρήσα[ν]τος Ξένωνος τοῦ Νικάνορος, καὶ ἀναδόχοις Ἀν[τ]ιγόνωι Δημέου, Τηλεμνήστωι Ἀντιγόνου· ἡ συγγραφὴ παρὰ Διονυσίωι τῶι Ἀγοράλλου. [...] καὶ Διακτορίδει Θεωρύλου μηνὸς Ἀπατου[ρι]ῶνος δραχμὰς ΗΗΗΗ ἐπὶ ὑποθήκει τῶι χωρίωι ὧι γειτονεύει τὸ χωρίον ὃ ἦν Φερεκλείδου καὶ ὃ καλεῖται Φυταλιὰ καὶ τοῖς ἄλλοις τοῖς ὑπάρχουσιν Διακτορίδει πᾶσιν καὶ ἀναδόχοις Καλλισθένει Θεωρύλου, Ἀντιγόνωι Διδύμου· ἡ συγγραφὴ παρ’ Ἐπιχάρμωι Θεοπρώτου. [...]

English translation:
[...] And we lent this money: in the month Lenaeon, by decree, to the city and to the pro-borrowers, the councillors, 3,000 drachmas, which Echenice daughter of Stesileos dedicated for a sacrifice to Apollo and Aphrodite, on the security of the public revenues; the contract is with Paches. [...] And for the grain purchase we lent from the sacred money, by decree, to the city and to the pro-borrowers Xenocrates son of Hierombrotus, Polyxenus son of Aresimbrotus and Sosidemus son of Nicon, 10,500 drachmas, on the security of the public revenues. [...] And we lent other money to the city and to the pro-borrowers, the councillors, by decree, for the sum paid to Cynon, 1,700 drachmas. [...] And we lent this other money from the sacred funds: to Autocles son of Teleson, in the month Aresion, 400 drachmas, on the security of the house in Thokos which belonged to Hierombrotus, adjoining the house of Satyrion, and on all the other property of Autocles, with the guarantors Antigonus son of Demeas and Telemnestus son of Antigonus; the contract is with Dionysius son of Agorallus. [...] And another sum to Autocles son of Teleson, in the month Aresion, 200 drachmas, on the security of the house which Nicanor bought from Theodorides, adjoining the house of Xenoclides and the [...] of Amnus, with the consent of Xenon son of Nicanor, with the guarantors Antigonus son of Demeas and Telemnestus son of Antigonus; the contract is with Dionysius son of Agorallus. [...] And to Diactorides son of Theorylus, in the month Apaturion, 400 drachmas, on the security of the estate adjoining the estate which belonged to Phereclides and which is called Phytalia, and on all the other property of Diactorides, with the guarantors Callisthenes son of Theorylus and Antigonus son of Didymus; the contract is with Epicharmus son of Theoprotus. [...]

[...] καὶ ἐδανείσ[α]μεν τεῖ πόλει καὶ τεῖ βουλεῖ τεῖ ἐπ’ ἄρχοντος Χαρίλα καὶ τοῖς ταμίαις Φιλοκλεῖ καὶ Φανοδίκωι καὶ τῶι γραμματεῖ Παρ[μ]ενίωνι καὶ [τ]οῖς προδανεισταῖς Μαντιθέωι, Ἀριστέαι Ἀντιγόνου, Ἀντιγόνωι Τελεσαρχίδου, Διογένει Τελέσωνος, κατὰ τὸ ψήφισμα τοῦ [δ]ήμου ·𐅇Χ𐅅ΗΔΔΔ𐅂𐅂𐅂𐅂ΙΙΙ· [...] καὶ ἄλλας ἐξείλομεν ·Μ· παρούσης βουλῆς καὶ γραμματέως τοῦ τῆς [πό]λεως Παρμενίω[νος], τοῦ τῶν ἱεροποιῶν Ἑλικάνδρου, καὶ ἐδανείσαμεν <u>τεῖ πόλει</u> <u>καὶ τοῖς βουλ</u>ευταῖς καὶ τοῖς ταμίαις Φιλοκλεῖ καὶ Φανοδίκω[ι] [καὶ τῶι] γραμματεῖ Παρμενίωνι καὶ τοῖς προδανεισταῖς <u>Πολυξένωι</u> [<u>Ἀλκι?</u>]<u>μάχου, Ἱερομβρότωι</u> Ἄμνου· αἱ συγγραφαὶ παρὰ Κλεοκρίτωι Δι[ο]νυσίου. [...]

English translation:
[...] and we lent to the city and to the council in the archonship of Charilas and to the treasurers Philocles and Phanodicus and to the secretary Parmenion and to the guarantors (prodanistai) Mantitheus, Aristeas son of Antigonus, Antigonus son of Telesarchides, Diogenes son of Teleson, according to the decree of the people, 6,634 drachmas 3 obols. [...] and we took out another 10,000 drachmas in the presence of the council and of the secretary of the city Parmenion and of the secretary of the hieropoioi Helicandrus, and we lent them to the city and to the councillors and to the treasurers Philocles and Phanodicus and to the secretary Parmenion and to the guarantors (prodanistai) Polyxenus son of Alcimachus (?), Hierombrotus son of Amnus; the contracts are with Cleocritus son of Dionysius. [...]

Η𐅃 [...] Ποσιδεῶνος· Κοσμιάδει Σήμου Η𐅄̣ ἐπὶ τῆι οἰκίαι ἧι γείτων ἡ Δημοχάρους [...] Τιμοσθένηι Κλεοκρίτου 𐅅 ἐπὶ τῆι οἰκίαι τῆι πατρώιαι [...] Τιμοξένωι Ἄμνου ΗΗ𐅄 ἐπὶ τῆι οἰκίαι καὶ τῶι ναυπηγίωι [...] Μενεθάλει Ἡρακλείδου Η ἐπὶ τῆι οἰκίαι [...] Θυμί[αι] Ἐχεκρατίδου Η ἐπὶ τῆι οἰκίαι τῆι ἐπὶ κλιμακίωι [...]

English translation:
[...] And we lent this, by decree, to the city and to the pro-borrowers, and to the council and the treasurers Thessalus and Antigonus and the secretary Apollodorus, Mennis son of Nicarchus and Apollodorus son of Phocaeus, from the sacred money, 1,300, according to the contract with Calliphantus [...] We lent another sum to the city and to the pro-borrowers and to the council and to the secretary Apollodorus and to the treasurers Thessalus, Antigonus, Xenodocus son of Eche[...], Polyxenus son of Parmenion and Demon son of Sosidemus, 5,514 drachmas and a fraction (?) [...] And we lent these from the sacred money: in the month Lenaeon, to Theaeus son of Theaeus, on the neighbouring house, 105 [...] Posideon: to Cosmiades son of Semus, 150, on the house adjoining that of Demochares [...] to Timosthenes son of Cleocritus, 500, on the paternal house [...] to Timoxenus son of Amnus, 250, on the house and the shipyard [...] to Menethales son of Heraclides, 100, on the house [...] to Thymias son of Echecratides, 100, on the house by the stairway [...]

[...] καὶ τόδε ἐδανείσαμεν κατὰ ψήφισμα τῆι πόλει καὶ προδανε[ισ<ταῖς>] καὶ τῆι βουλῆι καὶ ταμίαι<ς> Θεσσαλῶι, Ἀντιγόνωι καὶ γραμματεῖ Ἀπολλοδώρωι, Μέννι Νι(κάρχου) καὶ Ἀπολλοδώρωι Φωκαι(έως) τοῦ [ἱε][ρ]οῦ ἀργυρίου ΧΗΗΗ̣ κατὰ συγγραφὴν τὴν παρὰ Καλλιφάντωι [...] ἄλλο ἐδανείσαμεν τῆι πόλει καὶ προδανεισταῖς καὶ βο[υ][λ]εῖ [κ]αὶ τῶι γραμματεῖ Ἀπολλοδώρωι καὶ τοῖς ταμίαις Θεσσαλῶι, Ἀντιγόνωι, Ξενοδόκωι Ἐχε(—), Πολυξένωι Παρμενίων[ος], [Δ]ημόνω̣ι Σωσι̣(δήμου) 𐅆𐅅Δ𐅂𐅂𐅂𐅂𐅦 [...] καὶ τάδε ἐδανείσαμεν τοῦ ἱεροῦ ἀργυρίου· μηνὸς Ληναιῶνος· Θεαίωι Θεαίου ἐπὶ τῆι οἰκίαι τῆι γ̣εί̣[τονι]. Η𐅃 [...] Ποσιδεῶνος· Κοσμιάδει Σήμου Η𐅄̣ ἐπὶ τῆι οἰκίαι ἧι γείτων ἡ Δημοχάρους [...] Τιμοσθένηι Κλεοκρίτου 𐅅 ἐπὶ τῆι οἰκίαι τῆι πατρώιαι [...] Τιμοξένωι Ἄμνου ΗΗ𐅄 ἐπὶ τῆι οἰκίαι καὶ τῶι ναυπηγίωι [...] Μενεθάλει Ἡρακλείδου Η ἐπὶ τῆι οἰκίαι [...] Θυμί[αι] Ἐχεκρατίδου Η ἐπὶ τῆι οἰκίαι τῆι ἐπὶ κλιμακίωι [...]

English translation:
[...] And we lent this, by decree, to the city and to the pro-borrowers, and to the council and the treasurers Thessalus and Antigonus and the secretary Apollodorus, Mennis son of Nicarchus and Apollodorus son of Phocaeus, from the sacred money, 1,300, according to the contract with Calliphantus [...] We lent another sum to the city and to the pro-borrowers and to the council and to the secretary Apollodorus and to the treasurers Thessalus, Antigonus, Xenodocus son of Eche[...], Polyxenus son of Parmenion and Demon son of Sosidemus, 5,514 drachmas and a fraction (?) [...] And we lent these from the sacred money: in the month Lenaeon, to Theaeus son of Theaeus, on the neighbouring house, 105 [...] Posideon: to Cosmiades son of Semus, 150, on the house adjoining that of Demochares [...] to Timosthenes son of Cleocritus, 500, on the paternal house [...] to Timoxenus son of Amnus, 250, on the house and the shipyard [...] to Menethales son of Heraclides, 100, on the house [...] to Thymias son of Echecratides, 100, on the house by the stairway [...]

(amount lost) at interest of one tenth], with surety Nesiotes son of Dorieus, on the mortgage of the dwellings of Phanyllus [...] [to Lysixenus son of ... and] Hierombrotus son of Amnus 175 drachmas at interest of one tenth, with sureties [...] of Hierombrotus, Amnus son of Hierombrotus, Lysixenus [...] to Antilacus son of Simides 100 drachmas at interest of one tenth, with sureties Nicanor son of Diodotus and Epicharmus [...] to Menyllus son of Polybus 100 drachmas 3 obols at interest of one tenth [...] And we made the following loans [from the sacred money of the hestiatic fund] of the Echenikeion: to Menethales, with her father Pythocles as guardian, 150 drachmas at interest of one tenth [...] And we made the following loans [from the sacred money of the hestiatic fund] of the Echenikeion [...] to Arcileos son of Tlepolemus, from the Echenikeion, 150 drachmas at interest of one tenth [...]

English translation: (Face a) In the presidency of Dexiteles. Artemidorus son of Myron proposed: since Socrates son of Sosipater, of Sidon, continues to be well disposed to the people of the Chalcidians and is useful to many of the citizens in whatever anyone asks of him, lacking nothing in zeal and generosity, and has also several times imported grain and sold it at the price the magistrates asked of him, be it resolved by the council and the people that Socrates son of Sosipater, of Sidon, be proxenos and benefactor of the people of the Chalcidians, both himself and his descendants, and that they have the right to own land and a house, and security and inviolability both in war and in peace, and that they have all the other privileges that have been granted to the other proxenoi and benefactors of the people of the Chalcidians. (Face b) In the presidency of Antileon, in the month Olympion. Asclepiades son of [...]cles proposed: since Eubulus son of Agathinus, of Cnidus, continues to be well disposed to the people of the Chalcidians and is useful to many of the citizens whenever anyone happens to need him, be it resolved by the people that Eubulus son of Agathinus, of Cnidus, and his descendants be proxenos, and that he have the right to own land and a house, and that he have inviolability and security both in war and in peace, and that he have all the other privileges, just as has been granted to the other proxenoi. (Face c) In the presidency of Archias, on the fourteenth of the month Thargelion. Since, when the city needed money for the purchase of grain, Cleon son of Eunostidas, a Lacedaemonian, being proxenos of the city, on being asked to lend as much as was convenient for him, offered himself without excuse, giving thirteen thousand five hundred drachmas interest-free, choosing, as far as lay in him, that the people should not fall behind in any of its pressing needs, concerning these matters be it resolved by the synedroi to praise Cleon son of Eunostidas, the Lacedaemonian, for showing his sincere goodwill towards our city, and to invite him also to a sacrifice in the prytaneion at the common hearth; and that the generals and the secretary of the synedrion take care that the proxeny granted to him by the city be inscribed in the most conspicuous place of the agora, and likewise this decree also; and that the treasurer pay the expense for this, and that the grain-buyers make the repayment of the aforesaid money, as is written in the decree [concerning these matters]. English translation:
[...] And we lent the following loans from the sacred money according to the contracts deposited with [...]: [...] in the month Posideon: to Aristeas son of Aristeas, his wife Archiurge also approving, on the security [...] [...] and to Philagrus son of Diadelus [...] To Orthocles son of Orthocles, his wife Hagneis also consenting [...] To Antigonus son of Charistius 500 drachmas, on the security of the house [...] To Nicomachus son of Nicomachus 1,000 drachmas, on the security of the house in Potamos [...] [...] son of [...]aeron, his wife Xenaeno also consenting, 500 drachmas, on the security of the house by the sea [...] on the security of the house at Phlox and of his other property and that of the guarantors; guarantors: Ctesicles son of Ctesicles [...] [...] next to the sacred house, Hippon and his wife Eritado also consenting [...] [...] son of [...]des, his wife Hegenassa also consenting, 500 drachmas, on the security of the house at Stephane [...] [...] son of [...]lus, on the security of the house of Parmenion, his wife Aristophile also consenting, 500 drachmas [...] To Theodorus and Diophantus, sons of Sosibius, 500 drachmas, on their share of the paternal house [...] [...] son of Telesippus, his wife Hormano also consenting, on the security of the paternal house [...] on the security of the house at Halia and of his property and that of the guarantors; guarantors: Antigonus son of Charistius, Charistius son of Antigonus [...] [...] son of Nicomachus 13,400 drachmas, on the security of the garden adjoining the garden of Dorieus son of Dorieus [...] To Antigonus son of Alexicus, from the Gorgieian fund 650 drachmas [...] To Antigonus son of Alexicus, from the Gorgieian fund 650 drachmas and from the [...] fund [...] To Asstyphose daughter of Dionysius, with her guardian, [her husband(?)] [...] To Timonase daughter of Telemnestus [...] [...] house in [...] belonging to Praximenes and his other property [...] [...] son of Euanthus, from the Philonideian fund 100 drachmas and from the Echenicean fund 50 drachmas [...]

English translation:
[...] And we lent the following loans from the sacred money according to the contracts deposited with [...]: [...] in the month Posideon: to Aristeas son of Aristeas, his wife Archiurge also approving, on the security [...] [...] and to Philagrus son of Diadelus [...] To Orthocles son of Orthocles, his wife Hagneis also consenting [...] To Antigonus son of Charistius 500 drachmas, on the security of the house [...] To Nicomachus son of Nicomachus 1,000 drachmas, on the security of the house in Potamos [...] [...] son of [...]aeron, his wife Xenaeno also consenting, 500 drachmas, on the security of the house by the sea [...] on the security of the house at Phlox and of his other property and that of the guarantors; guarantors: Ctesicles son of Ctesicles [...] [...] next to the sacred house, Hippon and his wife Eritado also consenting [...] [...] son of [...]des, his wife Hegenassa also consenting, 500 drachmas, on the security of the house at Stephane [...] [...] son of [...]lus, on the security of the house of Parmenion, his wife Aristophile also consenting, 500 drachmas [...] To Theodorus and Diophantus, sons of Sosibius, 500 drachmas, on their share of the paternal house [...] [...] son of Telesippus, his wife Hormano also consenting, on the security of the paternal house [...] on the security of the house at Halia and of his property and that of the guarantors; guarantors: Antigonus son of Charistius, Charistius son of Antigonus [...] [...] son of Nicomachus 13,400 drachmas, on the security of the garden adjoining the garden of Dorieus son of Dorieus [...] To Antigonus son of Alexicus, from the Gorgieian fund 650 drachmas [...] To Antigonus son of Alexicus, from the Gorgieian fund 650 drachmas and from the [...] fund [...] To Asstyphose daughter of Dionysius, with her guardian, [her husband(?)] [...] To Timonase daughter of Telemnestus [...] [...] house in [...] belonging to Praximenes and his other property [...] [...] son of Euanthus, from the Philonideian fund 100 drachmas and from the Echenicean fund 50 drachmas [...]

English translation:
[...] And we lent the following loans from the sacred money according to the contracts deposited with [...]: [...] in the month Posideon: to Aristeas son of Aristeas, his wife Archiurge also approving, on the security [...] [...] and to Philagrus son of Diadelus [...] To Orthocles son of Orthocles, his wife Hagneis also consenting [...] To Antigonus son of Charistius 500 drachmas, on the security of the house [...] To Nicomachus son of Nicomachus 1,000 drachmas, on the security of the house in Potamos [...] [...] son of [...]aeron, his wife Xenaeno also consenting, 500 drachmas, on the security of the house by the sea [...] on the security of the house at Phlox and of his other property and that of the guarantors; guarantors: Ctesicles son of Ctesicles [...] [...] next to the sacred house, Hippon and his wife Eritado also consenting [...] [...] son of [...]des, his wife Hegenassa also consenting, 500 drachmas, on the security of the house at Stephane [...] [...] son of [...]lus, on the security of the house of Parmenion, his wife Aristophile also consenting, 500 drachmas [...] To Theodorus and Diophantus, sons of Sosibius, 500 drachmas, on their share of the paternal house [...] [...] son of Telesippus, his wife Hormano also consenting, on the security of the paternal house [...] on the security of the house at Halia and of his property and that of the guarantors; guarantors: Antigonus son of Charistius, Charistius son of Antigonus [...] [...] son of Nicomachus 13,400 drachmas, on the security of the garden adjoining the garden of Dorieus son of Dorieus [...] To Antigonus son of Alexicus, from the Gorgieian fund 650 drachmas [...] To Antigonus son of Alexicus, from the Gorgieian fund 650 drachmas and from the [...] fund [...] To Asstyphose daughter of Dionysius, with her guardian, [her husband(?)] [...] To Timonase daughter of Telemnestus [...] [...] house in [...] belonging to Praximenes and his other property [...] [...] son of Euanthus, from the Philonideian fund 100 drachmas and from the Echenicean fund 50 drachmas [...]

English translation:
[...] And we lent the following loans from the sacred money according to the contracts deposited with [...]: [...] in the month Posideon: to Aristeas son of Aristeas, his wife Archiurge also approving, on the security [...] [...] and to Philagrus son of Diadelus [...] To Orthocles son of Orthocles, his wife Hagneis also consenting [...] To Antigonus son of Charistius 500 drachmas, on the security of the house [...] To Nicomachus son of Nicomachus 1,000 drachmas, on the security of the house in Potamos [...] [...] son of [...]aeron, his wife Xenaeno also consenting, 500 drachmas, on the security of the house by the sea [...] on the security of the house at Phlox and of his other property and that of the guarantors; guarantors: Ctesicles son of Ctesicles [...] [...] next to the sacred house, Hippon and his wife Eritado also consenting [...] [...] son of [...]des, his wife Hegenassa also consenting, 500 drachmas, on the security of the house at Stephane [...] [...] son of [...]lus, on the security of the house of Parmenion, his wife Aristophile also consenting, 500 drachmas [...] To Theodorus and Diophantus, sons of Sosibius, 500 drachmas, on their share of the paternal house [...] [...] son of Telesippus, his wife Hormano also consenting, on the security of the paternal house [...] on the security of the house at Halia and of his property and that of the guarantors; guarantors: Antigonus son of Charistius, Charistius son of Antigonus [...] [...] son of Nicomachus 13,400 drachmas, on the security of the garden adjoining the garden of Dorieus son of Dorieus [...] To Antigonus son of Alexicus, from the Gorgieian fund 650 drachmas [...] To Antigonus son of Alexicus, from the Gorgieian fund 650 drachmas and from the [...] fund [...] To Asstyphose daughter of Dionysius, with her guardian, [her husband(?)] [...] To Timonase daughter of Telemnestus [...] [...] house in [...] belonging to Praximenes and his other property [...] [...] son of Euanthus, from the Philonideian fund 100 drachmas and from the Echenicean fund 50 drachmas [...]

English translation:
[...] And we lent the following loans from the sacred money according to the contracts deposited with [...]: [...] in the month Posideon: to Aristeas son of Aristeas, his wife Archiurge also approving, on the security [...] [...] and to Philagrus son of Diadelus [...] To Orthocles son of Orthocles, his wife Hagneis also consenting [...] To Antigonus son of Charistius 500 drachmas, on the security of the house [...] To Nicomachus son of Nicomachus 1,000 drachmas, on the security of the house in Potamos [...] [...] son of [...]aeron, his wife Xenaeno also consenting, 500 drachmas, on the security of the house by the sea [...] on the security of the house at Phlox and of his other property and that of the guarantors; guarantors: Ctesicles son of Ctesicles [...] [...] next to the sacred house, Hippon and his wife Eritado also consenting [...] [...] son of [...]des, his wife Hegenassa also consenting, 500 drachmas, on the security of the house at Stephane [...] [...] son of [...]lus, on the security of the house of Parmenion, his wife Aristophile also consenting, 500 drachmas [...] To Theodorus and Diophantus, sons of Sosibius, 500 drachmas, on their share of the paternal house [...] [...] son of Telesippus, his wife Hormano also consenting, on the security of the paternal house [...] on the security of the house at Halia and of his property and that of the guarantors; guarantors: Antigonus son of Charistius, Charistius son of Antigonus [...] [...] son of Nicomachus 13,400 drachmas, on the security of the garden adjoining the garden of Dorieus son of Dorieus [...] To Antigonus son of Alexicus, from the Gorgieian fund 650 drachmas [...] To Antigonus son of Alexicus, from the Gorgieian fund 650 drachmas and from the [...] fund [...] To Asstyphose daughter of Dionysius, with her guardian, [her husband(?)] [...] To Timonase daughter of Telemnestus [...] [...] house in [...] belonging to Praximenes and his other property [...] [...] son of Euanthus, from the Philonideian fund 100 drachmas and from the Echenicean fund 50 drachmas [...]

[...] And we lent the following loans from the sacred money: in the month [...] [...]: to the city and to the council in office under Polyxenus and to the secretary Diogenes and to the treasurers Boethus son of Orthocles, [Phanus ...] and to the pre-lenders (prodaneistai) Euxenides son of Phocaeus, [...], for the crown for King Eumenes, according to the contract deposited with Diophantus son of Sosibius, 1,500 drachmas.
