[...] In Hieros: to the city and to the council and to the secretary Diogenes and to the treasurers Boethus and Phanus and to the pre-lenders Ctesonides son of Amphithalus, E[...], for the crown for King Prusias, according to the contract deposited with Diophantus son of Sosibius, 190 drachmas. [...] In Aresion: to the city and to the council in office under Polyxenus and to the secretary Diogenes and to the treasurers Boethus and Phanus, for the gift voted by the people to the city of the Megarians, 1,000 drachmas. [...] And we lent this other money from the banquet money: in Buphonion: to Timaretus son of Timaretus, a loan of the sacred money, through the guarantors Ar[...] son of [...], Phillacus son of Emmenides, according to the contract deposited with Diophantus son of Sosibius: from the Philonideian fund 200 drachmas; and from the Philocleian fund 250; and from the Xenocleideian fund 250 [...]; and from the Philonideian fund [...] 1 obol; and from the Philocleian fund [...]; and from the Eutycheian fund 100 [...]. In Apaturion: to Callimus son of Aristodemus, a loan of the banquet money: from the [...] fund, through the guarantors Amphias son of Sosistratus and Agatharchus son of Lysagoras, according to the contract deposited with Diophantus son of Sosibius [...]. [...] To Apaturius son of [...], his wife Melissa also consenting, a loan of the sacred money: from the Eutycheian fund, through the guarantor Silenus son of Silenus, according to the contract deposited with Diophantus son of Sosibius [...]. [...] To Pistis(?) son of Phereclides: from the Chersonesian fund 100 drachmas, through the guarantor Rhadis(?) son of Didymus, according to the contract deposited with Diophantus son of Sosibius [...]. To Soteles son of Posidicus: from the Eutycheian fund [...]; and from the Philetaireian fund 104 drachmas; and from the Chersonesian fund 5 [...] 1 drachma 4 obols [...]; and from the Nesiadeian fund [...], through the guarantor [...] son of Antigonus [...]. To Hypselus son of Dionnus, of the sacred money: from the Philonideian fund 127 drachmas 3 obols; and from the [...] fund [...]; and from the Philocleian fund 350; and from the [...] fund [...]; and from the Nesiadeian fund 10, through the guarantors So[...] son of Sosibius, Dem[...] son of [...], according to the contract deposited with Diophantus son of Sosibius. [...]

[...] In Aresion: to the city and to the council in office under Polyxenus and to the secretary Diogenes and to the treasurers Boethus and Phanus, for the gift voted by the people to the city of the Megarians, 1,000 drachmas. In Apaturion: to Callimus son of Aristodemus, a loan of the banquet money: from the [...] fund, through the guarantors Amphias son of Sosistratus and Agatharchus son of Lysagoras, according to the contract deposited with Diophantus son of Sosibius [...]. [...] To Apaturius son of [...], his wife Melissa also consenting, a loan of the sacred money: from the Eutycheian fund, through the guarantor Silenus son of Silenus, according to the contract deposited with Diophantus son of Sosibius [...]. [...] To Pistis(?) son of Phereclides: from the Chersonesian fund 100 drachmas, through the guarantor Rhadis(?) son of Didymus, according to the contract deposited with Diophantus son of Sosibius [...]. [...] 12,000 denarii, on which the interest up to the 30th of the month Apellaeus of the current year is 1,200 denarii, on mortgage of two plots of land in Apollonia, one called [...]astion's, the other called "by Paparion's", and with guarantor Diodorus son of Musaeus, grandson of Diodorus, of Apollonia [...] another duplicate of a loan lent by me to Diodorus son of Musaeus, grandson of Diodorus, of Apollonia from Salbace, of a principal of 10,000 denarii, on which the interest up to the same due date is 2,450 denarii, on mortgage of a field [...] another duplicate of a loan lent by me to the same Diodorus son of Musaeus, of a principal of 10,000 denarii, on which the interest up to the 30th of the month Apellaeus of the current year is 2,450 denarii, on mortgage of allotments [...] another duplicate of a loan lent by me to Publius Albius Atimetus of Apollonia from Salbace, of a principal of 4,500 denarii, on which the interest up to the 30th of the month Apellaeus of the current year is 1,102 denarii [...] another duplicate of a loan lent by me to the same Publius Albius Atimetus, of a principal of 1,500 denarii, on which the interest up to the month Apellaeus of the current year is 367 1/2 denarii [...] another duplicate of a loan lent by me to Gaius Julius son of Gaius [...] of a principal of 3,000

[—] [— κα]ταλέλοιπα αὐτῇ γυμνασιαρχικὰ χρήματα [—] [πρὸς τὸ? ἔλαιο]ν ὑπηρετεῖν εἰς τὰς ἐξ ἐπιδόσεως γυμνασιαρχίας [καὶ?] [τὰ]ς λοιπὰς ζῶν μυριάδας ὑπεσχόμην καὶ ἀνέθηκα δέκα δύο, δη[νάρια] διακόσια ἑξήκοντα, πρὸς τὸ τὸν κύκλον τοῦτον ἐκ τῶν ἐμῶν ὑποσχέσεων τῇ ἐμῇ φιλοτειμίᾳ αὐξηθῆναι καὶ ἀνελλιπῶς ἀλείφεσθαι τοὺς πο[λ]είτας καὶ εὐχερέστερον εὑρίσκεσθαι τοὺς ὑπηρετοῦντ<α>ς ἐλαιῶνας. ἐπεὶ δὲ καὶ γράφοντί μοι τὴν διαθήκην ἔδοξέ μοι πλεῖον καταλιπεῖν εἰ[ς] [τὰ]ς αἰωνίους καὶ διηνεκεῖς ἐπιτελουμένας γυμνασιαρχίας καὶ εἰς τὰ ἄ[ν]ω μέρη τῆς διαθήκης περὶ τὴν ποσότητα ὑπεργραφαὶ γεγόνασιν, φανερὸ[ν] [π]οιῶ καὶ ἐπὶ τέλει τῆς διαθήκης, ὅτι καταλέλοιπα καὶ διὰ τῆς διαθήκης εἰς τὰς αἰωνίους γυμνασιαρχίας καὶ στεφανηφορίας μυριάδας δέκα τέσσαρας κα[ὶ] δηνάρια τρισχίλια ἐνακόσια δέκα τέσσαρα, ὥστε εἶναι ὁμοῦ ἅς τε ζῶν ἀνέθη[κ]α διμερῶς ἐν ἀρχῇ μὲν τοῦ νόμου κυρουμένου ὑποσχέσεων γινομένων [κ]αὶ ἐγὼ ὑπεσχόμην, μυριάδας <δ>ύο, καὶ πάλιν ἀνέθηκα μυριάδας δέκα καὶ δηνά[ρ]ια διακόσια ἑξήκοντα, καὶ ἃς διὰ τῆς διαθήκης καταλέλοιπα, τὰς πάσας γυμνασιαρχικὰς μυριάδας εἴκοσι ἕξ, δηνάρια τετρακισχίλια ἑκατὸν ἑβδομήκο[ν]τα ἐννέα. ἐπὶ στεφανηφόρου Ποπλίας Αἰλίας Ἀδράστου θυγατρὸς Ἀτταλίδος Σαβείνης τὸ δεύτ<ε>ρον, μηνὸς Κλαυδιήου, Ἄτταλος Ἀδράστου τοῦ Νικοτίμου τοῦ Ἀρτεμιδώρου τοῦ Ζήνωνος Ἱέρακος Ἄδραστος, ἱερεὺς θεοῦ Ἡρακλέου[ς,] φυλῆς Ῥωμαΐδος, γεγραπφὼς ἐν τῇ διαθήκῃ δηλῶ καὶ τῷ πιττακίῳ τ[ῷ] ἐνειλημ[μ]ένῳ ἐν τῇ διαθήκῃ τὰς δανε<ι>ακὰς ἀσφαλείας καὶ τὴν ποσότητα το[ῦ] ἀργυρίου οὗ καταλέλοιπα διὰ τῆς διαθήκης τῇ γλυκυτάτῃ μου πατρίδι εἰς τὰς αἰωνίους γυμνασιαρχίας καὶ στεφανηφορίας καὶ ὅσα τῇ βουλ<ῇ> καὶ τῇ γερουσίᾳ καταλέλοιπα δηλῶ καὶ φανερὸν ποιῶ καὶ διὰ τούτου τοῦ πιττακίου γράψας τῇ ἐμαυτοῦ χειρὶ ᾗ καὶ τὴν διαθήκην γέγραπφα τὰ ὀνόματα τῶν χρεωστῶν καὶ τί ἕκαστος αὐτῶν ὀφείλει ἀρχαίου καὶ τόκου, καὶ ἐστὶν καθὼς ὑπογέγραπται. [Μᾶ]ρκος Ἀν[τώνιος] Ἀπελλᾶς Δομετεῖνος ὀφείλει μοι διὰ τοῦ χρεοφυλακίου δηνά[ρια ἐ]νακι[σχίλια διακό]σια καὶ τὰ τοῦ τόκου μηνὸς ἑνὸς δηνάρια τεσσεράκοντα ἕξ [—]ναδ[—]ν τόκον ὀκτασσαριαῖον, διὰ τὸ εἶ[ναι αὐ]τὸν τ[— δα][νει]σμοῦ [—] Τιβερίου Κλαυδ[ίου —]

English translation:
[...] I have left to it gymnasiarchic funds [...] to supply [the oil (?)] for the gymnasiarchies from voluntary contributions [and (?)] the remaining [...]; while alive I promised and dedicated twelve myriads and two hundred and sixty denarii, so that this cycle might be increased by my munificence from my promises, and the citizens might be anointed without interruption, and the olive groves that supply it might be found more easily. And since, when I was writing my will, I decided to leave more for the perpetual and continuously held gymnasiarchies, and in the upper parts of the will there are additions concerning the amount, I also make it clear at the end of the will that I have left through the will for the perpetual gymnasiarchies and stephanephoriai fourteen myriads and three thousand nine hundred and fourteen denarii, so that together the sums I dedicated while alive in two parts, at the beginning when the law was ratified and promises were made and I too made a promise, two myriads, and again I dedicated ten myriads and two hundred and sixty denarii, and those I have left through the will, all the gymnasiarchic funds amount to twenty-six myriads, four thousand one hundred and seventy-nine denarii. In the year of the stephanephoros Publia Aelia Attalis Sabina daughter of Adrastus, for the second time, in the month of Claudieus, I, Attalus Adrastus son of Adrastus son of Nicotimus son of Artemidorus son of Zeno Hierax, priest of the god Heracles, of the tribe Romais, having written in the will, declare also in the note enclosed in the will the loan securities and the amount of the money which I have left through the will to my sweetest fatherland for the perpetual gymnasiarchies and stephanephoriai, and what I have left to the council and the gerousia; I declare and make clear also through this note, having written with my own hand, with which I also wrote the will, the names of the debtors and what each of them owes of principal and interest, and it is as written below. Marcus Antonius Apellas Dometinus owes me through the record office nine thousand two hundred denarii and the interest for one month, forty-six denarii [...] interest at eight asses (?), because he is [...] of the loan [...] Tiberius Claudius [...]

The following, being generously and benevolently disposed toward the people, promised and remitted half of the interest on the loans owed to them by the people: Ptolemaeus son of Andronicus 606; Cartalis son of Cartalis 474; Plistarchus son of Zosimus 430; Hermagoras son of Philopolis 80 [...]; Craterus son of Aristodemus 240; Plato son of Apollonius son of Aristomachus 440; Posidonius son of [...]echarus, Cyaneites, 395; Menodotus son of Menodotus 83; Callippus son of Archelaus 400; [...] Ptolemaeus son of S[...]nus 100 [...]; Hermolycus son of Hermolycus 40; Stasithemis son of [...]ius 140 [...]; Artemon son of Aristophanes [...]; Aristophanes son of Aristophanes [...]; [...]sis son of Hermaratus [...]; Hermapion son of Cleon 30 [...]; Me[...]ne daughter of Timagenes 303; Zosimus son of Hermandimasis 243; Hoplon son of Cleon 204; Aristeus son of Aristeus 115; Mimmis and Panathiatis, daughters of Demetrius, [...]96.

The following, being generously and benevolently disposed toward the people, promised and remitted half of the interest on the loans owed to them by the people: Ptolemaeus son of Andronicus 606; Cartalis son of Cartalis 474; Plistarchus son of Zosimus 430; Hermagoras son of Philopolis 80 [...]; Craterus son of Aristodemus 240; Plato son of Apollonius son of Aristomachus 440; Posidonius son of [...]echarus, Cyaneites, 395; Menodotus son of Menodotus 83; Callippus son of Archelaus 400; [...] Ptolemaeus son of S[...]nus 100 [...]; Hermolycus son of Hermolycus 40; Stasithemis son of [...]ius 140 [...]; Artemon son of Aristophanes [...]; Aristophanes son of Aristophanes [...]; [...]sis son of Hermaratus [...]; Hermapion son of Cleon 30 [...]; Me[...]ne daughter of Timagenes 303; Zosimus son of Hermandimasis 243; Hoplon son of Cleon 204; Aristeus son of Aristeus 115; Mimmis and Panathiatis, daughters of Demetrius, [...]96.

Original Text:
[...] οἵδε ἐδάνεισαγ Κνιδίωμ Μιλησίοις ἀργυρίου Ῥοδίου· vacat Σίφος Ἀκροτέλευς, Τιμοδάμας Λαχάρτου δραχμὰς ἑξακισχιλίας. vacat Φ̣ιλόφρων Φιλίστα καὶ Ἄρχιππος Τιμαιθίου δραχμὰς τρισχιλίας. vacat Δ̣ιότιμος καὶ Μελλῖνος Ἀγαθοβούλου καὶ Τιμᾶς Τιμᾶ δραχμὰς ἑξακισχιλ̣[ίας]. vacat [Κ]λεισίλοχος Ἀναξιππίδα δραχμὰς δισχιλίας. vacat [Ἀ]ντίγονο̣ς̣ Ἐπιγόνου δραχμὰς ἑξακισχιλίας. vacat [Θ]εσσαλάκων Καλλίππου δραχμὰς τρισχιλίας. vacat [Σ]τιφολαΐδας Ἀκροτάτου δραχμὰς δισχιλίας. vacat [Ἀ]ντικράτης καὶ Φιλοκράτης Ἐπικράτους δραχμὰς τρισχιλίας. vacat [Μ]ένιππος Ἀπολλοδώρου δραχμὰς τρισχιλίας. vacat [Ε]ὐφραγόρας Κλευμένης Κλεύμβροτος Φιλίστα δραχμὰς τρισχιλίας. vacat [Κ]αλλικλῆς Ἀθηνοκρίτου Ἁλικαρνασσεὺς δραχμὰς ἑξακισχιλίας. vacat [Ἀ]θηνόδωρος Θεοδώρου Κυρηναῖος δραχμὰς μυρίας δισχιλίας. vacat οὗτοι ἐδάνεισαν τρία ἔτη· ἄρχει τοῦ δανείου μεὶς Ἀρτεμισιὼν vacat ἐ̣π’ Ἀλεξίππου· τ̣όκος τῆς μνᾶς ἑκάστης ἑκάστου μηνὸς τρεῖς ὀβολ[ο]ί. vacat [οἵ]δε ἄτοκον ἐδάνεισαν ἐνιαυτόν· Ἀνθαγόρας Κλέωνος δραχμὰς ἑξακισχιλίας. vacat [Β]ο̣υλαρχίδας Ἀρχιπ[ό]λιος δραχμὰς ἑξακισχιλίας. vacat [Ἐ]π̣ικύδης Θεάνου δραχμὰς τετρακισχιλίας. vacat [Νί]κανδρος Συμμάχου Ἁλικαρνασσεὺς δραχμὰς δισχιλίας. vacat [τ]ὸ πᾶν Ῥοδίου τάλαντα δεκαδύο μναῖ δέκα.

English translation:
[...] The following of the Cnidians lent to the Milesians Rhodian silver: Siphus son of Acroteles, Timodamas son of Lachartes, 6,000 drachmas. Philophron son of Philistas and Archippus son of Timaethius, 3,000 drachmas. Diotimus and Mellinus sons of Agathobulus and Timas son of Timas, 6,000 drachmas. Cleisilochus son of Anaxippidas, 2,000 drachmas. Antigonus son of Epigonus, 6,000 drachmas. Thessalacon son of Callippus, 3,000 drachmas. Stipholaidas son of Acrotatus, 2,000 drachmas. Anticrates and Philocrates sons of Epicrates, 3,000 drachmas. Menippus son of Apollodorus, 3,000 drachmas. Euphragoras, Cleumenes, Cleumbrotus sons of Philistas, 3,000 drachmas. Callicles son of Athenocritus of Halicarnassus, 6,000 drachmas. Athenodorus son of Theodorus of Cyrene, 12,000 drachmas. These lent for three years; the loan begins in the month Artemision in the term of Alexippus; interest for each mina for each month three obols. The following lent free of interest for a year: Anthagoras son of Cleon, 6,000 drachmas. Bularchidas son of Archipolis, 6,000 drachmas. Epicydes son of Theanes, 4,000 drachmas. Nicander son of Symmachus of Halicarnassus, 2,000 drachmas. The total in Rhodian money: twelve talents ten minas.

English translation:
Recto. In the reign of our most divine and most pious master Flavius Iustinianus, eternal Augustus and Imperator, year 18, in the third year after the consulship of Flavius Basilius, vir clarissimus, Phamenoth 21, indiction 8, year 221 (and 190), in the city of Oxyrhynchus.
This agreement of acknowledgements and stipulations, without fraud, fear, force, compulsion or deceit, and free of all circumvention, is made by the pious community (koinobion) of Abba Hierax of holy memory, through Joseph, priest and head of the same pious place, and Theodorus who manages it, with the consent of all the most reverend monks in it, to Flavius Apion, the most magnificent former ordinary consul, son of Strategius of all-praised memory, through Menas, servant of his magnificence, who puts the question and acquires for his most magnificent master every action and claim that belongs or may belong under the present agreement; and it acknowledges what is written below.
Diogenes of illustrious memory, then living in the imperial city (Constantinople) and being in need of eighty solidi, asked Theophilus of reverend memory, who also happened then to be in the same imperial city, to lend them to him at half-hundredth interest, and to receive from him, as security for the same eighty solidi, a waterwheel-estate (mechane) of sixteen and a half arouras situated in the village of Ophis, and to take the annual interest from the produce and revenues of the same estate and to hold it until full repayment of the same eighty solidi. So, the same eighty solidi having been lent by Theophilus of reverend memory to Diogenes of illustrious memory, a public (agoraion) document was drawn up by him in the same imperial city, in which he mortgaged to the pious community of Abba Hierax of holy memory, through Theophilus of reverend memory, the said estate of sixteen and a half arouras, on condition that the pious community take from its produce and revenues the interest on the eighty solidi each year and hold this estate as security for both the principal and the interest to accumulate, until full repayment.
Again, the same Diogenes of illustrious memory, in need of another fifty solidi, asked the same Theophilus of reverend memory, who was then also living in the same imperial city, to lend him these too; and Theophilus of reverend memory, persuaded, provided the fifty solidi to Diogenes of illustrious memory, and for these fifty solidi another contract was made, in which the same Diogenes of illustrious memory gave a special and general mortgage on all his property.
These things having so proceeded, it happened that Diogenes of illustrious memory died before repaying the sums contained in these documents, and that Strategius of all-glorious memory, to whom Diogenes was indebted under various loan contracts carrying general and special mortgages, sought an heir of Diogenes of illustrious memory in order to recover lawfully from him what Diogenes of illustrious memory owed him. No heir of Diogenes of illustrious memory being found, and Apphouas of illustrious memory, his brother, and Klematia of noble memory, his sister, having then expressly renounced his inheritance, Strategius of glorious memory was compelled, for lack of an heir, to ask to take ownership, by right of the mortgages contained in his loan contracts, of all the property of Diogenes of illustrious memory; and having lawfully received possession of all the property, he came into possession also of the said estate, which belonged to the same property and was comprised in the mortgages of Diogenes of illustrious memory held by Strategius of all-glorious memory.
Hence Theophilus of reverend memory, having then gone to the imperial city, addressed entreaties to Strategius of all-glorious memory about the said estate, explaining that the pious community through him had given eighty solidi under a first loan contract to Diogenes of illustrious memory on the mortgage of the same estate, and another fifty solidi by another public document on a general mortgage of all his property, and he asked that on this account the said estate be ceded to his pious community. In reply Strategius of all-glorious memory produced his own loan contracts and showed that the general mortgage on all the property of Diogenes of illustrious memory contained in them was earlier than the public documents shown to him by that man, affirming that under the laws he had become owner of all the property of Diogenes of illustrious memory, justly, on account of what was owed to him.
Learning this, Theophilus of reverend memory, reckoning that he had no legal claim regarding the same estate but had altogether lost this mortgage because the mortgages contained in the loan contracts of Strategius of all-glorious memory were earlier, begged the same Strategius of all-glorious memory not to make full use of the law and of the rights belonging to him, but to look to piety and to the need of the brothers in the said pious community, who required the same one hundred and thirty solidi for providing their necessary sustenance, and to give the one hundred and thirty solidi to the same pious community as an act of piety. Strategius of all-glorious memory, moved [...], wrote to those attached to his magnificence in this city to give to the pious community managed by Theophilus of reverend memory one hundred and thirty solidi; they, having received these letters, then gave only seventy-two solidi to the said Theophilus of reverend memory, that is to the same pious community, and they then deposited them with Serenus of blessed memory, former zygostates of this (city) of the Oxyrhynchites, on condition that he lend them out and provide what accrued from them each year to the pious community, until an estate for sale should be found and the same pious community buy it, and the same Serenus give the pound of gold towards part of the price of the estate found and to be sold to the same pious community.
These things having so happened, it came about that Serenus of blessed memory, former zygostates of this illustrious city of the Oxyrhynchites, died, and that those of the pious community of Abba Hierax of holy memory then received from the heirs of Serenus the same pound of gold, and recently went up to the imperial city and entreated Apion, the most magnificent former consul, and his all-praised mother, who is also his guardian, to allow to be given what Strategius of all-glorious memory, while still alive, had out of piety ordered by his own letters those attached to him to provide, that is the other fifty-eight solidi less two hundred and thirty-two carats, on the private standard of this city of the Oxyrhynchites.
Now Apion, the most magnificent former ordinary consul, and Leontia, his all-praised mother, being by nature inclined to piety and disposed to grant the requests of those in need, especially of most reverend men, and because Strategius of all-glorious memory, while still alive, had written that one hundred and thirty solidi be given to the pious community but only seventy-two had been given up to now, have by their own letters allowed those attached to their magnificence in this city to provide another fifty-eight solidi to those of the pious community. The other fifty-eight solidi having therefore been given to the same pious community through Joseph the most reverend, those of the pious community, through the same most reverend priest and head and Theodorus the manager, have come to the present agreement, by which they acknowledge that from the beginning Strategius of all-glorious memory, not making use of the laws and all his rights and his earlier mortgages, and being under no obligation to provide them anything, but out of piety, then wrote that the one hundred and thirty solidi be given to them in the country, of which they then received only seventy-two, and that recently Apion the all-praised consul and his most glorious mother, following the pious purpose of the deceased, allowed another fifty-eight to be given to them.
The head of the same pious community and Theodorus, who manages the pious community, and through them the other most reverend monks of the same pious community further acknowledge that, first, while Strategius of all-glorious memory was alive, they received by his letters from those then attached to his glorious house one pound of gold, which, as narrated above, they acknowledge having received from the heirs of the blessed Serenus the zygostates, and that now likewise they have received into their hands another fifty-eight gold solidi less two hundred and thirty-two carats, which Apion the all-praised consul and his most glorious mother recently wrote to be given to them; and that they have no claim concerning the same estate, because, as has been said, from the beginning they had no lawful claim to vindicate it on account of the earlier mortgages of Strategius of all-glorious memory; and that they give thanks and pray for Strategius of all-praised memory for the one hundred and thirty solidi which out of piety he, while still alive, allowed to be given to them, and likewise beseech the divinity to grant long life to Apion, the all-praised former consul, and to his most glorious mother Leontia, in return for which they too, under no obligation, recently allowed another fifty-eight solidi to be given to complete what was then written by Strategius of all-glorious memory, while still alive, to be given to them.
And as security for what they have agreed, calling God as witness, they acknowledged that they will abide by these terms, keep them, and hold them valid for ever, and not oppose them or any part or article of them, neither now nor hereafter, neither in a local or foreign court nor out of court, nor by a petition submitted to our most victorious master, nor accuse or blame them before friends, or any part of them, either by law or in the holy churches, nor claim to have suffered any circumvention or fraud, because by careful reasoning and from the exact laws they have learned that they have no lawful action or proceeding on the mortgage of the said estate, because, as said, the mortgages in the loan contracts of Strategius of all-praised memory were found to be earlier, but that the same fifty-eight solidi were given to them, that is to their pious community, as an act of piety. And they further acknowledge that all evil fraud is and will be absent from this agreement, and that it is valid against them and those who after them manage and head the same pious community for all time to come; and having been asked on all points, they acknowledged in person, and they mortgaged as security for the present agreement all present and future property of the pious community, specially and generally, by way of pledge and by right of mortgage, in full form as for mortgages, nothing being or able to be excepted from this mortgage. And all having been read and interpreted to them and having pleased them, they subscribed through Pamouthius, asked by them since they are illiterate, the head and the manager making [...] marks (?). For the trust and confirmation of what we have agreed, we have also handed over to your eminence these loan contracts which Diogenes of illustrious memory issued to our pious community, even though we have no help at all from them. The agreement is valid. It was written in a single copy, as above.
Joseph, priest, archimandrite. Joseph, priest. Joseph.
The pious community called of Abba Hierax, situated in the western desert of this city of the Oxyrhynchites, through me Joseph, monk and priest, head of the same pious community: I have received the one hundred and thirty gold solidi on the Oxyrhynchite standard according to the narrative set out above, and I am released regarding what was owed by Diogenes of illustrious memory, and I have no claim to the waterwheel-estate called Tmao, situated in the plain of Ophis, mortgaged to me by the same Diogenes of illustrious memory, nor to other property of the same Diogenes of illustrious memory; but I also give thanks to your magnificence for the piety it has shown in ordering the same one hundred and thirty gold solidi to be given to the same pious monastery; and everything and each point is agreeable to me as above, and having been asked I acknowledged. And all having been read and interpreted to me, I, the same Joseph, the least, asked the most admirable Pamouthius to subscribe for me since I am illiterate, and I released (the document). I, Pamouthius son of Philoxenus of blessed memory, subscribed at the request of the same most reverend Joseph, who is illiterate and before me made three crosses with his own hand, and I released (it).
The pious community called of Abba Hierax, situated in the western desert of this city of the Oxyrhynchites, through me Theodorus, manager of the pious community: I have received the one hundred and thirty gold solidi on the Oxyrhynchite standard according to the narrative set out above, and I am released regarding what was owed by Diogenes of illustrious memory, and I have no claim to the estate called Mao, situated in the plain of Ophis, mortgaged to me by the same Diogenes of illustrious memory, nor to other property of the same Diogenes of illustrious memory; but I also give thanks to your glorious eminence for the piety it has shown in ordering the same one hundred and thirty gold solidi to be given to the same pious community; and everything and each point is agreeable to me as above, and having been asked I acknowledged. And all having been read and interpreted to me, I, the same Theodorus, manager, asked the most admirable Pamouthius to subscribe for me since I am illiterate, and I released (it). I, the same Pamouthius son of the blessed Philoxenus, subscribed at the request of the same most reverend Theodorus, manager, who is illiterate and after me made three crosses with his own hand, and I released (it). I, Samuel, by the mercy of God deacon of the holy catholic church, son of the blessed Martyrius, witness this security at the request of Joseph and Theodorus, the most reverend head and manager of the same pious community of Abba Hierax, as above. I, Pamouthius son of Papbaous of blessed memory, witness this security at the request of Joseph and Theodorus, the most reverend monks, Joseph being head and Theodorus manager of the pious community of Abba Hierax, as above. I, [...], vir clarissimus, son of Marcianus of illustrious memory, witness this security at the request of Joseph, head, and Theodorus, manager, of the same pious monastery of Abba Hierax, as above. I, Flavius Philoxenus, vir clarissimus, son of Ision of reverend memory, former priest of the pious clergy of this (city) of the Oxyrhynchites, witness this security at the request of Joseph, head, and Theodorus, manager, of the same pious community of Abba Hierax, as above. I, Flavius Phib, the respected comes, son of Matrinus of illustrious memory, witness this security at the request of Joseph, head, and Theodorus, manager, of the same pious community of Abba Hierax, as above. I, Theotimus, by the mercy of God deacon of the holy catholic church of Oxyrhynchus, son of Alexander of reverend memory, former priest, witness this present security at the request of Joseph, head, and Theodorus, manager, of the same pious community of Abba Hierax, as above.

English translation:
Recto. In the reign of our most divine and most pious master Flavius Iustinianus, eternal Augustus and Imperator, year 18, in the third year after the consulship of Flavius Basilius, vir clarissimus, Phamenoth 21, indiction 8, year 221 (and 190), in the city of Oxyrhynchus.
This agreement of acknowledgements and stipulations, without fraud, fear, force, compulsion or deceit, and free of all circumvention, is made by the pious community (koinobion) of Abba Hierax of holy memory, through Joseph, priest and head of the same pious place, and Theodorus who manages it, with the consent of all the most reverend monks in it, to Flavius Apion, the most magnificent former ordinary consul, son of Strategius of all-praised memory, through Menas, servant of his magnificence, who puts the question and acquires for his most magnificent master every action and claim that belongs or may belong under the present agreement; and it acknowledges what is written below.
Diogenes of illustrious memory, then living in the imperial city (Constantinople) and being in need of eighty solidi, asked Theophilus of reverend memory, who also happened then to be in the same imperial city, to lend them to him at half-hundredth interest, and to receive from him, as security for the same eighty solidi, a waterwheel-estate (mechane) of sixteen and a half arouras situated in the village of Ophis, and to take the annual interest from the produce and revenues of the same estate and to hold it until full repayment of the same eighty solidi. So, the same eighty solidi having been lent by Theophilus of reverend memory to Diogenes of illustrious memory, a public (agoraion) document was drawn up by him in the same imperial city, in which he mortgaged to the pious community of Abba Hierax of holy memory, through Theophilus of reverend memory, the said estate of sixteen and a half arouras, on condition that the pious community take from its produce and revenues the interest on the eighty solidi each year and hold this estate as security for both the principal and the interest to accumulate, until full repayment.
Again, the same Diogenes of illustrious memory, in need of another fifty solidi, asked the same Theophilus of reverend memory, who was then also living in the same imperial city, to lend him these too; and Theophilus of reverend memory, persuaded, provided the fifty solidi to Diogenes of illustrious memory, and for these fifty solidi another contract was made, in which the same Diogenes of illustrious memory gave a special and general mortgage on all his property.
These things having so proceeded, it happened that Diogenes of illustrious memory died before repaying the sums contained in these documents, and that Strategius of all-glorious memory, to whom Diogenes was indebted under various loan contracts carrying general and special mortgages, sought an heir of Diogenes of illustrious memory in order to recover lawfully from him what Diogenes of illustrious memory owed him. No heir of Diogenes of illustrious memory being found, and Apphouas of illustrious memory, his brother, and Klematia of noble memory, his sister, having then expressly renounced his inheritance, Strategius of glorious memory was compelled, for lack of an heir, to ask to take ownership, by right of the mortgages contained in his loan contracts, of all the property of Diogenes of illustrious memory; and having lawfully received possession of all the property, he came into possession also of the said estate, which belonged to the same property and was comprised in the mortgages of Diogenes of illustrious memory held by Strategius of all-glorious memory.
Hence Theophilus of reverend memory, having then gone to the imperial city, addressed entreaties to Strategius of all-glorious memory about the said estate, explaining that the pious community through him had given eighty solidi under a first loan contract to Diogenes of illustrious memory on the mortgage of the same estate, and another fifty solidi by another public document on a general mortgage of all his property, and he asked that on this account the said estate be ceded to his pious community. In reply Strategius of all-glorious memory produced his own loan contracts and showed that the general mortgage on all the property of Diogenes of illustrious memory contained in them was earlier than the public documents shown to him by that man, affirming that under the laws he had become owner of all the property of Diogenes of illustrious memory, justly, on account of what was owed to him.
Learning this, Theophilus of reverend memory, reckoning that he had no legal claim regarding the same estate but had altogether lost this mortgage because the mortgages contained in the loan contracts of Strategius of all-glorious memory were earlier, begged the same Strategius of all-glorious memory not to make full use of the law and of the rights belonging to him, but to look to piety and to the need of the brothers in the said pious community, who required the same one hundred and thirty solidi for providing their necessary sustenance, and to give the one hundred and thirty solidi to the same pious community as an act of piety. Strategius of all-glorious memory, moved [...], wrote to those attached to his magnificence in this city to give to the pious community managed by Theophilus of reverend memory one hundred and thirty solidi; they, having received these letters, then gave only seventy-two solidi to the said Theophilus of reverend memory, that is to the same pious community, and they then deposited them with Serenus of blessed memory, former zygostates of this (city) of the Oxyrhynchites, on condition that he lend them out and provide what accrued from them each year to the pious community, until an estate for sale should be found and the same pious community buy it, and the same Serenus give the pound of gold towards part of the price of the estate found and to be sold to the same pious community.
These things having so happened, it came about that Serenus of blessed memory, former zygostates of this illustrious city of the Oxyrhynchites, died, and that those of the pious community of Abba Hierax of holy memory then received from the heirs of Serenus the same pound of gold, and recently went up to the imperial city and entreated Apion, the most magnificent former consul, and his all-praised mother, who is also his guardian, to allow to be given what Strategius of all-glorious memory, while still alive, had out of piety ordered by his own letters those attached to him to provide, that is the other fifty-eight solidi less two hundred and thirty-two carats, on the private standard of this city of the Oxyrhynchites.
Now Apion, the most magnificent former ordinary consul, and Leontia, his all-praised mother, being by nature inclined to piety and disposed to grant the requests of those in need, especially of most reverend men, and because Strategius of all-glorious memory, while still alive, had written that one hundred and thirty solidi be given to the pious community but only seventy-two had been given up to now, have by their own letters allowed those attached to their magnificence in this city to provide another fifty-eight solidi to those of the pious community. The other fifty-eight solidi having therefore been given to the same pious community through Joseph the most reverend, those of the pious community, through the same most reverend priest and head and Theodorus the manager, have come to the present agreement, by which they acknowledge that from the beginning Strategius of all-glorious memory, not making use of the laws and all his rights and his earlier mortgages, and being under no obligation to provide them anything, but out of piety, then wrote that the one hundred and thirty solidi be given to them in the country, of which they then received only seventy-two, and that recently Apion the all-praised consul and his most glorious mother, following the pious purpose of the deceased, allowed another fifty-eight to be given to them.
The head of the same pious community and Theodorus, who manages the pious community, and through them the other most reverend monks of the same pious community further acknowledge that, first, while Strategius of all-glorious memory was alive, they received by his letters from those then attached to his glorious house one pound of gold, which, as narrated above, they acknowledge having received from the heirs of the blessed Serenus the zygostates, and that now likewise they have received into their hands another fifty-eight gold solidi less two hundred and thirty-two carats, which Apion the all-praised consul and his most glorious mother recently wrote to be given to them; and that they have no claim concerning the same estate, because, as has been said, from the beginning they had no lawful claim to vindicate it on account of the earlier mortgages of Strategius of all-glorious memory; and that they give thanks and pray for Strategius of all-praised memory for the one hundred and thirty solidi which out of piety he, while still alive, allowed to be given to them, and likewise beseech the divinity to grant long life to Apion, the all-praised former consul, and to his most glorious mother Leontia, in return for which they too, under no obligation, recently allowed another fifty-eight solidi to be given to complete what was then written by Strategius of all-glorious memory, while still alive, to be given to them.
And as security for what they have agreed, calling God as witness, they acknowledged that they will abide by these terms, keep them, and hold them valid for ever, and not oppose them or any part or article of them, neither now nor hereafter, neither in a local or foreign court nor out of court, nor by a petition submitted to our most victorious master, nor accuse or blame them before friends, or any part of them, either by law or in the holy churches, nor claim to have suffered any circumvention or fraud, because by careful reasoning and from the exact laws they have learned that they have no lawful action or proceeding on the mortgage of the said estate, because, as said, the mortgages in the loan contracts of Strategius of all-praised memory were found to be earlier, but that the same fifty-eight solidi were given to them, that is to their pious community, as an act of piety. And they further acknowledge that all evil fraud is and will be absent from this agreement, and that it is valid against them and those who after them manage and head the same pious community for all time to come; and having been asked on all points, they acknowledged in person, and they mortgaged as security for the present agreement all present and future property of the pious community, specially and generally, by way of pledge and by right of mortgage, in full form as for mortgages, nothing being or able to be excepted from this mortgage. And all having been read and interpreted to them and having pleased them, they subscribed through Pamouthius, asked by them since they are illiterate, the head and the manager making [...] marks (?). For the trust and confirmation of what we have agreed, we have also handed over to your eminence these loan contracts which Diogenes of illustrious memory issued to our pious community, even though we have no help at all from them. The agreement is valid. It was written in a single copy, as above.

The pious community called of Abba Hierax, situated in the western desert of this city of the Oxyrhynchites, through me Joseph, monk and priest, head of the same pious community: I have received the one hundred and thirty gold solidi on the Oxyrhynchite standard according to the narrative set out above, and I am released regarding what was owed by Diogenes of illustrious memory, and I have no claim to the waterwheel-estate called Tmao, situated in the plain of Ophis, mortgaged to me by the same Diogenes of illustrious memory, nor to other property of the same Diogenes of illustrious memory; but I also give thanks to your magnificence for the piety it has shown in ordering the same one hundred and thirty gold solidi to be given to the same pious monastery; and everything and each point is agreeable to me as above, and having been asked I acknowledged. And all having been read and interpreted to me, I, the same Joseph, the least, asked the most admirable Pamouthius to subscribe for me since I am illiterate, and I released (the document). I, Pamouthius son of Philoxenus of blessed memory, subscribed at the request of the same most reverend Joseph, who is illiterate and before me made three crosses with his own hand, and I released (it).

English translation:
In the reign of our most divine and most pious master Flavius Iustinianus, eternal Augustus and Imperator, year 24, in the 8th year after the consulship of Flavius Basilius, the most illustrious, Phaophi 22, indiction 14, in the city of the Oxyrhynchites. To Flavius Apion, the all-renowned and most magnificent ex-consul ordinarius, landowner also here in the illustrious city of the Oxyrhynchites, through Menas, servant, who makes the stipulation and acquires for his own master, the same all-renowned man, the right of action and claim, the community of the protokometai of the village of Takona of the Oxyrhynchite nome, which is under the pagarchy of the house of your Glory, through us, Aurelii Phoebammon, the headman, son of Pekysius, and Anup son of Aritsi, and Menas his brother, and Koulaetb son of Iohannes, and Anup son of Priscus, and Heraclides son of Palmas, and Phib son of Iulius, and the other komarchs of this village, greetings. We acknowledge that we have received from your Glory as a loan, and have had measured out to us from the produce of the present fourteenth indiction, for the sowing of our arouras for the crops of the, God willing, fifteenth indiction, two hundred artabas of dirty wheat, without sifting, by the kankellon measure, which were also given to us through the heirs of the late Menas son of Asklas, shipmaster of your same glorious house, total 200 artabas of wheat by the kankellon; which wheat we will of necessity repay to your Glory, new and sieved, by the kankellon measure by which we received it, together with our rent, in the month Payni of the current year 227/196 of the same present fourteenth indiction, from the new crops of the, God willing, fifteenth indiction, without delay, at the risk of our property, which is pledged for this. The deed, written in a single copy, is valid, and having been asked we acknowledged. We, the community of the protokometai of the village of Takona of the Oxyrhynchite nome, through the names written above in it, (have made) this deed to your Glory for the two hundred artabas of dirty wheat, without sifting, by the kankellon, total 200 artabas of dirty wheat, and we will repay at the stated term, and all that is written is agreeable to us as aforesaid, and having been asked we acknowledged and [...]. I, Aurelius Heraclides, secretary of the village of Takona, having been asked, wrote for them, as they are illiterate. Executed through me, Philoxenus. Phaophi 23, indiction 14 [...]. (Verso:) Deed made by the protokometai of the village of Takona on account of the sowing for the crops of the 15th indiction, 200 artabas of wheat by the kankellon.

'I, Pebe, son of John, the σύμμαχος, of Shmoun, do write to Leontius, son of Hatre, likewise of Shmoun, saying: I owe thee, clear and, a tremision of 7½ carats, by Alexandrian standard, that is, 7½ trem. of Alexandrian weight. English translation:
To King Ptolemy, greetings, Theonides of Ammonias. I am wronged by Seuthes, cavalryman holding 100 arouras, who lives in the same village. For, owing me by hand 15 artabas of barley, which he agreed to repay to me from the produce of year 26, although the time has passed and he has often been asked by me, he does not repay me. I therefore ask you, O King, if it seems good to you, to order Diophanes the strategos to write to Agathocles the epistates to send Seuthes to him and, if these things are true, to compel him to repay me; but if he disputes anything, let him swear to me that he does not owe and be released, so that I may not be wronged but, having taken refuge with you, O King, the benefactor of all, may obtain justice. Farewell. (Docket) To Agathocles. Having examined (the matter), see to it that he obtains justice. Year 1, Gorpiaios 30, Tybi 13. (Verso) Year 1, Gorpiaios 30, Tybi [13]. Theonides against Seuthes, about 15 artabas of barley.

English translation:
To Crateros, one of the first friends and strategos, from Isidorus, epistates of the village Tachenephre in the Memphite nome. In year 6, Phaophi 7, Hermias son of Dagouzis, of the same (village), submitted to me a memorandum against Chenephnibis son of Herieus and his wife Taarmotis daughter of Pasis, because, though they owe him 6 artabas of wheat under a six-witness contract, they do not repay these and the half (penalty) on them, and he asked that they be summoned and the wheat be repaid to him with the half. On the 8th of the same month I summoned Chenephnibis and, since he admitted it, I handed him over to [Peritas the chief of police], and he to Ptolemaeus the komarch, Hermias and another elder of the village being with him, until he should do what is just. But now, since Taarmotis (deleted: his wife) has turned against me and has lodged a written complaint against me as having joined in assaulting her, which did not happen, I ask you to order that a written guarantee be given to me, so that [...] I may defend myself concerning my affairs and not be harassed by anyone, and to write also to Ammonius the hypostrategos, under whom I am, to bring before you Peritas and Ptolemaeus and Hermias and the elder of the village, so that testimony may be given to you concerning my affairs. If this is done, I shall have obtained your help. Year 6, Hathyr 30. Farewell.

Year 4, Mecheir 27, at Pathyris, before Heliodorus the agoranomos. They made this contract willingly. English translation:
Year 4, Mecheir 27, at Pathyris, before Heliodorus the agoranomos. They made this contract willingly. Totoes son of Pelaias acknowledges that he owes Panobchounis son of Totoes 8 talents of copper and 13 1/2 artabas of wheat, without interest. Let Totoes repay this debt to Panobchounis in the month Mesore of year 5. To my lord and esteemed brother Iohannes son of Acindynus, honourable notary, from the city of the Apollonopolitans, from Flavius Psensoerius son of Anubion, soldier, from the same city. I acknowledge that I owe and am indebted to your brotherliness, without dispute, for the recovery of my earlier bond, one gold solidus less two carats by your weight, total 1 gold solidus less 2 carats, and this I am ready, with God, to provide to your brotherliness whenever you wish, with the lawful centesimal interest until the repayment and completion of the same one solidus; and for the security of your brotherliness I have made this security for you, and it is in my own hand, written by me. English translation:
In the consulship of Flavius Anthemius, vir gloriosissimus, Phaophi 13 of the ninth indiction. Aurelius Besarion son of Musaeus, grandson of Salacha, mother Tariste, from the village of Aphrodito of the Antaeopolite nome, writing slowly, to Aurelia Mariam daughter of Eulogius, most noble, the late protokometes, from the same village, greeting. Since you owe by a public mortgage five gold solidi by weight in the name of my blessed mother Tariste, and I have now received from you the same five solidi, and you asked to receive from me the mortgage (deed), I could not find it to give back to you because it has been lost among my papers; for this reason I have come to this written release or annulment, by which I acknowledge that I have no claim against you henceforth concerning the same aforesaid five solidi, neither by myself nor through my heirs, neither against you nor against your heirs. If it should happen that any person whatsoever sues you on the same ground of the mortgage, I am ready to keep you unmolested, and I will keep you free from loss concerning the same mortgage, at the risk of myself and all my property for this. And for your security I have made this release or annulment, valid and binding wherever produced; and having been asked I acknowledged. I, Aurelius Besarion son of Musaeus, the aforesaid, have made the annulment as aforesaid. I, Aurelius Isakios son of Iosephius, witness the annulment, having heard it from the maker. I, Iakob son of Biktor, deacon, witness the annulment, having heard it from the maker. Written by me, Victor son of Apollos.

English translation:
(All crossed out.) [...] I have signed. Year 19 of Trajan Optimus Caesar the lord, Epeiph 3. To Thracidas and Heraclides alias Demetrius, former gymnasiarchs, keepers of the property records of the Arsinoite nome, from Isarous daughter of Apollonius son of Eudaemon, mother Acousous alias Tamysthes daughter of Asclepiades, registered in the quarter of the Bithynians, Other Places, with her guardian, her full brother Eudaemon. The slave Sarapias, whom I registered through you on the present day, I wish voluntarily and of my own choice [to mortgage to ...]dora daughter of Souchion alias Eumelus against the 456 drachmas of silver capital which I owe her under a security, and the interest, and that no transaction be recorded for me nor any disposal be made at all until I produce a receipt for the repayment of everything. I, Isarous daughter of Apollonius, with my guardian, my brother Eudaemon son of Apollonius, have submitted the voluntary memorandum of the mortgage of the slave Sarapias against the 456 drachmas of silver capital and interest, as aforesaid. I, Eudaemon, wrote most of it. Year 19 of Imperator Caesar Nerva Traianus Optimus Augustus Germanicus Dacicus Parthicus, Payni 9. I, Isarous daughter of Apollonius, have submitted the mortgage as aforesaid. (Verso) ...

English translation:
Chrysermus, priest and archidikastes, to the strategos of the Oxyrhynchite nome, greetings. Let a copy of the memorandum submitted be served, as below. Farewell. Year ten of Imperator Caesar Traianus Hadrianus Augustus, ... To Chrysermus, priest of Alexander the founder of the city and of the age-classes, archidikastes and in charge of the chrematistai and the other courts, from Eudaemon the younger, son of Pet.uris alias Apollonius, of those from the city of Oxyrhynchus. As there are owed to me by Apollonius son of Sarapion son of Apollonius, mother Didyme, from the same city of Oxyrhynchus, under a written security made in the third year of Hadrian the lord in the month Neos Sebastos, three hundred [...] eight drachmas of silver capital, which he agreed to repay on the thirtieth of Tybi of the same year or to pay interest of one drachma (per mina per month) for the overdue time, and as repayment has not been made, I ask you to order a letter to the strategos of the Oxyrhynchite nome to serve on him a copy of this, so that he may repay me the aforesaid capital and the interest for the overdue time, or know that I will proceed to execution as is proper on his property. I have dispatched [...] [...] ...

English translation:
Iohannes son of Abraamius, from the village of Aphrodito, to the brothers Enoch son of Hermaus and Phoebammon son of Triadelphus and Iohannes son of Hermias and another Iohannes son of Promaus and Psan[...], protokometai of the same village, greeting. I have received and been paid in full [by you for the] bond of the fifty-one full-weight solidi by weight, and I make no [claim against you concerning the said] gold nor concerning [any other matter, written or unwritten], except for fifty-four gold carats only by weight, total 54 carats, and it shall not be permitted to me at any season or time to [...] or to dispute [about] any matter, written or unwritten, nor indeed about any other [...] of the intervening time up to now, except the fifty-four carats; and for your security I have made you this receipt (entagion) with my signature, as aforesaid. Choiak 24 of the second indiction. I, Iohannes, the aforesaid: the receipt is satisfactory to me as aforesaid. And after the payment of the said 54 carats, I am to give you back your bond of the fifty-one solidi. I, Pilatus son of Apollos, lawyer, witness the receipt, having heard it from Iohannes, who also made it.

English translation:
[...] of the city of the Antinoites, to Flavius [Constantinus], son of Callinicus son of Alexander of excellent memory, [singularis] of the ducal office, from the same [...] city, now living here in the same city of the Antinoites, greeting. I acknowledge what is set out below. Formerly your father of blessed memory, Callinicus by name, owed [me] by a written bond thirty-three full-weight solidi, having then pledged for the security and repayment of them and of their interest, as the same bond contains, visible pledges of whatever weight they are, namely a silver mesatin cup (?) and two gold pentarrostula (?). And the time for their redemption having passed, and your father, the original party, having died before their redemption and the repayment of the same debt, I accordingly made a claim against you, the aforesaid Constantinus, concerning the said debt and its interest, being obliged, as is proper, to be paid these and to give back to you the pledges pledged to me by your father while he lived; and your clarity being in no way able to redeem them, you made requests to me to have, hold and appropriate to myself the said pledges in place of the aforementioned debt and its interest, with full ownership, from now for all subsequent and coming time, and to have power over them and to be able to use the aforesaid pledges in every way as owner, as I wish, without hindrance, impediment or complaint, of necessity. And after the written renunciation of these made to me by you today, you asked me for the bond, that is your father's security made to me for these, but I did not find it at once to give it back to you; therefore I have come to this settlement agreement, which has the force of an annulment, by which I acknowledge that I am ready to give back to you the said security of your father whenever I search and track down all my documents and find it; or, if I find it has been lost among my papers, I further acknowledge that in no way or time shall I have any claim against you henceforth, nor will have concerning the same bond, neither I nor my heirs nor successors nor holders, against you or your heirs, because I have not found the same bond among my papers and have already received the same pledges by your written renunciation and appropriated them to myself for the same debt and its interest, which fully pays me the amount of the debt, both principal and interest. And if it is ever found at any season or time with me or my heirs or any person whatsoever, it shall be void and invalid wherever produced before any authority and power, so that you, the said Constantinus, and your heirs shall in no way be sued or harmed or claimed against on the ground of the same bond and its interest at any season or time, because I have been released and paid in full the principal and interest contained in it and have settled with you on account of the force it contains, all my present wealth being bound and pledged to you for this, and to those who will succeed to your succession at any time, and my property in general and in particular, by way of pledge and right of mortgage, in every kind and sort, to drive off and turn away from you at all times any person who proceeds against you on this account. And for your security I have made this settlement agreement, valid and binding wherever produced, signed by me and by customary witnesses, by whom having been asked I acknowledged.

Aurelius Iohannes, farmer, son of Menas, from [the village of ...] of the Heracleopolite nome, to Aurelius Gerontius son of Anteinus, from the same village, [...] [...] that I owe, clearly and undisputedly, [...] fifty gold solidi of pure gold (obryza) [...] and for the security [...] [...] from the [...] of Aurelius Ammonius [... in the place] called Tarot, six arouras, with their share of the cistern and water-supply there, and of the water-wheel and its emplacement and the machine's equipment and tower and every right belonging to them altogether; neighbours: to the south a public road, to the north the canal there, to the east land of [...]; so that you, the said Gerontius, and your heirs and all successors have these immovable properties with all their rights according to the description given above, and the power over the plots to sow, harvest and draw revenue from them yearly, if you wish, the rent of the plots being reckoned and set off against the interest (philanthropon) of the same debt; and neither I nor my heirs may take these immovable properties, or part of them or any right, away from you or your heirs until the settlement of the same debt and the full payment of the same debt [...] [...] debt, as you received from me; and having been asked I acknowledged and released (the document).

To Flavius Apollonius, strategos of the Arsinoite nome, Heraclides division, [from Lucius I]gnatius Casianus. Of the official document which I obtained from the review a copy is subjoined, [and I ask that an equal copy] be served through one of your assistants on Marcus [Valerius] Turbo, made known through it, in person, so that he may know. Year 16 of Aurelius Antoninus Caesar the lord [...]. The copy of the document is: Diodorus, priest and archidikastes, to the strategos of the Arsinoite nome, [Heraclides division], greetings. Let a copy of the memorandum submitted be served, as below. [Year 16 of Aure]lius Antoninus Caesar the lord, Mesore 7. [...] To [...]onius, former strategos of the city, priest, archidikastes and in charge of the chrematistai and [the other] courts, from Lucius Ignatius Casianus. In the current year, in Payni, Marcus [Valerius Turb]o served on me, through the strategos of the Heraclides division of the Arsinoite nome, a copy of a diastolikon [concerning ...] the sums owed to Gaius Iulius Antoninus, on whose death [...] became heir, by Iaius Lucius Ignatius, soldier of the second cohort of Thebans, and [his children] Lucius Ignatius Casianus and Ignatia Aphrodous, under a synchoresis [...] at drachma-interest, on mortgage near the village of Philadelphia, of Lucius Ignatius Casianus three arouras of grain land and of Ignatia Aphrodous two arouras. Therefore, [making] the necessary objection, I declare that I am within the age that is protected by law, [and further] that no money was paid out to me [...] to be protected by the prefects and judges of the time, and what is paid out in good faith [...] [...] that nothing of the kind is possible, I will prove necessarily through your authority [...] and I ask you to order a letter to the strategos of the Heraclides division of the Arsinoite nome to serve a copy [of this] on Valerius Turbo, so that he may know that the diastolikon served by him is invalid and void, together with whatever he may dare to serve [...]. Year 16 of Aurelius Antoninus Caesar the lord, Mesore. I have signed. I, Areius, assistant, [have served it] in person. Year 17 of Aurelius Antoninus Caesar the lord, Phamenoth [...].

English translation:
To my lord brother Diodorus, Lucius and Sarapion, many greetings. Before all else we pray that you are in good health with your whole household. These days we expect you to come to us. Please, then, go to Aretion the baker and receive from him the four talents which he took from us while he was in Alexandria; but see that you do not neglect it. If then you get the four talents from him, when you come to us buy us grain for our use, and get the garum (?) and send it to us. See, I have written to Aretion that he should give you the four talents. Since you said that you want a pastas (?), I will send it to you when it is brought in. I received the small jar (?) of vinegar from Ammonas and sent you through him a small basket of sweetmeats and a razor-shell (?). We greet our sister and daughter Helenous and her daughter. Greet Aphynchis and Techosis and Ptolemus from us. If you learn that Aretion is going to slander you about the bronze vessels, write to me and I will send him an additional (?) [...]. I pray for your health for many years. (Verso) Deliver to Diodorus, retailer, from Lucius his friend.

English translation:
Ammonius and Herais and Euporus to Priscus their lord father and Thaesis their lady mother and Herminus the most estimable, many greetings. On the 17th of Epeiph, that is yesterday, we received letters through Chaeremon from Artapatou (?), in which you say that Cephalon, in his ingratitude, came forward saying that the document was not his, and even approached the epistrategus. A most ridiculous and astonishing affair: debtors terrify their creditors! If then these things have been done as you say, let him be vigorously served with notice according to the law. And if the official neglects it, bring him before the epistrategus and let him make the registration in the notification, as the laws command. And send to me at once, so that I too may approach the superior official; for I am permitted to petition about any matter I wish. His document is in the office, in registration, with my subscription that it is his autograph, in accordance with the instruction. I will bring the other matter alone before the superior official here; what is being decided is this, that he should be served with notice and registered. If he has chosen to be ungrateful, I have many proofs for refutation, first the document, second some other things. And do not [...] approach [...], but as having the [...] from me. And [...] nothing [...] is left to the ungrateful man except registration. And for you [...] nothing else can happen unless he is served with notice and you register, and I will have him (?) summoned. For I learned that you are also summoning [...] to the estate (?) [...]. Greet her mother [...] by name. We pray to all the gods for your health. (Verso) To Priscus, neocorus, and Herminus, many-times victor, from Ammonius, diastoleus (?).

I acknowledge, willingly and persuaded, that I have leased from you for a period of four years, reckoned from the crops of the sixth indiction, with God, both that year and the following time, the whole estate belonging to you, with its holding of however many arouras it has, called Prmres(?), with two cisterns, a dwelling, a tower, a farmstead, a chaff-store, a plot, an orchard, vegetable land and plants and date palms, olive groves, sycamores, citrons, acacias and all the trees belonging to it, fruit-bearing and barren, and the surrounding arouras and all rights inside and outside, within its old boundaries all round, situated in the western plain of the same village of Aphrodite, in the allotment of Anoubis, on condition that I hold it under me for cultivation and planting(?) on half-shares, and do all the farming and vine-dressing work with my own animals, expenses and labourers, and water it unceasingly and without neglect, and dig, prune, prop up and guard, and that what remains from it, with God, of must and of the fruit of the date palms and of the orchard shall be divided between us in half shares, I taking one share for my labours and you taking one share for your landowner's share; and when I cut reeds and fine split canes for the need of propping, we shall pay half the cost of the wooden machine from the common stock; and I am ready to give you, as a fixed rent for the surrounding arouras each year, in a full and not unflooded year (which may it not be), ten artabas of clean rent-quality wheat by my measure and one solidus of gold less one carat on the standard of the same village of Aphrodite, total 10 artabas of wheat and 1 gold solidus less 1 carat, and to pay these to you each year, the wheat at the threshing floor, the one solidus at the time of the public (taxes), as agreed. I have from you and owe for the advance for the oxen, that is eight solidi of gold, each less one carat, to account for these to you at the time of completion of the term of the present written lease, as agreed, without dispute. The lease shall be valid and secure, and to everything, being asked, I acknowledged. It is clear that I shall give you, for the completion of the rent for the surrounding arouras, the following: if we sow beans, for the years to account to you five artabas of beans; if we do not sow beans, to account to you five artabas of barley, as agreed; and on condition that I account to you for an iron tool of ten and a half litrai at the time I leave the same estate, for what I took beforehand from you; and again I acknowledged; and that I may have one date palm each year for the account of the farmer, for the care of all the date palms. I, Menas son of Psates, agree to this lease as stated above. Aurelius Psates son of Ananias, I witness this lease as stated above. Aurelius Georgius son of Onnophrius, I witness this lease as stated above. Written through me, Collouthus, with God, tabellio.

To the all-holy, beloved and sweetest Paieous, presbyter, and Dioscorus and Hierax and [...] and Apa Sourous and all the brothers and all those with you, by name, Moyses [and Herieous], your inferiors in the Lord, greeting. First of all making [our] obeisance [to you], beloved patrons, we wish [to tell you] about this beloved [Pamonthius] that he is in great distress [and has suffered most shamefully] at the hands of certain [merciless] and godless men, so that you too [may make haste] for him [...] and of your exceeding love to dwell in heaven. So, of necessity, make every haste for him without hesitation, because the lenders have seized his children into slavery. If you hold me as a brother, help this man, beloved, because he pressed us very hard in this way about this need, and we will not hesitate. Whatever we found we handed over to him, and indeed we did beyond our means. Whatever you can, collect money, pay it out, and write to me about what you have given, so that we may get the security and may also be trusted, since he owes very much money. See that you do not neglect it, beloved, since the brother has fallen into such distress. I pray for your health [...]. (Left margin) Show then your innate love and compassion and the affection of your fatherliness. (Verso) I write to you, then, brother Paieous [...] this distress, so that [...] by every means, and establish [...] for him among the brothers, so that [...] they may give; for I know that much [...]; and send to the brothers [...].
